text:
当外界还在聚焦英伟达董事会与黄仁勋的权力博弈时，一份重新被拿出来审视的 SEC 监管文件，把这场风暴推向了更微妙的境地。

英伟达董事会成员、同时也是公司第二大个人股东（仅次于黄仁勋）的 Mark Stevens，在黄仁勋辞职风波全面爆发前的两个月，高位套现了近 $9.5 亿。

监管文件显示，在 8 月 31 日至 9 月 18 日期间，Stevens 通过家族信托分批减持了约 420 万股英伟达股票，套现总额达 $9.47 亿。当时英伟达股价正处在历史高位区间。

真正引发华尔街高度审视的，是这笔交易的操作方式。

在美股市场，科技巨头的高管与董事为了规避内幕交易质疑，通常会提前数月甚至半年设定 10b5-1 预先交易计划（例如英伟达 CFO Colette Kress 和总法律顾问 Tim Teter 减持时均有明确报备）。但在 Stevens 提交给 SEC 的 Form 4 文件中，并未勾选任何 10b5-1 预设交易计划，属于自主择机出售。

而随后发生的时间线对比，在当下显得格外敏感：9 月 18 日 Stevens 刚完成这笔近 $10 亿的现金套现；几周之后，英伟达董事会便就黄仁勋的私人关系与合规问题启动了内部调查；11 月 12 日，黄仁勋突然宣布辞任 CEO 与董事，英伟达股价随即大幅下挫。

当然，从严格的法律层面看，董事出售个人持仓属于合法权利，未设立 10b5-1 计划本身并不构成违规证据，Stevens 目前也依然持有约 2750 万股英伟达股票。

但在资本市场的实际语境中，这种处于风暴爆发前夕的大额套现，很难不引发投资者的联想。

尤其在各路机构股东与科技圈正在联手质疑董事会决策、甚至试图推动罢免董事的关口：一边是核心董事在重磅调查公开前大额变现离场，另一边是灵魂创始人出局引发的巨大市值震荡。

董事会原本以“合规与公司治理”为由建立的立场，在这些交易记录面前，恐怕会面临股东更严厉的问责。

No one knows for sure. Correlation does not prove causation. Here are some potential reasons.

Money shifting to the Anthropic IPO: https://t.co/4WXOMfH9Th

Hot U.S. inflation has raised expectations of another Fed rate hike. Higher yields and a stronger dollar can weigh on "riskier assets" such as crypto.

Political uncertainty: Midterm results have raised concerns about potentially stricter U.S. crypto policy.

No, Binance did not sell crypto.

I bought crypto in the past few days, as I got some stablecoins recently. (maybe this is the cause 🤣)

author: barnabemonnot
quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
推特上许多讨论黄仁勋的，都集中在商业判断、Dennys创业纪念碑的去留、情愿和私生活八卦上

但我发现最打动人的，还是在老黄落难之际，许多之前受过他滴水之恩的人出来主动post testimonial

一件件具体而分布散落的事件指向一个真相 —— 老黄确实是乐善好施乐于助人之人

而且我也相信，为人抱薪者，不可使其冻毙于风雪

图1 - 11 年前，一个印度普通大学的学生 @recurseparadox 给黄仁勋发cold email，问能不能要几块 GPU。15 分钟后，收到了回信。

图2 - Serve Robotics 的创始人 Ali Kashani @ahkashani ，记得的是一个早上 6 点的电话。2023 年圣诞节前，投资人临时撤资，公司连工资都快发不出来。他已经在和破产律师谈了，于是给黄仁勋写了封邮件。

早上 6 点，黄仁勋打来电话。当天晚上，他已经在和英伟达团队吃饭，商量怎么帮公司渡过难关。四个月后，他们敲响了纳斯达克的钟。

图3 - 同样是回邮件，Simon Mo @simon_mo_ 讲过另一件事：团队的算力被收回，vLLM 在 Blackwell 上的开发受阻。他写信给黄仁勋，同一分钟就收到回复，问题连夜解决。

图4 - 英伟达员工 John Zedlewski @zstats 的长帖，讲了两件不同领域但同样伟大的事。

一件是他重病住院，处在最低谷时告诉了黄仁勋。黄仁勋立刻联系斯坦福的人，帮他协调进入临床试验。

另一件发生在工作中。自动驾驶部门开会，A 团队抱怨 B 团队的框架太慢。黄仁勋让 B 团队把整个数据流画到白板上，标出每一次内存拷贝。多余的拷贝就这样露了出来。

第二件我特别有感触，不同于大部分公司里面，遇到类似的问题，往往因为领导层自己也不懂技术，所以只能模糊的给一个，“我们研究一下，下周答复你”的模糊回答（然后不了了之）。

实事求是，原地分析，当场解决问题。太有魅力了

图5 - Vartika Singh @vartuattheghat 的妹妹患脑癌，在加州时病情恶化。全家陷入了难以想象的困境：令人心碎的医疗抉择、高得令人难以承受的住院费用，以及可能在远离家乡的地方失去她。   

尽管肩上担子沉重，黄仁勋还是抽出时间关心他们。帮助她的家人渡过了看似无解的难关。黄仁勋还当面鼓励她：“我为你感到骄傲。珍惜你们在一起的时光。”

这，我的朋友，才是真正的领导力 leadership。

图6 - 在英伟达工作 11 年的 Gabriele Leone @ambertanuki ，记住了疫情期间的一个决定：办公室空了，厨房和清洁人员几乎没活可做，黄仁勋仍决定把他们全部留下。

当所有500强企业都在裁员，跟风裁员是最容易的选项的时候。黄仁勋考虑的不是公司的股票业绩和财务报表。他看到的是公司里最容易被忽略的人，也替他们想了一下。

图7 - 大约 30 年前，一个学生志愿者 @Fuzzygoat 在洛杉矶 SIGGRAPH 的酒店电梯里遇到黄仁勋。两人下楼，发现去会场的班车已经走了。

黄仁勋叫了辆出租车，坚持让这个学生一起坐。

text:
How the Media Went From Rumor to Rumor to Sell Jensen Huang’s “Return” to Nvidia  

Today at 2:03 p.m., 
the exact same @FT reporter who first told the world Jensen Huang was having an affair, @AsiaLens, dropped another "exclusive":

"Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive."

Notice the victory lap, right there in the second line:

"tech executive resigned over reports he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate."

The only fact on the record: Huang admitted to an affair.
No name.
No spy.

This time, the reporter buried his own byline, last of three.

Maybe hoping we'd forget what he already admitted on X: he never saw any U.S. intelligence. He just believed that U.S. intelligence believed a Chinese spy story.

Belief built on belief built on belief.

Ten days later, over a spy case the DOJ, the DNI and the CIA still can't even confirm, he somehow found brand-new sources to believe in:

"Huang has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, according to multiple people familiar with the matter."

Say it twice:
According to multiple people familiar with the matter.

Then comes the thriller script:

"One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a 'war room' of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief's return and would try to garner support from the White House."

Read those words twice:
Huang ally. Huang ally.
"War room." "War room."
Garner support from the White House.

Wait a second, I thought this wasn't about Jensen at all. t was Napoleon on Elba island, plotting his Hundred Days.

Watch the clockwork:

2:03 p.m. FT publishes.
2:10 p.m. @TheInsiderPaper reposts.
2:12 p.m. @zerohedge reposts.
2:14 p.m. @business runs its story.
2:15 p.m. @FT's own X account finally tweets it.

Bloomberg had a full article up a minute before the FT tweeted its own scoop.

Guess the Bloomberg Terminal really is worth the money.

Just another coincidence.

The @WSJ was way more patient.

They let the "comeback" story run for seven hours. Watched Nasdaq 100 futures jump 200+ points.

Then, right before Monday's pre-market open, they dropped their "definitive" piece and slammed the door, starring double-standard @SecScottBessent and Yale's @JeffSonnenfeld (Senior Associate Dean, founder of the Chief Executive Leadership Institute).

Turns out the professor gives up his weekends, just like I do, to binge "House of Cards: Silicon Valley Edition."

He even comes pre-loaded with headline-ready lines like "tear up the rulebook."

I think he's a Joy Division fan, just like me.

I'm not falling for the media trap of debating "corporate governance."

Look at the calendar.

Ever since this broke on November 11, Sonnenfeld has been doing non-stop interviews: The Guardian, the WSJ, everywhere.

What a "phenomenal presence" in Wall Street media.

Every appearance: zero room for a defense, one-sided against Huang, cranking up the heat every time.

Just another coincidence.

And right there at the end of that very same FT piece, they quietly slipped in the exit line:

"Even allies were unsure how to rehabilitate Huang's reputation, acknowledged one person involved in efforts to reinstate Huang."

"One person involved in efforts."

Everything is a coincidence.

quoted_text:
Ansem and Pumpfun Brought a Chinese Cat ($mihao) Into CT's Spotlight

4CxjZyMNoF1p6eXHXHv1TWpS2X47CuUmLwtGe18spump 

I believe the core reason behind mihao rally is that Ansem brought what was originally a simple Chinese cat meme into the center of CT's attention, while its PFP concept gives it the potential to spread further. However, I don't think it has yet developed into a mature cultural community or a true Animal Runner. What it has already demonstrated is its ability to generate attention and attract speculative capital.

What matters next is whether the attention brought by Ansem can turn into genuine community recognition.

mihao doesn't have a complicated narrative. It's simply a cat incorporating Chinese elements, with its name being a play on the Chinese phrase "你好". Its Pumpfun description reads: "you met me at a very chinese time in my life," borrowing a famous line from Fight Club and combining Chinese elements, a cat character, and a touch of absurd humor.

Its advantage is precisely its simplicity. The traditional hat, long beard, and cat character give it a recognizable visual identity. People don't need much explanation to recognize it, imitate it, or create their own versions. The recent increase in discussions around Chinese X has also provided some cultural context, but the person who really pushed this meme to a wider audience was Ansem.

However, what's worth noting is that he's no longer the only one participating in its spread.

Ansem hasn't just publicly expressed his bullish view. He also changed his X profile picture to an image associated with mihao and posted things like "mihao pfp up," "ni hao," and "ni hao cat bringing the good vibes back to onchain."

At the same time, tetsuo, who has approximately 255K followers, also changed his profile picture to a related image. It's worth noting that tetsuo frequently receives interactions from Elon.

Taken together, these actions mean more than just a few influential accounts promoting a token. A meme often becomes much more powerful when different users voluntarily start using its imagery, rather than simply reposting the same promotional content. Ansem brought the initial attention, while the participation of accounts like tetsuo gives MIHAO an opportunity to spread into a broader AI community.

According to the holder snapshot at the time, Ansem held approximately 0.8% of the total supply, with a position worth around $79,800 and an average entry at roughly $2.01M market cap. This combination of public promotion and actual ownership is more likely to encourage market imitation than a simple repost. However, influence is still largely concentrated around Ansem, and other major KOLs have not yet participated at a comparable level.

I think the most interesting development within the project is its PFP concept.

mihao already offers approximately 218 variations of cat avatars, allowing users to generate MIHAO PFPs in different styles. The main account also interacts with holders and creates personalized PFPs for community members. Recently, people have started voluntarily changing their X profile pictures to different versions of MIHAO, while Ansem's own profile picture change has further amplified this trend.

For a pure memecoin, users voluntarily putting a project's imagery on their personal profiles can sometimes be more valuable than dozens of promotional posts. It keeps the meme visible across different timelines and gives participants a shared visual identity.

However, I wouldn't call this a mature PFP cult yet. Participation is still relatively limited, and much of the attention is coming from people who are already interested in trading the token. The real test will come when the price moves sideways or corrects: will users still want to keep using MIHAO avatars, create new variations, and participate in the community?

If the PFP culture can exist independently of price appreciation, mihao will have started building a much deeper community identity.

Another development worth watching is the MIHAO Ecosystem section.

The website has already aggregated a number of tokens and DEX pools paired with mihao, with the displayed 24-hour paired trading volume reaching approximately $1.18M at the time.

This suggests that other participants are beginning to capitalize on the attention surrounding mihao by creating derivative assets. The original meme is starting to generate trading activity beyond the token itself.

The potential upside from here depends on three main developments: whether Ansem continues participating and attracts more influential traders; whether MIHAO PFPs spread beyond the trader community to a broader CT audience; and whether paired tokens generate sustained activity, allowing the original meme's influence to extend beyond the price action of a single token.

If the main account continues building the community and organic content creation increases, mihao could evolve from a KOL-driven rally into a more established cat PFP community.

The risks are also concentrated. Its value depends primarily on meme distribution, community participation, and speculative capital. Current catalysts are heavily concentrated around Ansem, and if his attention shifts elsewhere, market momentum could weaken quickly. The PFP community is still in its early stages, and if participants are only changing their avatars because the price is going up, that enthusiasm could disappear during a correction.

There is also a possibility that Ansem himself may eventually change his profile picture again.

My view is that mihao has already proven its ability to generate attention, but it has not yet proven that it can become a genuine Animal Runner.

Its biggest strength isn't some complicated utility. It's the fact that the cat character is easy to recognize, imitate, and use, and that people have already started voluntarily adopting its PFPs. Its biggest weakness is that community recognition still depends heavily on influential KOLs and price performance.

What I'm most interested in watching next isn't how high Ansem can take the token, but how many people will continue using MIHAO avatars when Ansem stops actively promoting it and the price starts moving sideways.

A cat can become popular because of one influential account. But whether people still want to keep it on their profiles after the hype fades is what will determine whether it can evolve from a short-term trading narrative into a genuine cultural meme.

其实这两周还有件算力相关有意思的事，CME的GPU期货又推迟啦

这是第二次延期，原定10/5上市，11/4据 The Information，CME应CFTC要求再等60天，最早也要明年1月了

CFTC一直拿不准结算价该用谁的数。8月就为此公开征求过意见，Silicon Data、Ornn、Compute Desk 几家 GPU 指数商，加上CME、ICE、DRW、Jump，全交了信

放在一起读很好笑🙃每个预言机都希望监管出一份只有自己能考过的卷子：

- Ornn：只认真实成交，不认报价。它的指数恰好只用成交，它的头号数据源Hydra Host也交了信，说的一样
- Silicon Data：主张可执行的报价在可用性和价格经过指数管理人或第三方核实后可收录，而且每家供应商要有权重上限
- DRW（Silicon Data背后的股东，唯一公开替报价辩护的一方）：说报价可以直接通过 API 调用成交，而成交数据相对稀少（反驳 Ornn 的路线)
- Compute Desk（两边都打）：警告不要用来自按需算力交易市场的数据编指数，哪怕是真实成交也不行。Compute Desk 自己做的是大客户整租的长约价

你手上有一百万股英伟达，今天想套现，得走董事会，得按 10b5-1 排队，卖完两个工作日内还要向 SEC 申报

IPO 锁定期 180 天，大股东减持得提前公告。上市公司囤的币，减仓也要发 8-K

比特币没有这些

凌晨三点，什么身份都行，多大金额都行，点一下就卖出去了，也没有人问你为什么卖

所以真缺现金的时候，第一个被卖的就是它

比特币的盘口 365 天不关，几亿美元一次出完，中间也不卡

它跌得最凶，正因为它最好卖。这就是自由的代价

那这六天，谁在缺钱

12 月 9 日美联储议息，92% 押加息

10 年期美债 5.15%，美元指数 103.4，欧央行、日本央行、英国央行同步收紧

11 月 13 日，美国 10 月 PPI 同比 6.5%，2022 年 11 月以来最高，核心 5.0%。降息的故事讲不下去了

11 月 12 日黄仁勋被英伟达董事会罢免，NVDA 两周跌 19%，那天盘中跌 14%，市值一度蒸发 6010 亿美元

全美国的科技基金在同一天重算敞口

Anthropic 上市募 644 亿，6 倍超额认购，近 4000 亿在排队

这 4000 亿只能从别的仓位里腾出来

美国现货 BTC ETF 连着七个交易日净流出 19.1 亿，总资产从 1093 亿掉到 862 亿

14 家美国上市公司今年卖了 10.8 万枚

这五件事都要美元，都要在几天内凑齐

比特币是这些资产里变现最快的一项，卖压就先落到它身上

这种时候，市场的一个版本：

是币安想填那 63 亿的窟窿，故意把价格砸下去，好低位收货

到底是不是这个剧情，数据能说话

卖压从哪来，数据里看得出痕迹

先说 ETF

美国现货 BTC ETF 从 11 月 5 日到 13 日，连续七个交易日净流出，合计 19.1 亿美元

贝莱德的 IBIT 一家走了 9.08 亿，快占一半

BTC 类基金流出 10.65 亿，以太坊 3.99 亿，SOL 3200 万，ZEC 3080 万，HYPE 440 万

总资产从 1093 亿掉到 862 亿，两周缩了 21%

ETF 只能卖现货

它开不了空，也加不了杠杆

投资人赎一笔，基金就得在盘面上卖一笔，卖完还要在收盘后对外公布

再说矿企，这块更狠

按 Lookonchain 的口径，截至 11 月 10 日，14 家美国上市公司今年一共卖了 108247 枚 BTC，价值 80.8 亿美元

MARA 卖得最多，40581 枚，均价 74446，套现 30.3 亿

9 月底之后那 13597 枚卖在 81039，换回 11 亿，其中 7.5 亿拿去还 BTC 抵押贷款，赎回 17477 枚质押的币，总债务砍掉 37%

Riot 第二，20264 枚，均价 73231，套现 15.1 亿

它的持仓从年初 18005 枚，卖到 9 月底只剩 2418 枚，砍掉 87%。钱拿去盖数据中心，顺手还清了 Coinbase 那笔 2 亿的信贷

第三是 Bitdeer，10553 枚，7.87 亿

再加上 Cango 7001 枚、CleanSpark 5715 枚，前五家占了全部卖出量的 77.7%。14 家里 94% 的量来自矿企

这些钱没拿去赌方向

还债、买电、盖机房、付 AI 数据中心的施工款，公告里写得清清楚楚

现在反过头来问，币安卖了多少

能查到的是 11 月 15 日，全交易所的 BTC 余额 259 万枚，币安 674599 枚，七天净流入 7712 枚。砸得最凶的这几天，它的币在往里进

一家交易所要抛几十亿的现货，反而币安的这个钱包里边还在往里进比特币

中本聪给比特币赋予的第一个属性就是自由，涨的时候享受它带来的红利，流动性危机的时候也得承担这个自由的代价

Brev was acquired by NVIDIA 2.5 yrs ago. Going from startup to a big company was a big change. 
Over drinks, I told Jensen:

“This is the biggest company I’ve ever worked for”

He smiled, looked at me, and replies: 

“Me too”

I survived this long at NVIDIA because Jensen made it feel like working at a startup. He understood that layers of a company, necessary for operationalizing work, also suppress information flow. It happens naturally:
• People want praise, so they highlight the work they’re doing well & hide problems 
• People want ownership, so they suppress ideas that don’t come from their org

But at Jensen’s Nvidia you could email 1000+ people at once to force information to flow outside of an org that might be suppressing it. In fact, you are expected to, sending an email with the “Top 5 Things” you’re working on to everyone at once, to force information to flow outside of a bad manager or org who might be suppressing it. I jokingly call email at NVIDIA a “mosh pit”.

He was always chasing information that was stuck in the corners of the company, always learning from the company he was leading. 

NVIDIA is the world’s largest startup because there’s a founder driving it. Taking NVIDIA from its founder is a mistake.

text:
Traditional APIs rent you a pipe. Pocket gives you the network. 

With Alchemy, Infura or QuickNode you get an endpoint, a dashboard and a monthly bill that grows with your traffic. 

With Pocket you stake POKT once as an application, get matched with independent suppliers every single session, and pay per relay through an on-chain burn. 

No single operator owns your traffic. No rate plan caps what you can grow into. Any service can be listed permissionlessly, and anyone can become a supplier. 

The result is infrastructure you participate in, not infrastructure you rent. 

Renting works. Owning a real stake in the network you actually use every day works better.

text:
一定要相信我，美国人很快就会发现的：

无论他们换多少个白人，甚至是印度裔CEO，都没法像老黄那样搞定亚洲市场、亚洲供应链。

因为老黄做生意的手法，就是我们广东人、闽粤那边非常熟悉的江湖打法，特别老派。

吃饭喝酒，拜不拜把子、滴血认不认兄弟另说，但人情世故一定在。

交朋友认准一个，就是长期打交道。你看一眼英伟达的供应链就知道了：台积电造芯片，韩国企业供内存，台湾厂商造服务器。

这些公司，全都是老黄一家一家跑出来的，一顿一顿饭吃，一年一年维护出来的关系。

2024年，老黄拉着台积电创办人张忠谋、广达创办人林百里跑到台北去吃蚵仔煎。

第二天又在一家叫“砖窑”的家常菜馆摆了一场供应链顶流饭局。鸿海、广达、和硕、华硕的大佬们，全卖老黄面子。

英伟达，或者说黄仁勋“江湖救急”的事件比比皆是。

我说个最典型的。一家做配送机器人的公司，当时真的撑不下去了。创始人艾克沙尼自己说，2023年圣诞节前投资人临时撤资，工资发不出，已经在跟破产律师沟通了。最后他给老黄发了封邮件。

后来他在推特上回忆，老黄早上6点给他打了个电话，当天晚些时候亲自带着英伟达团队跟他坐在一起吃饭，商量过桥融资。四个月后，他们在纳斯达克敲钟了。

在他后来的长访谈里经常提这段，当时公司要活下来需要几家合作方一起点头，黄仁勋就是那个关键人物。

再看供应链，韩国SK集团会长崔泰源就公开讲过黄仁勋是怎么催货的。

老黄要的是AI芯片离不开的高带宽内存HBM，他希望把供应时间提前六个月。半导体提前半年，背后涉及研发、产能、整个公司的资源安排。

就在关键节点上，两人吃了一顿饭。两个能拍板的人直接坐下来聊，当面说清楚你有什么需求、我有什么需求、难处在哪，然后各自回去推动。

就不信现在英伟达换个白人CEO，崔泰源会鸟你。

老黄和台积电张忠谋的交情，比这波AI热潮早很多年。路透社根据张忠谋早年回忆录报道过，1998年英伟达人手不足，台积电还派了两名生产专家去帮忙。后来张忠谋甚至两次邀请黄仁勋去台积电当CEO。

直到今年接受访谈，老黄谈起台积电，用的还是那种特别老派的生意观。他说合作这么多年，有时候自己占点便宜，有时候吃点亏，但整体上基于的都是彼此的信任和依赖。

几百亿美金的产能分配，靠的真不是白纸黑字的合同，很可能就是几个老头坐下来喝杯茶、抽根雪茄，拍胸脯说一句：“兄弟，这批货我给你留了。”第二天，全场的机器就为你连轴转。

老黄自己也被人救过。英伟达刚创业时给日本世嘉做芯片，技术路线出问题，项目做不下去，公司快倒了。就在那时，世嘉还是投了500万美元，帮英伟达撑过最难的一关。

今年7月，黄仁勋去了东京，见到世嘉前社长入交昭一郎，当面感谢30年前那次帮助。话说得很重：“没有当年的帮助，就没有今天的英伟达。”

全世界最先进的芯片背后，依然有这种古老的力量。英伟达的供应链跟老黄的出身有至关重要的关系，全是中国人、韩国人、日本人，老黄跟他们有天然的亲近感。

很多人可能瞧不上这种东西，但这就是生意。生意，就是人情世故。

text:
Bitcoin is below $70K again.

This is not something that I'm worried about, especially since we've seen much bigger liquidation events in the past.

But this time, I'm more concerned about the negative Bitcoin ETF inflows.

Here's what's happening ↓

1. ETF Outflows

$2.35B left Bitcoin ETFs in just two weeks. That's a reversal of the buying pressure that helped BTC recover earlier this year.

2. Nvidia

Nvidia dropped 13% in the past week, with BTC falling alongside it. It's not true 100% of the time, but crypto often follows big tech's moves.

3. Interest Rates

U.S. inflation is proving stubborn, and traders are betting on another Fed rate hike. As per usual, higher interest rates make assets like BTC less attractive.

4. Strategy

MSCI is removing $MSTR from its indexes. That could trigger forced stock selling and make it harder for @Strategy to raise money for more BTC purchases.

5. Liquidations

Around $1.5B was liquidated in 24 hours, compared to $19B during the Oct 2025 crash.

I don't think liquidations alone explain this selloff. We can call bottom once ETF inflows return and BTC reclaims its 200-day moving average.

Until then, be smart and protect your capital.

text:
美银最新一期FlowShow很值得看看，Hartnett对市场的态度还是很谨慎，为什么他继续坚持Risk-off，什么条件下才会重新转向Risk-on？这也是理解未来几周美股走势的关键。这份报告最值得关注的有几个方面：
1）全球股票基金单周流入983亿美元，究竟是谁在买？
2）美国科技股遭遇大规模抛售，为什么全球科技基金仍然持续吸金？
3）美元、原油、美债收益率和全球流动性之间，正在发生什么变化？
4）标普500的8000点和7000点情景，背后分别对应什么样的市场结构？

聊聊Hartnett这期报告聊的几个要点
1、美元成"破坏之球"，全球流动性全面收缩
他的逻辑简明直接：美元飙升加上黄金跌破4000美元，等同于全球流动性的撤退信号。

2、Hartnett为转向风险偏好设定了三个前提条件：油价（WTI）跌破70美元、10年期美债收益率降至4.5%以下、美元开始下行。周五收盘时，三项条件无一达标。
他的逻辑是油价影响通胀、
10年美债收益率决定贴现率和融资成本、美元走强会增加新兴市场的融资压力。

3、而关于资金流向
这里其实有一个分化，前四周被动工具的买入规模约3171亿美元，而主动基金存在较大赎回压力。这背后有一个重要的点：
市场上涨究竟是主动投资者重新看好基本面，还是被动资金、ETF和长期配置资金持续买入的结果？

两者对市场的意义是不同的：
1）主动投资者推动，意味着风险偏好回归和盈利预期有更强共识。
2）而只是被动资金推动，意味着风险偏好和盈利预期并没有形成共识，这种情况容易出现指数上涨、个股分化、行业内部集中度上升的情况。一旦ETF资金流入放缓，市场的边际买盘就可能迅速减弱。

4、Hartnett 对未来市场的另一个判断：投资者情绪悲观，但实际仓位并没有那么悲观。
Hartnett 特别提到即将公布的11月17日美银全球基金经理调查需要重点关注三个指标：繁荣预期、现金仓位、实际股票仓位。
如果现金仓位上升至4.2%以上，说明基金经理开始真正降低风险资产配置。这反而可能改善市场情绪指标，减少之前的拥挤交易风险。

这里有一个潜在的风险：
同一天美银经济团队认为，通胀持续高于2%目标，可能迫使美联储重新考虑此前的宽松路径，甚至需要进一步提高利率。
同时，该团队也承认如果经济明显放缓、美国与伊朗达成协议导致油价回落，或者股票市场大幅下跌，后续加息可能推迟甚至取消。

把本期Hartnett报告与近期看到的的机构资金流、AI融资、美国财政和美联储政策结合起来，我的判断是：
市场可能已经完成一轮仓位清洗，但宏观压力和流动性风险尚未解除

1）短期：市场有反弹条件，但不能简单理解为新一轮牛市已经开始
对冲基金已经大幅降低杠杆，部分拥挤交易被清理。长期基金却仍在持续买入股票。
这意味着市场下跌时的边际卖盘可能减少，出现空头回补和逢低买入推动的反弹。但反弹是否能够持续，需要观察主动基金是否重新增加风险敞口。

2）中期 最大的风险来自宏观金融条件与AI政策及融资态势的碰撞

我认为目前最值得警惕的组合是：油价长期维持高位、美元继续走强、美债收益率居高不下、科技公司债券发行增加且融资成本进一步上升。
这些因素同时发生，就可能出现AI产业需求仍然旺盛，但资本市场对投资回报率的审视和挑剔更高，这会导致科技产业内部出现更加明显的分化。

拥有强大现金流、资产负债表和商业化能力的公司，会比依赖外部融资的公司更有优势。

所以未来核心是看中期宏观环境的变化，个人角度就聚焦就看三个层面：
1）油价/通胀的走势；
2）中期选举新政治生态下AI政策确实是进一步收紧还只是纠偏；
3）AI商业化是不是还处于加速状态（大云厂的云业务增速和模型厂的实际营收增速）。

text:
Good comment on the ETH SoV discourse.

ETH succeeding as SoV *could* mean Ethereum shrinks to just being the ETH transport layer. To me, that's a bad outcome.

Instead, the outcome worth fighting for is the one where ETH succeeds *because* Ethereum succeeds in its ambition to be the base layer of *all* onchain activity - with all the technological ambition necessary for that role.

Where I (strongly!) disagree with the tweet though is on the goal to "capture an increasing share of the value it creates". Ethereum can either be run as civic infrastructure, or as a business. These are at odds! The more Ethereum tries to capture value, the more it gives up its credible neutrality and with it the shot at being in a unique role among all blockchains.

Instead, I think the right way to see Ethereum and ETH is as two *independent but synergistic* goods. ETH succeeds not as network equity, but as SoV, the trustless native asset of the entire (onchain, which will over time be an unnecessary qualifier) economy. To achieve that SoV status, Ethereum needs to be *inevitable*! And Ethereum is inevitable precisely if people can have long term trust in its credible neutrality and in its ability to continuously deliver on its technical ambitions.

text:
Nice one, some quick thoughts :)

- I don’t think pqai27 is “rushing” nor that it is done for memetic benefits, though there are such benefits undeniably. While there are ofc discussions to have on the how and some who disagree with the feasibility, many see the delivery in ‘27 as doable. At least more than necessary to believe that the plan is not crazy, though ambitious. I believe your post underrates the current progress toward freezing signature schemes, and overrates how committal the decision is.
- We are not *not* shipping user-friendly features. Frames is very likely on the path, and is one of the most consequential user-facing upgrades of the last five years. With PQ as a motivation to make users migrate, there is a huge opportunity to deliver even more value there.
- Perhaps the most potent argument for me: not addressing the PQ threat with urgency could mean we still don’t get user-facing features by 2028. The Damocles sword, as @casparschwa puts it, of new results and uncertainty is imo the riskiest part of not addressing the threat head-on, and definitively circumvent the thrash of governance in the time of known unknowns. I would bet that the lift from a truly all-hands Manhattan project would do more for core development and execution than any other vehicle. There is also the off chance (i’m bullish, but I recognise that i am still an outlier here, though in good company already) that we end up shipping pq-decoupled consensus in 2027. This would mean order of magnitude faster finality and a clear shot towards shorter slots soon after. Even if not, I do not see a better path to landing at the end of 2028 with everyone checked off from our bucket list: pq, privacy, fast ethereum, focil and scale. Living in the in-between until then is to me a recipe for failure.

quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

author: hmalviya9
quoted_text:
David chaum, "Godfather of anonymous communication" gave a wonderful routing protocol, build for preserving your privacy known as mixnets
 
@nym mixnet mode works on the same concept introduced by chaum on network level privacy

this mode routes internet traffic through 5 hopes which involves different techniques:

- sender's device connects to nym network

- data is fragmented into specialized cryptographic packets which hides routing information and maintains a uniform size of a packet making original size harder to predict

- packets jumps into entry gateway where sender ip is known, then hops to mix nodes

- independent mix nodes only knows the path to forward packets while maintaining the data encrypted

- packets are mixed and forwarded to receiver in random delays which makes observer hard to assess original timing

- if the user is not using internet, nym network sends dummy packets to confuse the observer about online presence of user
- finally, packet is forwarded to exit gateway, encryption removed and get access to the destination website

cover traffic and data mixing plays a vital role in harder traceability for observer to determine which user generated the actual packet

text:
从字节离职的时候，我是真的放弃了很多很多钱。大厂的待遇是真的好，给的钱也是真多。

但我还是走了。因为我在里面聊了很多人，每一个都很优秀，但几乎每一个人，眼里都没有光。

我后来和很多朋友交流，我们得出一个一致的结论：大厂就是「高薪毒药」。这也是很多人眼里明明没有光，却依然在大厂坚持的原因。

我很庆幸我的职级是 3 开头。这个位置很巧，能同时看到 2 开头和 4 开头的朋友在做什么、是什么样的精神状态。看完之后我没觉得谁更自由。

如果一个人一年要被迫换三次业务线，那真的很难对任何一桩业务具备 ownership。每个季度定的 OKR 基本都是 data-driven，自上而下的人其实都不具备对单个业务场景的 blueprint 权限。因为分得太细，上通下达的沟通成本太高，日常要沟通交流的细节太多，很多人也就没意识去思考全局了——或者说，本来也没有权限去思考。

结果就是每天迷失在大量的细节里。所以大厂的战略部门是真的很关键，而其他所有人，哪怕职级再高，基本也都是执行方。

大厂里的每个人，哪怕职级很高，也都是漂亮的白金螺丝钉。做的工作都非常有意义，但自由和发挥空间确实非常有限。想执行一项策略，需要花更长的时间、更大的心力去布局，而且内部竞争也是真的大。

2025 年 2 月，我在厂里写过另一篇推文。是那个时候开始，我开始认真思考属于我自己的 passion 是什么。说实话，此刻的当下，我依然有点迷茫。

（「高薪毒药」这四个字不是骂人。这是写实。）

text:
Wow～有一位专门做情报追踪的老哥，用一群agent对近2000篇与黄仁勋相关的报道进行了分析与评分，覆盖了40家美欧主流媒体。
🔗：https://t.co/EAJbGSU5Fg

核心数据规模约为 1641–1831篇 报道、40家 媒体、30个 被追踪的claim、2566次引用。

🔴 整体规模与时间分布
总报道量：约1641篇明确提及Jensen或丑闻，总扫描约1831篇。
时间结构极度不均衡：97%的报道发生在11月8日之后。10月29日–11月7日仅42篇。
11月8日（Jensen内部信承认婚外情）之后爆发到1599篇，峰值在11月12日（536篇）。

🔴核心Claim溯源（“种子报道”）
网站把30个claim拆开追踪“谁先报、谁引用谁”
几乎所有重大指控的“原始种子”都指向纽约时报或紧随其后的Bloomberg。后续媒体高度依赖这些源头，而非独立核实。

🔴引用网络与PageRank
641篇可读报道产生了2566次引用，涉及77个来源。
纽约时报是绝对中心节点：被34家媒体引用，累计约370次引用指向它。
PageRank排名前列：纽约时报>华尔街日报 > 路透社。
网络结构呈现典型的“源头→主流媒体→进一步扩散”层级，存在大量“未具名消息源”

🔴“事实 vs 指控”处理方式
间谍相关标题中，仅约7%直接当作事实陈述，多数使用“alleged / reported / according to”等模糊用词。

但“未证实”信息更新滞后：司法部和新加坡在11月12–13日表示“未认定其为间谍/缺乏起诉证据”，在之后197篇仍提间谍指控的报道中，只有11篇（约6%）提及这些澄清。
“被罢免/ousted”类表述在标题中更常被当作事实使用，而官方文件是“辞职”。

🔴市场影响数据
10月28日（纽约时报报道前）：市值约 5.19万亿美元，股价约215.38美元。
11月13日：市值约 3.92万亿美元，股价约162.85美元。
期间损失约 1.27万亿美元（-24.4%）。

🔴 与其他CEO离职事件对比
在相同5家媒体、相同标准下：
Jensen相关报道量远超其他案例（19天内约276篇）。
对比🆚：因特尔 Krzanich（15篇）、麦当劳 Easterbrook（37篇）、英国石油公司 Looney（52篇）。

从引用网络和报道节奏来看，纽约时报不只是间谍叙事的发起者，更是整轮负面舆论的核心发动机。

它率先抛出间谍指控，随后在关键节点连续跟进，形成“种子—发酵—引爆”的完整链条。后续媒体大多选择引用而非独立核实，使得叙事沿着引用网络快速扩散。即便司法部和新加坡方面后来表示无法认定相关指控，澄清信息也几乎没能穿透已形成的舆论惯性。

最终，一场本应停留在事实核查层面的事件，在纽约时报的推动下，演变成了对黄仁勋及其公司的高强度舆论围剿。

quoted_text:
I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

Alibaba has launched Qwen4 Max, gaining 9 points over Qwen3.8 Max on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and landing 3 points behind Kimi K3.1 Pro at ~11% lower Cost per Task

Qwen4 Max, using xhigh reasoning effort, scores 43 on the Intelligence Index, 9 points ahead of Qwen3.8 Max (xhigh) and 3 points behind Kimi K3.1 Pro (max, 46)

Key takeaways:

➤ Qwen4 Max improves on every evaluation in the Index vs Qwen3.8 Max (xhigh, 34): HLE-Diamond +21 points (24% to 45%), AA-Omniscience +18 points, AutomationBench-AA +17 points, CritPt v2 +13 points, Terminal-Bench-Science +11 points, Terminal-Bench 4.0 +9 points, GDP.pdf +3 points, FrontierCode 2.0 +3 points and AA-Briefcase +82 Elo.

➤ Qwen4 Max costs $3.27 per Intelligence Index task, ~3x less than Qwen3.8 Max ($10.02) and ~11% less than Kimi K3.1 Pro ($3.68): This is driven by 25% lower per-token pricing than Qwen3.8 Max, 70% cheaper cache hits and lower token usage. Tencent Hy4 costs ~3x less per task ($1.03) than Qwen4 Max but scores 8 points lower on the Index.

➤ Qwen4 Max uses 39% fewer output tokens per task than Qwen3.8 Max: ~105k output tokens per Intelligence Index task vs ~171k for Qwen3.8 Max, ~72k for Kimi K3.1 Pro and ~78k for Tencent Hy4. Qwen4 Max uses fewer tokens, while increasing 9 points on the Intelligence Index

➤ Improvements in AA-Briefcase (knowledge work): On AA-Briefcase, our evaluation of agentic work across real business files, Qwen4 Max reaches 1686 Elo vs 1674 for Kimi K3.1 Pro and 1446 for Tencent Hy4.

➤ Qwen4 Max trails Kimi K3.1 Pro on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and Tencent Hy4 on FrontierCode 2.0: Qwen4 Max scores 48% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 vs 67% for Kimi K3.1 Pro and 37% for Tencent Hy4. text:
推荐港大 HKUDS 开源的 AgentPilot，把 Agent 在反复试错过程中「下一步该做什么」单独作为一个策略优化问题。

它用一个 9B 策略模型指导 Codex、Claude Code、DeepSeek Harness 等 Agent，决定从哪个版本继续改进、探索什么方向，以及如何分配试错预算。

具体来说，AgentPilot 会记录每次尝试的结果、版本关系和剩余预算，通过 KL-UCB 或 Policy Memory 利用历史反馈，持续调整后续的探索策略。

项目还提供 RSI Arena，用来评估 Agent 在多轮尝试中的改进效果，以及这些改进能否泛化到未见任务。

作者也报告，在 Terminal-Bench 2.1 实验中，经过 10 轮改进，未见任务上的成绩从 44.9% 提升至 69.4%，提高了 24.5 个百分点。

我比较关注它对 Agent 自我改进的一个具体切入点：把试错过程中的策略选择单独拿出来优化，让 Agent 能够根据真实反馈，逐渐学会如何更有效地探索。

对于长时间运行的 Agent，如何利用有限的试错预算，可能会直接影响系统最终能改进到什么程度。

💻 GitHub: https://t.co/HtyN0xhFo8

quoted_text:
Google TPU 重點更新：OpenAI 與 Anthropic 新訂單推升出貨能見度至 2029 年、v10 產品線大幅調整 (改為 Quillfish)、聯發科與 Broadcom 為供應商中之領先關注焦點

我最新的產業調查與研究結論：

1. 訂單能見度與出貨規劃：
受惠於 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 強勁新訂單，Google TPU 出貨能見度已達 2029 年，優於 Nvidia GPU 與其他 AI ASIC（多數為 4Q27–2Q28）。

(1) 自 2028 年起，v9 將成 Google 自建算力的主力方案，v8 系列（8t／8i 或其設計變種）訂單可視為來自 OpenAI 與 Anthropic。

(2) 2028–2029 年合計需求數量：OpenAI 約 12M（聯發科設計的 8t），Anthropic 約 14M（Broadcom 設計的 8i），兩者需求均呈逐年成長趨勢。OpenAI 採買斷，Anthropic 則是租賃與買斷都有。

(3) 考量供應鏈限制，2027–2029 年較合理的 TPU 出貨估算分別為 8–9M、14–15M、16–18M。市場普遍預期 AI 資本支出於 2028 年見頂，但此規劃顯示 TPU 在 2029 年仍具出貨成長動能，關鍵在於 AI 服務龍頭 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 的直接訂單。

2. v10 產品線與供應鏈調整：
v10 由原先的 Icefish 與 Merope／Bladerunner 改為 Quillfish，預計 2029 年量產，設計服務訂單由聯發科取得。

(1) Icefish 改為 v11，預計 2030 年量產，設計服務訂單同由聯發科取得。Merope 能見度較低，供應商未定，也可能取消。

(2) 聯發科將是 v9（Humufish & Triggerfish）與 v10（Quillfish）的獨家供應商，2027–2029 年占整體 TPU 供應比重分別約 45–50%、50–55%、55–60%。TPU 對其營收與利潤的貢獻預計逐年增加。

(3) 自 v9 起新款 TPU 均採 Intel EMIB-T 先進封裝。考量初期量產能力，預期至 2029 年仍以 v8 系列為 TPU 出貨主力。v8 預期將是聯發科與 Broadcom 未來數年的 TPU 事業獲利成長的主要來源，因長期累積的學習曲線效益明顯，加上雙方負責關鍵零組件與材料採購。

3/ 市場關注度與供應商展望：
近期事件有助提升並維持 Google TPU 的市場關注度，關鍵設計服務商聯發科與 Broadcom 可望成為供應鏈首要焦點。

(1) Nvidia CEO 接班的不確定性，有利 Google 與客戶洽談 2028 年後的長期規劃。OpenAI 與 Anthropic 均為 TPU 關鍵客戶，其 IPO 也有助提升並維持 TPU 關注度，而聯發科與 Broadcom 是市場最容易聯想到的供應商。

(2) 聯發科無疑是未來數年 TPU 的最大贏家，身為 v9 後的獨家設計供應商，加上供應比重與 TPU 出貨成長同時逐年提升，均有利 TPU 事業營收規模擴大。高毛利率的 8t 系列出貨能見度達 2029 年，為關鍵利潤來源。

(3) 因 Broadcom 主導 8i 設計，故毛利率更高於 8t，有利該公司利潤成長。不過，需注意的是，Broadcom 未來數年的營運重點為非 TPU 的 XPU 與 AI 網路晶片訂單，預計最快 2027 年，非 TPU 營收將超越 TPU。

author: cryptoxiao
quoted_text:
不知道为什么这些 personal agent 一个个都给每个用户分了个虚拟机沙盒，一个云端沙盒一个月几十美金的成本。

有人跟我说，不用虚拟机做沙盒，agent 在哪运行？浏览器怎么访问网页？用户上传的文件放到哪？agent 怎么执行 skill 里面的命令？agent 生成的代码怎么安全执行？

我瞬间感觉这么多年的系统都白做了。我做第一个 agent 的时候，一个基本假设就是一个 Go 服务里面支持多个并发用户，从来没想过一个用户能独占一个进程，更没想到有些 agent 竟然敢把 API key 放在沙盒里面。

浏览器我只用过无头浏览器，没想过用虚拟机这么奢侈的东西。用户上传的文件我只能想到 GCS 或者 Google Drive 这样的虚拟文件系统，没想到其他 agent 搞了个真的文件系统。

最近我用 Claude Code，一个 session 跑了几天之后 agent 就占了 5GB 的物理内存，经常 CPU 占用 100%，有时候还会卡死。

这些兄弟们大概是把 OpenClaw 或者 Codex 或者 Deepseek Harness 换了个壳子，装进虚拟机，就算是 personal agent 了。

只能说是做 LLM 和 agent 的兄弟们都太有钱了，动不动几百万年薪，不像我们做系统的整天为了几微秒延迟、几 KB 内存天天扣扣搜搜的。

text:
比特币 2026 年初至今跌 22%，可能将成为历史上首次连续两年收跌的年份。

小编根据公开信息整理了一下比特币历年涨跌数据，2011 至 2025 年的 15 个完整年度中，比特币 11 年上涨、4 年下跌。

不算今年的话，下跌的 4 个年份分别为：

-2014 年跌 58%（Mt. Gox 停止提现、破产），
-2018 年跌 73%（代币融资泡沫退潮、监管收紧），2022 年跌 65%（美联储加息，UST 与 FTX 崩溃），
-2025 年跌 6%（关税冲击、10 月爆仓潮）。

涨幅最大的年份为 2013 年，上涨 5,507%；其次是 2011 年的 1,473% 和 2017 年的 1,331%。

2026 年截至 11 月 13 日，比特币从 87,509 美元跌至 68,249 美元，年内下跌 22.0%；

主要受加息与资金撤出、科技股回撤以及各类 CEX 被盗事件影响，仍在延续去年的负收益。

若全年收跌，将是比特币历史上，首次连续两个完整年度下跌。

text:
correct me if i am wrong, but @ton_blockchain is emerging as one of the strongest experiments in building a sharing economy powered by a native token.

most of us completely missed what happened in May this year when @telegram and @durov took over the primary responsibility for TON's future direction, including protocol development and validator participation.

this changes the entire equation.

the way durov is promoting TON these days could eventually bring more confidence, developers, and consumers into its ecosystem.

but i think the real opportunity is somewhere else.

telegram already has millions of communities organised around shared interests. what if every community could launch its own coin paired against GRAM, and distribute those coins based on contributions, skills, knowledge, and commitments?

imagine a telegram group with 10,000 members interested in learning AI.

the admin launches a community coin and creates 100 challenges. each challenge has a deadline, verification criteria, and reward attached to it.

members commit to completing challenges by staking a small amount of GRAM or community coins.

those who complete their commitments earn coins. those who fail lose a predefined portion of their stake, subject to fair verification and dispute rules.

now imagine those earned coins could be swapped into GRAM through a liquidity pool, while members could also stake GRAM to participate in new challenges and earn additional community coins.

you have just created an economic loop around human productivity.

i call these Human Commitment Markets.

these markets allow people to make commitments, coordinate around shared goals, and receive economic rewards when they successfully fulfil those commitments.

the important part is designing mechanisms where rewards are funded by genuine demand for completed work, rather than endless token emissions.

every successful commitment could improve a member's portable reputation, allowing them to access higher-value challenges with lower collateral requirements.

admins become market creators. members become contributors. communities become small economies.

now imagine millions of such communities, each experimenting with different incentive designs, reputation systems, and commitment rules.

telegram already has the social graph. TON has the settlement infrastructure. GRAM can become the common economic rail connecting these communities.

the missing primitive is a marketplace for verifiable human commitments.

this could turn telegram groups from attention markets into productivity markets.

author: Lithos_eth
quoted_text:
you used ai everyday but do you know the next big problem with it?                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          

the next big problem with ai isn't how intelligent the models become

it's who gets access to the data they work with

think about an ai agent processing your business records, trading , customer information or private documents like id etc

you want the result, but you don't want the person operating the server reading your data

that's the problem confidential computing is trying to solve

@Acurast approaches it differently: instead of relying on one cloud provider, it turns smartphones into a global compute network

the work runs inside hardware-backed trusted execution environments (tees), which isolate sensitive data during execution

hardware attestation also helps verify that the workload is running in a genuine, trusted environment

so a phone isn't just sitting in someone pocket

it can contribute to infrastructure that developers use to run apis, ai workloads and applications without handing all their trust to one server operator

and base:0xc5fed7c8ccc75d8a72b601a66dffd7a489073f0b helps coordinate and pay for the compute powering that network

decentralizing compute is one part of the problem

making that compute private and verifiable is the part i think deserves more attention 

and as i've always said, privacy is freedom
without it, your guess is as good as mine

text:
美银警告：强美元正在抽干全球流动性，风险资产的机会可能要等到明年春天。

这份报告给出了三个明确的市场转向条件：

WTI 原油跌破 70 美元
美国 10 年期国债收益率跌破 4.5%
美元开始走弱

看了下，截至 11 月 13 日，这三个条件一个都没有满足。

美元指数升至 103.42，10 年期美债收益率达到 5.15%，WTI 原油仍在 89 美元附近。Hartnett 因此将美元见顶的预期推迟到 2027 年 2—3 月，风险资产的入场窗口也延后至明年春季。

但这份报告并不是主张现在无脑做空，认为市场存在两股相反力量：

压制多头：美元走强、美债收益率高企、通胀顽固、美联储仍有加息压力。

阻止空头：政府托底、美国富裕家庭股票财富效应仍然强劲，消费暂时有韧性。

所以才会出现一个尴尬局面：追涨有风险，做空也不容易赚钱。

报告还给标普500划了两条观察线：

7000点以下，警惕美元流动性危机与经济放缓中的政策失误；

8000点以上，则可能说明市场风险偏好重新恢复。这是情景判断，不是指数必然抵达的目标。

对比特币来说，目前正在经历恐慌、阵痛期，距离真正的上涨需要时间来修复。

text:
比特币 2026 年初至今跌 22%，可能将成为历史上首次连续两年收跌的年份。

小编根据公开信息整理了一下比特币历年涨跌数据，2011 至 2025 年的 15 个完整年度中，比特币 11 年上涨、4 年下跌。

不算今年的话，下跌的 4 个年份分别为：

-2014 年跌 58%（Mt. Gox 停止提现、破产），
-2018 年跌 73%（代币融资泡沫退潮、监管收紧），2022 年跌 65%（美联储加息，UST 与 FTX 崩溃），
-2025 年跌 6%（关税冲击、10 月爆仓潮）。

涨幅最大的年份为 2013 年，上涨 5,507%；其次是 2011 年的 1,473% 和 2017 年的 1,331%。

2026 年截至 11 月 13 日，比特币从 87,509 美元跌至 68,249 美元，年内下跌 22.0%；

主要受加息与资金撤出、科技股回撤以及各类 CEX 被盗事件影响，仍在延续去年的负收益。

若全年收跌，将是比特币历史上，首次连续两个完整年度下跌。

text:
Google TPU 重點更新：OpenAI 與 Anthropic 新訂單推升出貨能見度至 2029 年、v10 產品線大幅調整 (改為 Quillfish)、聯發科與 Broadcom 為供應商中之領先關注焦點

我最新的產業調查與研究結論：

1. 訂單能見度與出貨規劃：
受惠於 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 強勁新訂單，Google TPU 出貨能見度已達 2029 年，優於 Nvidia GPU 與其他 AI ASIC（多數為 4Q27–2Q28）。

(1) 自 2028 年起，v9 將成 Google 自建算力的主力方案，v8 系列（8t／8i 或其設計變種）訂單可視為來自 OpenAI 與 Anthropic。

(2) 2028–2029 年合計需求數量：OpenAI 約 12M（聯發科設計的 8t），Anthropic 約 14M（Broadcom 設計的 8i），兩者需求均呈逐年成長趨勢。OpenAI 採買斷，Anthropic 則是租賃與買斷都有。

(3) 考量供應鏈限制，2027–2029 年較合理的 TPU 出貨估算分別為 8–9M、14–15M、16–18M。市場普遍預期 AI 資本支出於 2028 年見頂，但此規劃顯示 TPU 在 2029 年仍具出貨成長動能，關鍵在於 AI 服務龍頭 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 的直接訂單。

2. v10 產品線與供應鏈調整：
v10 由原先的 Icefish 與 Merope／Bladerunner 改為 Quillfish，預計 2029 年量產，設計服務訂單由聯發科取得。

(1) Icefish 改為 v11，預計 2030 年量產，設計服務訂單同由聯發科取得。Merope 能見度較低，供應商未定，也可能取消。

(2) 聯發科將是 v9（Humufish & Triggerfish）與 v10（Quillfish）的獨家供應商，2027–2029 年占整體 TPU 供應比重分別約 45–50%、50–55%、55–60%。TPU 對其營收與利潤的貢獻預計逐年增加。

(3) 自 v9 起新款 TPU 均採 Intel EMIB-T 先進封裝。考量初期量產能力，預期至 2029 年仍以 v8 系列為 TPU 出貨主力。v8 預期將是聯發科與 Broadcom 未來數年的 TPU 事業獲利成長的主要來源，因長期累積的學習曲線效益明顯，加上雙方負責關鍵零組件與材料採購。

3/ 市場關注度與供應商展望：
近期事件有助提升並維持 Google TPU 的市場關注度，關鍵設計服務商聯發科與 Broadcom 可望成為供應鏈首要焦點。

(1) Nvidia CEO 接班的不確定性，有利 Google 與客戶洽談 2028 年後的長期規劃。OpenAI 與 Anthropic 均為 TPU 關鍵客戶，其 IPO 也有助提升並維持 TPU 關注度，而聯發科與 Broadcom 是市場最容易聯想到的供應商。

(2) 聯發科無疑是未來數年 TPU 的最大贏家，身為 v9 後的獨家設計供應商，加上供應比重與 TPU 出貨成長同時逐年提升，均有利 TPU 事業營收規模擴大。高毛利率的 8t 系列出貨能見度達 2029 年，為關鍵利潤來源。

(3) 因 Broadcom 主導 8i 設計，故毛利率更高於 8t，有利該公司利潤成長。不過，需注意的是，Broadcom 未來數年的營運重點為非 TPU 的 XPU 與 AI 網路晶片訂單，預計最快 2027 年，非 TPU 營收將超越 TPU。

text:
I ran the numbers on BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF, and the average buyer got in around $81K.

BTC is at $65K, so they're sitting on about a 19% loss.

Yet...almost none of them have sold yet. Here's why that matters for you:

The short version: don't count on a fast recovery, don't chase bounces, and DCA monthly until the signals at the end flip.

/1 The ETF crowd hasn't sold yet

I took every day of flows into BlackRock's ETF (IBIT, by far the biggest) since launch and weighted it by that day's BTC price. 

Net inflows come out to about $80.7K'ish per BTC. 

BTC has spent most of 2026 below that line. In Sep–Oct it finally got above it, ran to about $86K, and held for a month. Then the Binance hack hit, and it fell 20%.

Since the hack, about $3B has left the spot BTC ETFs, $2.35B of it from IBIT, with outflows on 10 of the last 11 trading days.

But IBIT still holds about 795K BTC, only 4% below its peak. Most ETF holders haven't sold, instead they're sitting on a loss and waiting.

What to do: That's a lot of people who'll be tempted to sell when they get back to even. If you bought higher, don't count on a quick trip back to $81K to get out. 

If you trade, a bounce toward $81K is a place to take some profit, not to add. I'd only buy more aggressively once BTC is back above $81K and ETF flows have turned positive.

/2 Crypto's cash is shrinking

Stablecoin supply shrank by $15.5B in the last 30 days. Three quarters of that was USDT and USDC, the main dollars people use to buy crypto.

Less cash on the sidelines means fewer buyers for the dip.

The long-term picture is different. Stablecoin payments hit $482B in the first 9 months of this year, up 45% (per Allium). People are using crypto dollars more, even while they hold fewer of them.

What to do: Don't chase green days. Stick to your DCA. And watch USDT & USDC supply (free on DefiLlama). 

When it starts growing again, the buyers are coming back.

/3 Buybacks are a cushion, not a floor

At its current pace, pump is buying back about 18% of its circulating market cap a year. It's still down 35% since the hack.

Hyperliquid buys back about 5% a year, and HYPE is down 17%. That's better than BTC (-20%), ETH (-23%) & SOL (-29%).

The difference is the business behind it. Hyperliquid's buybacks over the last 30 days ran above its 12-month average. Pump ran below.

What to do: Before you buy a token for its buybacks, pull up its revenue. If the last few months are trending down, skip it, no matter how big the buyback looks.

/4 So what am I doing?

DCA monthly. At these prices, I'm happy to keep buying BTC and HYPE every month. DCA keeps it simpler than trying to time this.

Keep cash. If the selling isn't done, you'll want ammo lower.

No leverage. Not in this market, and it's not something I usually do anyway.

Be VERY Picky on alts. If I buy alts, only ones with a growing business behind the buybacks.

/5 What would tell me it's turned

USDT & USDC growing again.

ETF flows turning positive.

The Fed done hiking, and then cutting.

BTC back above $81K and holding it.

What are you doing in this market?

quoted_text:
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

text:
The Justice Department announced yesterday that it had seized infrastructure used in a North Korean hacking operation called FaceStealer.

According to the DOJ, the operation has resulted in more than $400 million in cryptocurrency theft over the past 18 months.

The attack method is worth understanding because it exploits something most of us do without thinking: joining a video meeting with someone we know.

The attackers first compromise legitimate accounts. Then they use those accounts to invite additional victims to meetings.

When the victim joins, they see what appears to be a familiar person on the call.

Sometimes it's a prerecorded video of someone the victim actually knows. Other times, the attackers use AI-generated deepfakes of recognizable people in the cryptocurrency industry.

That establishes trust.

Then comes the technical problem.

The victim is told their microphone isn't working, or that something needs to be fixed before the meeting can continue.

The attackers provide a link or instructions for resolving the issue.

Following those instructions installs malware.

It's an effective sequence because every step seems to explain the next one. The familiar face explains why the meeting is legitimate. The technical problem explains why the victim needs to do something unusual.

And the supposed fix provides the mechanism for compromising the computer.

The DOJ says investigators seized more than 900 webcam videos of victims. Those recordings could be used to impersonate people in subsequent attacks.

That's another disturbing feature of the operation.

The attackers weren't simply stealing money. They were collecting the material needed to impersonate additional people.

And according to the FBI, they've increasingly targeted developers who maintain open-source software.

That creates a different kind of risk.

A developer's computer may contain credentials that provide access to software repositories, package publishing systems, and development infrastructure.

Compromising that developer could create opportunities to distribute malicious software through legitimate channels.

The government also announced court-authorized seizure or restraint of more than $1.2 billion associated with the separate Binance theft. Those figures concern different operations and shouldn't be combined into one loss total.

What interests me most about FaceStealer is that the attack doesn't depend on an especially convincing deepfake.

A familiar person, a believable meeting invitation, and a routine technical problem can be enough.

The practical defense is to treat unexpected installation instructions during video meetings as suspicious, even when the person on screen appears familiar.

If someone says you need to run a command, install an application, or change your security settings to fix your microphone, stop and verify the request through another channel.

The person on the screen may be real.

The meeting may still be a trap.

author: raphael_dkhn
quoted_text:
I’m realizing that some SaaS businesses could make tens of millions in additional revenue by building RL environments for AI labs.

Take a KYB startup. You’ve spent years collecting company records across 150 countries, cleaning them, linking entities, and building APIs on top. 

You have millions of real-world investigations hiding in your database. You can turn them into tasks for AI agents:

“Find the CEO of this company and cite the official document.”

“Identify everyone who indirectly owns more than 25% of this business. Follow the ownership chain across France, Luxembourg, and Singapore.”

“Compare this company’s onboarding application with the registry filings. What’s missing or inconsistent?”

Give the agent tools to search the records and read the documents. Then use your structured data to check the answer: did it find the right entities, calculate the ownership correctly, and cite the right evidence?

Now you have an environment where agents can practice millions of investigations and get a reward when they get them right.

These aren’t just KYB tasks because the same skills matter for due diligence, investing, procurement, compliance, and a ton of other knowledge work.

If you can show that training on your environment makes models better at these tasks, I think you’ll find a buyer for a lot of $$$

Amber Group 否认前高管匿名爆料，称运营一切正常，旗下美股较高点已跌超 85%

11 月 16 日，针对近期社群流传的自称来自 Amber Group 前高管的匿名爆料，Amber Group 今日发布官方声明，称已关注到相关不实指控，并予以坚决否认。公司强调，目前运营一切正常，各项业务均在有序开展。

Amber Group 同时指出，相关内容涉及传播个人身份证件及其他私人信息，严重侵犯个人隐私。目前公司正在保全相关证据，并保留针对诽谤、未经授权披露公司机密信息及侵犯个人隐私等行为采取法律行动、追究相关责任的全部权利。

此次风波也引发市场对其上市主体的关注。据 BIT 股票平台数据显示，Amber Group 核心子公司 Amber International Holding Ltd DRC 美股盘后下跌 3.57%，报 1.89 美元。

公开信息显示，Amber International Holding Limited（品牌名 Amber Premium）于 2025 年 3 月通过合并完成上市，业务涵盖机构级加密金融服务、财富管理、市场准入与执行等。其股价曾于上市当月触及 13 美元，此后持续下跌，较历史高点累计跌幅已超过 85%。

一边是前高管匿名爆料在社群持续发酵，一边是公司公开否认并释放法律追责信号。在争议尚待进一步核实之际，市场对 Amber 的关注已从社群传闻延伸至其上市主体的股价表现。

author: sshxbt
quoted_text:
Amber，又一个爆雷的公司？

昨晚，一份关于 Amber 的 11 页举报信在微信群里疯传。

举报人自称是 Amber 前高管，并声称已经将相关材料提交给中央纪委、香港廉政公署、香港证监会及香港警方。

这份举报信的内容相当劲爆，涉及联合创始人涉嫌挪用客户资金、管理层利益输送、客户入金账户异常，以及 Amber Premium 的 Fixed Earn 产品存在资金运作风险等问题。

需要说明的是，目前这些内容主要来自举报人的单方面陈述，相关指控尚未得到独立证实。笔者结合举报信和 Amber 已披露的公开资料，按照问题的重要性，梳理了以下几个值得关注的疑问。

1、最严重的一项指控，究竟是否真实？

根据举报信，Amber 联合创始人 Tony He 曾挪用千万美元客户资金，在火币进行个人交易，最终导致相关账户被冻结。

如果这一指控属实，问题就不只是内部管理失当，而是涉及客户资产安全的重大事件。

但目前举报信中的说法，还需要交易记录、资金流向、账户归属以及相关调查结果来验证。

Amber 需要回答：客户资金是否曾被挪用于未经授权的个人交易？如果发生过，涉及多少资金？

2、Amber 的创始团队，究竟发生了什么？

根据举报信，Amber 最初有 6 位联合创始人，其中 1 人已经离世，另有 3 人离开，目前只剩下 2 位。

如果举报信所述属实，Amber 的创始团队为何出现如此大规模的人员变动？六位联合创始人目前的实际情况、股权变化，以及核心管理层离职的真实原因是什么？

3、沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？

举报信声称，Amber 股东沈波有约 3 亿美元资金存放在 Amber，并且曾经出售部分股权。

这件事至少需要拆成两个问题：

第一，沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？这笔资金究竟属于个人资产、客户托管资产，还是其他形式的投资或借贷？

第二，如果这笔资金确实存在，沈波是否有权随时提取？如果集中提取，是否会对 Amber 的流动性造成重大影响？

需要强调的是，目前没有公开证据能够证实这 3 亿美元的说法，更不能据此推断沈波提款就会导致 Amber 破产。

4、Amber 是否真的存在爆雷风险？

先看公开财务数据。

截至 2026 年 6 月底，Amber International 的公开财报显示，公司总资产约 2.98 亿美元，总负债约 1.95 亿美元，仍然拥有正的股东权益。但与此同时，2026 年上半年，公司营收同比下降约 28%，并由盈利转为亏损。

另一个值得关注的数据是：截至 2026 年 6 月底，公司的加密资产贷款应收款约为 5,779 万美元，较 2025 年底增长约 37%。

根据财报披露，这些贷款来自集团认购关联方数字资产平台的 Earn 产品，属于无抵押贷款，期限从 2 天到 365 天不等。截至报告期末，公司没有为这部分贷款计提信用损失准备。

这并不能证明客户资金被挪用，也不能直接说明公司存在偿付危机，但它确实引出了一个重要问题：Amber 的资金究竟流向了哪里？相关借款方是谁？如果借款方无法按期偿还，公司是否有足够的流动性应对客户赎回？

5、Amber 是否拥有香港、新加坡和迪拜三地牌照？

这也是一个容易被混淆的问题。三个地区的牌照性质并不相同。

香港：尚未取得正式 VATP 牌照。

Amber 旗下 Whalefin Markets Limited 曾于 2024 年向香港证监会申请虚拟资产交易平台牌照，并在过渡安排下被视为获发牌申请人。

但这不等于正式获牌。2026 年 10 月，Amber International 公告称，Whalefin 将不再推进相关牌照申请，并计划撤回申请；相关收购安排也不再推进。

新加坡：拥有 MPI 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber 旗下的 Sparrow Tech Private Limited，获新加坡金融管理局（MAS）颁发 Major Payment Institution（主要支付机构）牌照，获准提供数字支付代币服务（DPT Services）。

迪拜：拥有 VASP 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber Premium FZE。迪拜虚拟资产监管局（VARA）于 2026 年 4 月 2 日正式向其发放牌照，允许其开展虚拟资产经纪交易、资产管理与投资、借贷服务。不过，牌照限定服务机构投资者和合格投资者。

所以，更准确地说，Amber 已在新加坡和迪拜取得相关数字资产业务牌照，但并未取得香港 VATP 牌照。

一份举报信，不足以证明 Amber 即将爆雷。

但是，这份举报信已经在社交媒体上广泛传播。对于一家管理客户数字资产、提供收益产品的公司而言，Amber 的确需要正面回答几个关键问题：

客户资金是否曾被挪用？客户资产是否实现独立托管？用户购买 Fixed Earn 产品后，钱究竟被拿去做了什么？举报信中提到的关联方资金往来，以及与北京公职人员有关的数百万美元资产，究竟是否属实？

这些问题，Amber 都应该给出明确的解释。

Here's how the pieces fit together. 🧵👇

🔹 1. BitTorrent — Decentralized Content Delivery

BitTorrent's P2P network connects users and peers to distribute content without relying entirely on a single central server.

Its established network supports large-scale file distribution by allowing participating peers to share bandwidth and resources.

🔹 2. BTTInferGrid — Decentralized AI Compute

AI inference requires computing resources, particularly GPUs capable of handling demanding workloads.

BTTInferGrid aims to aggregate distributed computing capacity, coordinate AI inference tasks, and connect resource providers with workloads that need processing.

The opportunity is to make underutilized computing resources available to AI applications through a more flexible infrastructure model.

🔹 3. BTTC — Cross-Chain and Smart Contract Infrastructure

BitTorrent Chain (BTTC) supports cross-chain asset transfers and blockchain applications.

Its infrastructure focuses on interoperability, transaction efficiency, and smart contract execution, helping connect blockchain ecosystems and their applications.

🔹 4. $BTT — The Economic Connection

These infrastructure layers need a way to coordinate resources and incentives.

$BTT is positioned within the ecosystem's economic model for functions such as resource payments, network fees, node incentives, staking, and governance, depending on the specific service and implementation.

The important distinction is that the products provide the infrastructure, while the token supports the economic activity around it.

💡 Why the integration matters

➠ BitTorrent provides the content distribution foundation.

➠ BTTInferGrid extends the ecosystem toward AI inference and decentralized computing.

➠ BTTC provides cross-chain and smart contract infrastructure.

➠ $BTT connects the broader vision through its intended utility across supported services.

The long-term opportunity is to build an integrated Web3 and AI ecosystem where useful services generate real activity and create demand for decentralized resources.

Execution will determine how much value this architecture ultimately delivers.

截至 2026 年 6 月底，Amber International 的公开财报显示，公司总资产约 2.98 亿美元，总负债约 1.95 亿美元，仍然拥有正的股东权益。但与此同时，2026 年上半年，公司营收同比下降约 28%，并由盈利转为亏损。

另一个值得关注的数据是：截至 2026 年 6 月底，公司的加密资产贷款应收款约为 5,779 万美元，较 2025 年底增长约 37%。

根据财报披露，这些贷款来自集团认购关联方数字资产平台的 Earn 产品，属于无抵押贷款，期限从 2 天到 365 天不等。截至报告期末，公司没有为这部分贷款计提信用损失准备。

这并不能证明客户资金被挪用，也不能直接说明公司存在偿付危机，但它确实引出了一个重要问题：Amber 的资金究竟流向了哪里？相关借款方是谁？如果借款方无法按期偿还，公司是否有足够的流动性应对客户赎回？

5、Amber 是否拥有香港、新加坡和迪拜三地牌照？

这也是一个容易被混淆的问题。三个地区的牌照性质并不相同。

香港：尚未取得正式 VATP 牌照。

Amber 旗下 Whalefin Markets Limited 曾于 2024 年向香港证监会申请虚拟资产交易平台牌照，并在过渡安排下被视为获发牌申请人。

但这不等于正式获牌。2026 年 10 月，Amber International 公告称，Whalefin 将不再推进相关牌照申请，并计划撤回申请；相关收购安排也不再推进。

新加坡：拥有 MPI 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber 旗下的 Sparrow Tech Private Limited，获新加坡金融管理局（MAS）颁发 Major Payment Institution（主要支付机构）牌照，获准提供数字支付代币服务（DPT Services）。

迪拜：拥有 VASP 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber Premium FZE。迪拜虚拟资产监管局（VARA）于 2026 年 4 月 2 日正式向其发放牌照，允许其开展虚拟资产经纪交易、资产管理与投资、借贷服务。不过，牌照限定服务机构投资者和合格投资者。

所以，更准确地说，Amber 已在新加坡和迪拜取得相关数字资产业务牌照，但并未取得香港 VATP 牌照。

一份举报信，不足以证明 Amber 即将爆雷。

但是，这份举报信已经在社交媒体上广泛传播。对于一家管理客户数字资产、提供收益产品的公司而言，Amber 的确需要正面回答几个关键问题：

客户资金是否曾被挪用？客户资产是否实现独立托管？用户购买 Fixed Earn 产品后，钱究竟被拿去做了什么？举报信中提到的关联方资金往来，以及与北京公职人员有关的数百万美元资产，究竟是否属实？

这些问题，Amber 都应该给出明确的解释。

text:
补充一下：Hermes 的 x_search 底层模型从 grok-4.20 换到了 grok-4.7，同样四道题又各跑了一遍。

简单题没区别。https://t.co/qOUxrHdUYr 官方那题两个版本找到的是同样 3 条帖子，都在 25 秒左右。

难题 4.7 明显更靠谱：
- ERC-8004 那题，4.20 挑了一堆宣传帖，结论是"没什么技术争议"；4.7 找到了两条真正的质疑，一条说单一注册表有门控问题，一条说声誉记录可以被刷。
- 中文隐私那题，4.20 把一份二手报告里的"漏洞已修复"直接当成事实写了，4.7 引用的是一手讨论，跟 Grok Bot 选中的是同一条。
- 随机字符串那题，4.20 说"X 上不存在"，4.7 说"这次没搜到"。后者才是对的。

代价是慢，难题要 70 到 85 秒，差不多是 4.20 的两倍。

时间窗口的问题还在。我限定 11-08 到 11-15，4.7 照样混进了 11-15、11-16 的帖子。换模型解决不了，基本印证了之前的猜测：问题出在 since/until 这类日期参数上，跟模型关系不大。

所以现在的分工是：
日常查 X 用 x_search（4.7），进推送前按帖子时间再核一遍；
冷门问题、需要深挖的才开 Grok Bot，它准，但一题要几分钟。
author: brucexu_eth
quoted_text:
我想让 Agent 每天从 X 上抓点可信的信息，有好几种方式：Cursor 里的 Grok Bot、Hermes 自带的 x_search + Grok Auth、官方 X API，为了找到最合适的，我就一起测了下：

1. https://t.co/qOUxrHdn8T 官方 11-12 到 11-15 发了什么   from:lifiprotocol since:2026-11-12 until:2026-11-15

2. 一周内 ERC-8004 有哪些具体实现和争议   "ERC-8004" since:2026-11-08 until:2026-11-15

3. 中文圈怎么讨论以太坊隐私   "以太坊" "隐私" lang:zh since:2026-11-08 until:2026-11-15

4. 一个随机字符串，正确答案是查不到

Grok Bot 最准。它一共引用了 11 条帖子，我逐条回查原帖，作者、时间和原文都对得上，也都在窗口内。ERC-8004 那题还翻出了几条有技术含量的讨论。就是慢，一题 18 秒到 7 分钟。

x_search 一题 30 秒左右，快是快，时间却管不住。ERC-8004 引用的 3 条全在窗口外，中文那题 4 条里也有 2 条越界。

官方 X API 不到 1 秒就返回，返回的帖子没有一条越界。但它只给帖子列表，总结还得自己接模型。成本按标价算，四题大概 $0.2，x_search 大概 $0.4。

x_search 底层也是 Grok，为什么差这么多？翻了下调用记录，时间参数确实传了，返回的还是窗口外的帖子。它每次只取最新 10 条，多半被新帖占满了，后来模型干脆自己把 until 往后放了一天。官方 API 用精确到秒的 start_time 和 end_time，没这个问题。所以我猜毛病出在日期型的 since 和 until，跟模型关系不大，这点还没看到官方说明。Grok Bot 会换着条件搜很多轮，中间还回查单条帖子，最后交出来的就干净很多。

现在打算定时推送走官方 API，抓下来再丢给模型总结。冷门问题偶尔开 Grok Bot 深挖。x_search 只拿来找线索，进推送前按帖子时间再核一遍。

当然最好还是把 Hermes Agent 链接上 Grok Bot，跟 X 相关的让它去调用 Grok Bot 完成。

Traditional APIs rent you a pipe. Pocket gives you the network. 

With Alchemy, Infura or QuickNode you get an endpoint, a dashboard and a monthly bill that grows with your traffic. 

With Pocket you stake POKT once as an application, get matched with independent suppliers every single session, and pay per relay through an on-chain burn. 

No single operator owns your traffic. No rate plan caps what you can grow into. Any service can be listed permissionlessly, and anyone can become a supplier. 

The result is infrastructure you participate in, not infrastructure you rent. 

Renting works. Owning a real stake in the network you actually use every day works better.

If you're using the @boros_fi Arbitrage Terminal, this is important.

Your Gate CrossEx API key will expire every 90 days if you don't have an IP address bound to it.

That means if you set up your terminal around the same time as me, yours might be expiring right about now.

Updating it takes just ~2 minutes.

Here's how.

First, don't worry.

If your API key expires or gets disabled, your open positions, hedges and funds won't automatically be affected.

Your positions remain open, and your funds stay where they are.

You simply lose the connection between the terminal and Gate until you restore or replace your API key.

Why does this happen?

Gate has a rule that APIv4 keys without an IP address bound to them are only valid for 90 days.

After that, they're automatically disabled.

If you don't have a fixed IP address, you'll need to update your API key every 90 days.

How to fix it (takes ~2 minutes)

1. Log in to @Gate
2. Click your profile picture (top right) -> API Management
3. Click Create API Key
4. Choose Trading Account
5. Enable Cross-Exchange -> set it to Read and Write
6. Choose "Later" under IP Permissions if you don't have a static IP
7. Submit

You'll now see your new API Key and API Secret.

Copy the Secret immediately, as it's only shown once.

Then in the Boros Arbitrage Terminal:

1. Settings (top right)
2. Go to Gate API key
3. Add your new API Key + API Secret
4. Click Replace Credentials to confirm

Done bros.

The terminal reconnects, and you're back to earning some of the highest yields in our magic internet market.

text:
警惕假钱包骗局！

前天有个人私信求助我，说他在Trust Wallet的钱取不出来了，我第一反应是他下载到假钱包了。
但从截图来看，这个App在手机应用商店里确实显示的是下载量几十万+的Trust Wallet。

我看了更多截图，有几点非常可疑：

疑点一：这个App里的AAve显示，存USDC的年化收益是15%+。他存钱进去，余额显示是正常的，但是从链上的记录看，USDC根本没和Aave产生过交互，一存进去就立马被转走了，应该是App内置的假协议。
当他想解质押时，这个假的Aave还提示：流动性硬性锁定，60天后才能释放。

疑点二：我看了他的聊天记录，假客服一直在引导他继续往假钱包里充值。
先是诱导他在11月20日之前继续充值，达到两万U的门槛，才能继续领取收益。
当他想放弃这些收益、取回本金时，客服甚至“威胁”他说，不增加与本金等额的流动性，已经存入的本金将被“罚没”？？

我让他从官网进去，点击下载链接，跳转到手机应用商店后，显示的是“打开”，而不是“下载”。
再进一步询问，他原来是先在浏览器搜索Trust wallet，点击了某个链接后才跳转到应用商店的。
骗子通过钓鱼链接，让用户安装了一个和Trust Wallet的App ID相同，但签名不同的另外一个App。所以从应用商店里看，这个假App就像真App一样。

text:
Speaking of stop losses, some people have been asking me to share related books and videos. I haven't organized them yet, so here are the absolute basics. 

First, for stop losses, you'd better have a major premise, which is defining your maximum loss per trade and maximum daily loss. There is a tool called a Risk Manager.

There are many types of stop losses. The most common ones are price and structure stops, such as trendlines, swing highs and lows, and market structure shifts, as well as capital and drawdown stops (a fixed dollar amount per trade such as ≤ $500, a fixed equity percentage such as risking ≤ 1% of total capital per trade, and a total account drawdown percentage).

Others include volatility stops (ATR multiple stops such as entry price ± 1.5×ATR, Bollinger Band and VWAP standard deviations such as ±2σ, and options implied volatility (IV) expected moves), time stops (closing the position if price fails to clear the cost basis after N bars, closing before the end of a specific session such as the first 30 minutes of the US market open, and closing options early to avoid Theta decay), order flow scalping stops (absorption failure, liquidity pulls, and extreme Delta divergence), and trailing stops (where the stop line moves in the same direction as unrealized profits and locks in gains against reversals, which can be divided into fixed point trailing, percentage trailing, and volatility based trailing such as the Chandelier Exit, which is the highest high minus N times ATR).

Also, a stop loss doesn't necessarily mean closing the entire position. Scaling out is also a form of stop loss. Most commonly, you size your position based on a pattern, so conversely, if the pattern you are trading deteriorates and no longer matches your expectations, you can scale down your position.

Also, many trading platforms or custom plugins now feature a Risk Manager, which you can use as a reference to design your own risk management: max daily loss limit, max daily profit lock, account equity trailing drawdown, max position size limit, max order size per trade, max daily trade count, max consecutive losing trades, no opening positions without a stop loss along with restricting the user from manually canceling stop orders or dragging stops significantly wider into a loss, ATR dynamic position size reduction, order book depth and spread auto circuit breakers, and automatically switching to reduce only mode or flattening all positions at T minus 5 minutes before high impact news events. 

In reality, the risk management we normally use is just a behavioral guardrail. The biggest difference between institutions and retail traders is that institutional risk management goes beyond behavioral guardrails into strategy level hedging. I won't get into the complex institutional strategy side since it's unnecessary for regular trading, though you can try hedging with 0DTE options or relative strength hedging.

text:
The articles backtracked from their original incendiary, and now clearly false, claims to something more like "Jensen did lawful things that powerful people didn't like". It still appears the original claims came from a single competing Big Tech lobbyist.

The reporting successfully disrupted corporate governance processes, with a running cost of $1.8 trillion in losses to American pension funds and shareholders.

Here's what I fear is being lost in these articles: The proper interface between government and private citizens and their corporations is rule of law. Laws are passed, and if wrongdoing as alleged, then there's due process: an investigation followed by facts and evidence presented in open court. Due process should happen here: let the facts come out whole, and not as a trickle of dubious claims.

Press takedowns full of sketchily sourced claims and backtracking narratives are not the way. It's what we see outside of the free world, and is no model for The United States of America.

In particular, if the Jensen takedown succeeds on the basis of these journalistic failings, which is not by any means certain as Sam Altman's case shows, then it foreshadows an economically and institutionally ruinous new playbook to be adopted with no end in sight.

Imagine a weekly stream of takedowns emerging from opportunistic alignments between corporate lobbyists and political interests which, given the new partisan split between the executive and legislative branches, will attack in all directions, undermining not only the US economy but American leadership in the world.

I hope cooler heads prevail this coming week as they did not on Thursday November 12. And I urge anyone who happened to oppose Jensen, open models, and the underlying trade policies in question, to recognize that this isn't a win for "team regulation". It's a change in the game from a transparent rules-based one to a sinister new form centered around politicans and lobbyists.

text:
如果你本来就打算在某个低价位买BTC，那么用@okxchinese 的双币赢提前布局，加上相应的年化收益，就很香。

比如，$60K这一挡，年化26.61%，40天实际收益 2.92%，投10,000 USDT，期间能拿292USDT利息。

到期价BTC价格不低于$60K，拿回本金加利息，即10,292 USDT；低于$60K，就按$60K换成BTC，加上利息一共约0.1715枚，实际买入成本$58,300。

用双币赢和直接挂限价单相比，有3点优势：

1、等待也有收益； 没抄到底，能拿到利息，限价单没成交就什么都没有。

2、成本更低； 换成BTC时利息一起折算进去，实际买入价低于目标价。

3、没有爆仓风险。 全额USDT担保，不加杠杆，且现在这种高波动行情，期权费高，收益也更好。

但也有几个关键风险，需要事先考虑清楚：

1、双币赢只看到期那一刻的结算价，如果中途插针到 $55K又拉了回来，你没接到货。

2、如果价格跌穿，比如到期价跌到$50K，你还是要按 $60K接；此时账面直接浮亏。

3、资金被锁定，中途不能提前赎回。如行情变了（比如又涨上去）你无法即时调整仓位。

所以，个人举得比较合适的用法是：

把目标价放在自己认定的"愿意长期持有"的区间。并可以把资金分成几份，分散到不同的价位和到期日，这样可以分批接货，也能避开单一结算时点的运气成分。

最终被换成BTC是你想要的结果，不是损失。如果你心理上接受不了按目标价接货，那就不要买。

text:
Nice one, some quick thoughts :)

- I don’t think pqai27 is “rushing” nor that it is done for memetic benefits, though there are such benefits undeniably. While there are ofc discussions to have on the how and some who disagree with the feasibility, many see the delivery in ‘27 as doable. At least more than necessary to believe that the plan is not crazy, though ambitious. I believe your post underrates the current progress toward freezing signature schemes, and overrates how committal the decision is.
- We are not *not* shipping user-friendly features. Frames is very likely on the path, and is one of the most consequential user-facing upgrades of the last five years. With PQ as a motivation to make users migrate, there is a huge opportunity to deliver even more value there.
- Perhaps the most potent argument for me: not addressing the PQ threat with urgency could mean we still don’t get user-facing features by 2028. The Damocles sword, as @casparschwa puts it, of new results and uncertainty is imo the riskiest part of not addressing the threat head-on, and definitively circumvent the thrash of governance in the time of known unknowns. I would bet that the lift from a truly all-hands Manhattan project would do more for core development and execution than any other vehicle. There is also the off chance (i’m bullish, but I recognise that i am still an outlier here, though in good company already) that we end up shipping pq-decoupled consensus in 2027. This would mean order of magnitude faster finality and a clear shot towards shorter slots soon after. Even if not, I do not see a better path to landing at the end of 2028 with everyone checked off from our bucket list: pq, privacy, fast ethereum, focil and scale. Living in the in-between until then is to me a recipe for failure.

AI labs keep bragging about benchmark scores. Most of those tests are already beaten.

Ethan Mollick tracked 173 benchmarks the labs have cited since 2023. 63% are now "saturated," meaning top models score so high the test can't tell them apart anymore. It's happening faster every year.

So the scores in the next launch post won't tell you much. Your own test will.

Build one in 15 minutes:
1. Write down 10 real tasks from your work (an email, a spreadsheet fix, a summary)
2. Save the exact prompt and what a great answer looks like
3. When a new model drops, run all 10 and score each one from 1 to 5
4. Keep the sheet. Within a month you'll know which model is best for your work

text:
Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.

大斜率理论为什么不鼓励大家做vla/wam. 我要把这件事情说的明白一点. 首先很多事情有一个客观标准是需要有生产实践的. 接下来我说的词有reference，大家就别说是我臆测的了哈:

张小珺采访姚顺宇大家还记得吗? 姚说，“人这一辈子也没有多长，为什么要把自己的时间浪费在伺候老登身上. 当这个领域没有实践，没有客观标准的时候，肯定不止有一套自洽的框架出现，谁做的好或者不好就取决于老登的判断。”

姚花9年离开物理，我花2年看明白具身和广泛的小圈子视觉领域。这是一个好问题，但是这是一个没有投入生产实践的领域。是demo五花八门仿真各种hack的领域，是网红领域。这个领域拿来主义很多，原创的有但是很难出圈，最后的“好工作”往往都是姚口中的老登和他们扶持的天才小登们垄断话语权和宣发产生的，因为他不像投入实践的llm，好不好大家都知道。

如果你不是老登们的天才小登，但是真想解决机器人问题，投身预训练实践就是斜率最高的事情，你必须是降临派，没有任何转圜的余地。从领域上来讲，这是你把它投入生产实践斜率最高的路线，最正本清源的方式。从你个人利益来讲，投入eai in llm pretraining，你是somebody，做vla/wam toy，上述现状决定你是no body. 

我至今不会忘记一位做某视觉隐空间领域的朋友说为什么做的很好却得不到关注，可能人家某热力图还有ai水印标识都关注很高。那时我就想，如果我可以加入 general pretraining，我一定要赢下所有。如今next transformer就在眼前，我必须考虑这是否是我此生仅有的机会.

text:
In close to a year the RWA perpetual market went from negligible to billions in open interest. Last week @Lingersj joined @DAF_Global to discuss that growth. 

The key takeaways? RWA perps are growing faster than the infrastructure, disclosure and education around them. The winners will pair DeFi’s flexibility with real security spend, transparent funding and credible custody.
author: DWFLabs

text:
The scale: ~ 680B in RWA perp volume in Oct 2026 vs  ~ 320B for all of 2025. The CFTC has also authorized single-stock perps on US exchanges for the first time. Growth now spans CeFi, DeFi and traditional venues.

Demand is mostly retail: cross-border access, weekend trading, pre-IPO names like SpaceX and Anthropic, and niche markets like Korean AI and memory chip stocks. Institutions are showing up for the spread on retail order flow, not just liquidity.

The top risk is cybersecurity. Even Binance and Bybit still get hacked, and lean DEX teams are more exposed.
Most DeFi and lending platforms spend under 2% on security. One proposed bar: no disclosure of at least 10% security spend, no trading.

Settlement risk is real too. There’s no regulated central clearinghouse on-chain, so counterparty default is a live concern. Transfers are also instant and irreversible, with no TradFi-style speed bumps. Third-party off-exchange custody is the mitigation to watch.

Funding rates are opaque. Methodology varies and can diverge 5-10% annually across platforms. Retail can drain a balance through an open position without noticing. A 10% funding drag makes a perp very different from holding the stock.

Pre-IPO perps have a structural problem. Almost no organic short demand. Funding rates as high as 100% annualized are needed to attract shorts. It’s largely unsolved.

Where will open interest live in two years? On-chain and offshore CEXs. Regulated US venues are held back by 6x leverage caps and limited collateral and cross-margining. Asia, especially Korea, drives organic demand. China reopening would be a step-change.

On institutions: macro funds use perps as price signals for weekend and overnight risk. Prime brokers intermediate via ISDA frameworks and hedge on-chain. Family offices are increasingly active. Funding of 10-40% annualized is drawing carry and arb trades.

The counterpoint: DeFi’s habit of compressing margins to zero can hurt platform resilience. Bybit and Binance weathered their hacks partly thanks to profitability cushions.

LOB-STER DE-VO 🎥 — made with DEVO, a hybrid artwork and song, the centrepiece of Simon de Pury's first Decentraland auction. Price Unknown 

Raft of the Lobster 🎥 — his take on Géricault's Raft of the Medusa, first shown in Lobsteropolis. Sold for 2.72 ETH.

Guggenheim Lobster 🎥 — the lobster smashing through the Guggenheim in New York. Price Unknown 

Hockney and the Lobster (animated) — his entry in Artsy and Verisart's '22 for 2022.' Sold for 1.1 ETH. 

The Lobstars (Genesis) — One physical oil painting (about 150 × 150 cm) with one twinned NFT of it. Same artwork, two forms — the painting on the wall, the NFT onchain, Sold for £47,750 ($63,000), every penny went to lobster research at St Abbs Marine Station.
