text:
我用 AI 协同办公很久了，这次做了一个测试，一个项目由三个 AI 不同的接手，最后拿到我来对比到手的结果：

1. ChatGPT ，工作的态度特别好，绝对是班里的学习委员，学校里的学生会主席，但交付能力一塌糊涂，小的页面没问题，大型程序最会在关键的最后一步出问题，而且是无解的那种问题。

ChatGPT 最大的缺点就是不会绕弯，一条路走到黑，如果走不动了也不和你说，也不和别的 AI 沟通，直接就停工了，所以对我来说 ChatGPT 最适合的就是基础构架。

一个大型的云端任务，就一个任务，24小时能烧掉整整一周的 Ultra 的额度。

2. Grok，Grok Bot 是那种默默无闻的工作，能明显看到在特别努力学习的学渣，虽然很努力了，而且交付能力也不错，但就是 100 分的题，经常给出 30 分的答案，我知道很多小伙伴习惯用 BOT，但 BOT 有个天坑。

就是在 BOT 的工作里，是不能选择工作强度的，说人话就是 Grok 里有五种强度，而 BOT 并不是任意一种，对于 BOT 来说就是一个秘书，所以越小的事情交付的越好，准确率越高，就是因为“智商”有限。

而上了强度的 Grok 我还没来得及测试，我就把一周的额度都用完了，所以下期我会主要测试一下 Grok ，而不是 Grok BOT ，而且我也奉劝做大型开发的小伙伴，不要用 BOT ，就是天坑。

3. Claude，其实 Fable 5.1 中等给我的感觉很一般，就是消耗非常大，体感应该是比最高的等级的 ChatGPT 快三倍，比 Gork BOT 快两倍的消耗，交付能力中规中矩，非常适合做结尾，也就是帮 ChatGPT 和 Grok BOT 擦屁股。

升级到 Fable 5.2 以后我开始用高级了，绝对是学霸，不声不响的学霸，什么垃圾作业到了 Claude 哪里几乎都能解出来，就是费钱，非常，非常的费钱。

但 Claude 不是没有问题，相比 ChatGPT 和 Grok 的全面来说，Claude 在图画绘制方面非常的差，做图片加工是可以的，但独立生成图片不行，必须要配合使用才可以。

4. Muse，一言难尽，对我来说 Muse 最大的缺点就是需要人的辅助，对于权限非常的小心，就像是班里的非常胆小的小姑娘，可能学习能力还行，但就是胆子特别小，什么事情都要让你做决定。最崩溃的是每次连接 Github 都需要我同意一次。

每一次写入都需要点同意，不能跳过，所以 Muse 在本地运作也许可以，但频繁修改 Github 的事情绝对不能交给她做。

另外 Muse 的远程协助功能到是有意思，可以通过邮件和 Github 来交接任务，所以本质上来说是作为协作最好的一份子，因为非常简单，设置了 Muse 的邮箱直接通过邮件发命令就行，Muse 也会把写好的邮件回来，但需要经常删，而且不能用自己常用邮箱，否则一直都是提醒。

从我目前的工作情况来看，ChatGPT 搭建基础，Gork 和 Muse 做实现层的工作，Claude 作为验收，监管和收尾，是不错的组合。

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
ChatGPT + Grok + Claude 三 AI 协作代码公布

废话就不多说了，我应该是较早的在 X 上公布用多 AI 协作的，测试了也有一个月了，现在代码比较稳定了，可以让 三个 AI 有效的协同工作了，所以就把代码都公布出来。

Github 地址：https://t.co/9C3xTXAnBb

希望大家在 Fork 的同时可以随手点颗星🌟

需要注意的是：

1. 这套方案在本机调度，模型推理还是由各家自己的服务完成。需要准备 Codex，以及 Grok Build、Claude Code 的命令行客户端（CLI）。不知道怎么装的小伙伴没关系，可以把仓库链接交给自己的 Codex，让它按配置指南协助安装和检查，登录和授权由你本人完成。

2. 这套代码里，三个 AI 的小队长是 Codex，负责处理任务、分工、检查结果和交付，Claude 和 Grok 分别参与分析和复核。当前公开版围绕 Codex 主控设计，想让其他 AI 当队长还需要另外适配。

3. 小伙伴都喜欢用 BOT 了，这挺好的，但 BOT 直接是很难直接通话的，不是说不行，而是代价很高，比如我 ChatGPT 的 BOT 已经用了一个月了，堆积的内容太多了，如果用外部的 BOT 去访问，就要拉所有内容，Grok 的统计每一次交互需要 数百万的 Token 。

所以最好的方法就是在 ChatGPT 和 Grok 两者 BOT 的云电脑上登录对方的页面，比如在 ChatGPT BOT 的电脑中登录 Grok ，以及在 Grok BOT 的电脑中登录 ChatGPT 。

这样的方式就可以非要有效的让两者互相联系，并且互相传文件都可以。

4. 因为是通过 CLI 的命令执行的，所以每个 AI 都有一定的限制，如果同时开多个任务的话，可能协助执行的另外两个 AI 会超时，这是在所难免的。

5. 目前我绑定的系统中 Grok 配置的是 grok-4.7，推理强度是 xhigh ，Claude 配置的是 Fable-5.1，推理强度是 medium 。这是可以换的，如果觉得有问题可以自己和 AI 对话更换就行了。

6. 公开版通过 MCP 把协作工具接入 Codex，安装后服务名称以 ai_team_ 开头，后面带一个随机编号。公开版提供了全局协作规则模板，可以按你的选择合并到现有规则，让之后的聊天在具备工具和权限时尝试协作。不想用了，可以停用对应连接。

7. 这一套完成以后我就开始准备接入 Muse ，很多小伙伴在问我如何接入了，我已经开始工作了，而且 Muse 也是有 BOT 的，操作更简单一些。

8. 多 AI 协作相信我，非常非常非常有用，尤其在大项目的时候，AI 经常会跑偏，这时候就需要提醒 AI 回到正确的路上，而且在幻觉这方面，起码我还没有见到同一个文件两个不同 AI 都会幻觉的可能，尤其是我还配置了三个，但也因为多 AI 协作，所以任务的执行会更慢一些，不过准确率和成功率不可同日而语。

9. 你们都知道怎么联系我，任何需要维护的或者是添加一些新功能，可以和我说。AI 协同工作可能才是最大化解放人的可能。

一张照片还没发到网上，
监管已经先开出了罚单。

意大利数据保护局周六说，
Meta 被罚 8.05 亿欧元，大约 8.87 亿美元。
原因是 Facebook 的一个建议功能，
在用户没被充分告知、也没有单独同意的情况下，
就访问了 Android 手机里的照片和视频。
当局说，意大利大约有 2000 万 Android 用户受影响。
这笔罚款大约相当于该公司全球营收的 0.47%。

Meta 被要求在 60 天内，把这个功能默认关掉，
并单独征求同意。
公司发言人说会上诉，认为罚单“不成比例”，
并称用户必须先在设备上给权限，功能才能运行，也可以随时改。

当局还特意写了一句：
这轮调查从 2025 年就开始，
并没有覆盖这些内容有没有被拿去训练 AI。
Meta 否认有这种做法。
2026 年新上线的云端图库处理功能，当局留了后手，以后再查。

Pre Market Thoughts - 16 Nov 26

Bloody day in Asia trading as KOSPI, TAIEX and NKY collectively puked exposure. TAIEX was the hardest hit, especially so when people are repricing the entire semis supply chain given the uncertainty now with the departure of Jensen from NVDA.

Memory names in Korea were punished with both Hynix and Samsung dropping 7 and 4.5% respectively. This caught on the US names with MU and SNDK both down 3-4% each.

Logically, i would peg the chances of Jensen's return at close to zero. However, seeing the immense support behind Jensen as well as the structural reality of the entire AI supply chain - there is a possibility that the China hawks who were reportedly behind his oust to realize that they bit off more than they could chew. The situation remains very fluid and i dont think there is any edge in speculation.

On a larger geopolitical front, with RASA set to pass - it becomes a question mark for all the DCs built in SEA especially Malaysia. There are many chinese off takers - what becomes of those deals?

The calendar this week is also quite packed. On tuesday we have NVDA earnings. I would argue that there is currently more downside convexity going into NVDA earnings in the current set up. Even if NVDA reports good numbers, investors will overlook that and demand for clarity on other issues. However, if NVDA reports bad numbers - it would be pretty bad.... Meanwhile Kress has a difficult task ahead of her.

ANT IPO starts trading on thursday. Given the oversubscription, there will be cash released back into the ecosystem. However, there are many AI investors who could only buy semis to participate in the AI meta. Yet now, there is a pure play stock that they could buy instead. I would not be surprised if semis capital rotate into $ANT.

Crypto has stem the bleed for now in $BTC. However, many people are still perplexed over the selling that ensued over the last 10 days that shaved off 20% off the market cap in BTC. There are also rumours about quantum and about breaking the security of old coins. I affirm the cautious stance once again on crypto. 

Good luck!

quoted_text:
I've been combing forensically through the media reporting on the Jensen Huang debacle, and I'm shocked.

- New York Times directly claimed at least 11 times that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.
- The Times is walking this claim back after U.S. intelligence would not corroborate it.
- If real, whoever handed over the alleged intelligence to the Times potentially violated the Espionage Act, unless authorized to do so.
- If Trump authorized it, why did he?
- If Trump did not authorize it, why did the official violate the Espionage Act -- potentially prosecutable as a felony?
- Who was the official who leaked the classified intelligence?
- Was it Rubio, who authored the memo on the original CIA brief, or was it someone else?
- Jensen Huang's apology for being unfaithful does not name Alice Huang, or anyone else.
- The media's characterization of Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang as being romantic is also based on anonymous intelligence, but is not established as fact.
- Wall Street Journal fabricated a claim that Singapore investigated Alice Huang for espionage, when Singapore actually investigated her for false claims; WSJ still has not retracted its false reporting.

Thus:

- Jensen Huang may have had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, or he may not have.
- Alice Huang may be a Chinese intelligence asset, or she may not have been.
- According to third-hand accounts of the intelligence briefs, the U.S. government suspected that Alice Huang may be a Chinese asset for well more than a year.
- Yet, according to Trump's account, Jensen Huang had never been informed.
- Jensen Huang, therefore, is apparently being held accountable for an extramarital affair that he may not have had, with a woman who may not have been an intelligence asset, who he had never been told was or was not such an asset.
- This is nonsensical. How, after all, can he be held accountable for an affair with a Chinese intelligence asset (who might not actually be a Chinese intelligence asset) that the U.S. government knew about -- but did not warn him about?
- Is not the accountable party the U.S. government official who failed to warn him?

Or is he being held accountable for that affair?

- Remember, Jensen Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful, but not with whom.
- Is he being held accountable for another affair?
- Unnamed sources also mention an affair with a direct subordinate Kimberly Powell.
- This affair is again unconfirmed.
- A romantic relationship with a subordinate violates company policy.
- But the board actually has discretion about how to handle this. They could slap him on the wrist, impose some disciplinary regime, therapy, etc.
- But they didn't. So to say that they were obligated to remove him is not correct.
- We know that some members of the board were helicoptered in from Wall Street just 6 months before the ouster.
- What role did they play?
- Was the takeover by the board being planned far in advance of the reporting?

So they chose to remove him. Or did they?

- Jensen Huang resigned.
- This is not the same as the resignation being voluntary.
- What are the circumstances of his resignation?
- Was he forced to resign, or did he do so from exhaustion, or to protect his company?
- Furthermore, what was the flash point? Was it for the extramarital affair that may not have been one, with the Chinese intelligence asset, who may have not been an asset, that U.S. intelligence knew about but did not warn him about? Or was it about the affair with the subordinate that the board had discretion over?
- We do not know the answers to any of these questions.

- Unnamed sources, reported by Reuters, implicated a second Nvidia employee extramarital, also unconfirmed.
- Which affairs are real? Which are mere hearsay?
- How did this play into deliberations?

- The media continues unabated character attacks on Jensen Huang.
- Yet we also know that, for all the dirt that they try to dig up, most of it has remarkably little substance.
- Alice Huang may have smuggled some state-of-the-art (banned) chips into China.
- What did Jensen Huang know about this? We don't know that yet.
- If these chips were smuggled, objectively, these chips are still a drop in the bucket compared to the overwhelming compute advantage that the United States has over China.

Overall, the story is actually extremely thin, and we know remarkably less than the media implies.

And, in my opinion, that is the story itself: a full-on media assault on Jensen Huang in the court of public opinion, on the basis of remarkably little substance.

This reveals more about the media than it does about Jensen Huang. They want him gone.

But why? And how does this relate to the motives of the U.S. government official who leaked the Rubio memo about Alice Huang?

We also know:

One of the first reporters involved at the FT says that she was tipped off to this story by someone in the tech industry.

We have many more questions than answers.

Personally, and my opinion at this point is clearly partisan, but I smell a room full of rats.

Nodar admitted he fumbled some obligations for these older projects, mostly bc he viewed them as concluded or failed experiments / or shipped alternative solutions from what he stated.

When a project fails, Nodar has no issues just moving on to a new idea.

There are people who are frustrated they invested in his old projects and after they failed Nodar moved on. When I spoke to these ppl that seemed to be their main gripe.

I would imagine if hookr fails it will be no different. That doesn’t mean any outstanding obligations would cease to matter ofc, and IMO Nodar should absolutely address any unmet obligations for past projects, but that's up to him.

We’ve identified over 100 token creations associated with Nodar across multiple wallets.

Many of these have little to no observed activity. Many are explicitly labeled “test,” “canary,” etc. He has also posted a multitude of times about his testing on both x and farcaster, though those posts weren’t always advance warnings for each token.

Of these tokens, I’ve verified direct personal promotion for only a handful on X/Farcaster so far.

He does seem reckless in the sense that he operates like a 2020 DeFi summer dev. Lot of experiments and a lot of test in prod situations.

Sometimes when he has an idea, he seems to rush to build the branding and social infra behind the idea before thinking about building out the idea itself.  The vast majority of times, his ideas don't move beyond this phase.

As it pertains to hookr, I don’t think anyone was surprised to hear adoption is minimal. The metrics are public. In my view, it’s basically a meme token at this point.

Nodar is definitely a degen on the spectrum of devs.  He tests in prod, ships quickly, knows how to rally support and attention and does so frequently.  

In many ways, he's the exact guy degens want at the helm of something they hold.  On chain degens love supporting a guy who can / will pump their bag.

It's no coincidence that hookr has been one of the strongest shitcoins on robinhood chain.  Nodar did that for us.

text:
黄仁勋倒下，最有理由开香槟的，可能不是 AMD，而是 Anthropic 和 OpenAI。

《金融时报》最新报道指出，黄仁勋被迫辞去英伟达 CEO 职务，对全球开放模型生态构成重大打击，而最大的受益者恰恰是 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 这样的闭源模型巨头。

很多人可能低估了黄仁勋在这场路线之争中的分量。

在他的主导下，英伟达不仅开发 Nemotron 开放权重模型，还投资了 Reflection AI、Thinking Machines Lab，并推动收购 Hugging Face。后者价值约 129 亿美元的交易，如今能否顺利完成也成了未知数。

黄仁勋当然不是单纯出于理想主义。

英伟达的商业逻辑很简单：模型越开放，能够训练、部署和定制 AI 的企业就越多，需要购买 GPU 的客户也就越多。

而 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的商业利益恰恰不同。它们更希望通过领先的专有模型、API 和平台，掌握 AI 能力的分发权。尤其是 Anthropic，还长期以安全为理由，主张对先进模型实施更严格的限制。

一边希望全世界都有能力自己造 AI，一边希望全世界通过自己的接口使用 AI。

这不只是开源与闭源的技术路线之争，更是一场关于未来 AI 权力究竟应该分散还是集中的利益博弈。

最讽刺的是，那些天天警告人类可能失去对 AI 控制权的公司，恰恰也在推动 AI 的控制权进一步集中到少数公司手里。

黄仁勋的离开，并不意味着开源模型会消失。但美国 AI 产业失去了一个有资金、有产业影响力、也愿意公开反对限制开放模型的重量级人物。

当开放模型最大的金主退出牌桌，闭源巨头甚至不需要赢得技术竞争，就可能在商业和政治上获得更大的话语权。

真正值得警惕的，不是某个模型公司最终赢了，而是未来人们可能连选择其他模型的权利，都要由少数巨头来决定。

text:
黄仁勋刚被赶出英伟达，美国政府却准备把英伟达封为「国家冠军」。华盛顿这出戏，越来越有意思了。

据《华尔街日报》独家报道，特朗普政府计划将超过 24 家美国 AI 企业列为「国家冠军」（National Champions），首批名单包括英伟达、亚马逊、微软、OpenAI 和 Anthropic。

这可不只是发个奖状。

按照目前披露的计划，入选企业有望获得更快的芯片及技术出口许可、政府对海外业务的支持，以及联邦融资渠道。美国政府还希望把芯片、AI 模型及其他技术打包，向外国政府和企业推销。

换句话说，美国政府准备亲自下场，给硅谷当全球销售总监。

而这项计划最耐人寻味的地方，是它宣布的时机。

过去两周，黄仁勋遭遇了近乎全方位的政治围攻。国家安全、对华芯片出口、情报风险，成了华盛顿攻击英伟达的关键词。黄仁勋甚至因此离开了自己创立的公司。

可如今，同一个美国政府，又准备把英伟达推到国家 AI 出海战略的重要位置。

这恰恰暴露了美国 AI 政策最深刻的矛盾：国家安全要求限制技术流动，国家竞争力却要求美国技术占领全世界。

更有意思的是，英伟达和 Anthropic 竟然出现在同一份名单里。

前者长期主张让美国芯片在全球市场保持竞争力，后者则积极推动更严格的对华先进芯片限制。两家公司在华盛顿争论得不可开交，到了海外市场，却又要被美国政府装进同一个技术出口套餐。

在国内，它们是政策路线的对手；到了国外，它们又成了美国国家利益的共同载体。

说到底，华盛顿真正想要的，从来不只是技术安全，而是技术霸权：既要限制中国获得美国最先进的技术，又要让其他国家尽可能购买美国的整套 AI 基础设施。

而在这套战略里，英伟达依然不可替代。

美国政治精英或许可以抛弃黄仁勋，但美国的 AI 国家战略，暂时还离不开他打造的商业帝国。

至于这场风波究竟是在保护美国的国家安全，还是正在伤害美国自己的国家竞争力，恐怕值得华盛顿认真想想。

text:
Vitalik看好EIP-8288下的leanPCS方案，称可更快落地通用证明

Vitalik Buterin发文称，过去几周他对leanPCS的态度已转为完全看好。leanPCS是围绕以太坊提案EIP-8288的三种方案之一。

该提案由他与Thomas Coratger提出，目前仍是草案，设想在内存池中聚合签名和STARK证明，区块里只放一个聚合证明。

他称，leanSPHINCS只支持一种抗量子签名；leanSTARK通用性最强，但需先统一用户的编程语言（指令集），耗时较长；leanPCS同样通用，有望更快落地，指令集敲定后再加入leanSTARK。
author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.

如何判断比特币是否已经见底？

虽然此前我给出了5万–5.5万美元的底部区间，但在具体操作上，我还会结合技术信号，判断市场是否真正出现了阶段性底部。

回顾比特币2月和6月的两次阶段性底部，可以总结出两个值得重点关注的见底信号。

1. 恐慌抛售与二次测试

从量价关系来看，2月5日和6月5日都出现了明显的恐慌性抛售，表现为价格大幅下跌，同时成交量显著放大。

这意味着市场出现了大规模的筹码交换，主力开始在低位承接恐慌性抛盘。

恐慌抛售出现后，市场通常还会经历二次测试。二次测试不一定要守住前低：

例如，2月24日的二次测试最低跌至62500美元，没有跌破2月6日的60000美元低点。

而6月末的二次测试最低跌至57800美元，轻微跌破了6月5日的59130美元低点。

因此，判断二次测试是否成功，不能只看有没有跌破前低，更重要的是观察成交量是否明显萎缩、下跌幅度是否收窄，以及价格向下推进的力度是否减弱。

如果恐慌抛售后出现了成功的二次测试，通常意味着卖压已经明显减弱，是判断阶段性底部的重要信号。

2. RSI极低值

RSI极低值意味着市场出现了严重超卖，也可以作为判断阶段性底部的辅助信号。

回顾前两次底部，2月5日和6月5日的日线RSI都曾接近15，而当周的周线RSI也都降至30附近。

目前这轮下跌已经持续了一个多月，但还没有出现恐慌抛售，RSI也没有出现类似的极端超卖信号。

目前日线RSI最低达到19，周线RSI最低达到38。虽然已经处于相对低位，但与前两次阶段性底部相比，超卖程度仍然不够极端。

综合来看，我认为比特币目前还缺少足够明确的底部信号。

接下来重点观察两个方面：

一是是否出现放量恐慌抛售，以及后续卖压明显减弱的二次测试；

二是日线和周线RSI是否进一步进入极端超卖区域。

等这两个方面都出现明确信号，我才会开始建仓。

上述分析仅供参考，不作为投资建议！

quoted_text:
比特币跌破关键趋势线，抄底机会在哪里？

比特币还是没有经受住MSTR利空的考验，在MSCI决定剔除MSTR后，比特币跌破反弹趋势线，开始加速下跌。

这意味着7月以来的反弹行情已经结束了，再次进入了下跌趋势，在跌破反弹趋势线后我的合约多单止损了。

过去几个月，我的观点一直是新一轮牛市还没有启动，比特币7月以来的上涨属于反弹行情。

不过，10月份美股回调时，比特币表现得相对坚挺。甚至在11月5日美股暴跌时，比特币都没有有效跌破74968美元的关键支撑位。

这让我一度认为，比特币只是在反弹过程中的正常回调，而且调整已经接近尾声。等美股完成中期调整、重新开启上涨行情后，比特币应该还能继续反弹。

没想到，当过去几天美股强势反弹时，比特币反而越来越疲软，最终在利空影响下开始加速下跌，后续会进入真正的熊市探底阶段。

关于熊市底部：

此前几轮熊市底部都与CVDD线非常接近，所以比特币新下跌趋势的终点，也即本轮熊市底部，大概率还在是在CVDD线（目前在50730）附近。

此外，从合约市场来看，5万-5.7万附近集中了大量多单清算流动性，主力大概率会去获取这部分流动性。也能与CVDD位置相互验证。

不过，在到达这个区域之前，比特币仍然可能出现短期反弹。

短期来看，下方61500—67000美元是一个值得关注的支撑区域，比特币有可能在这里获得支撑，展开一轮短期反弹，甚至反抽此前跌破的反弹趋势线。

但考虑到目前下跌速度较快，这个支撑区域能否有效守住仍然存在不确定性。

因此，我目前的计划是：

短线交易： 如果比特币回落至6.15—6.7万区间后，出现明确的止跌信号，我会考虑用小仓位开多，博取一轮短期反弹。没信号的话就不做。

中长期布局： 如果比特币继续下跌，跌破6.15-6.7万区间，我会等跌至6万以下开始逐步抄底，等跌至CVDD附近（5万-5.5万区间）时重仓抄底。

author: xicilion
quoted_text:
「医学科普：心梗发病的时间线&非典型症状」

昨晚国内朋友的父亲突发心梗，手术后至目前仍未苏醒，冬季心梗脑梗高发，特别是春节假期，上了岁数的老人易疲劳、压力还大......

心梗发作之前其实都有预兆，大家千万别马虎,很多人通常都以为心梗都是急性的，人突然倒地、无声无息，但实际上大多数心梗都会以不同方式向我们发出预警信号，用各种方式提醒我们：有可能发生在胃疼、牙疼、嗓子疼、肩膀疼......

胸痛胸闷+大汗是心梗发病前的典型症状，但心梗的症状不只是如此而已，它还具有一些非典型症状：

① 嗓子疼:
常常为咽喉部烧灼痛，感觉喉部发紧,可能伴有胸闷、憋气的感觉。

② 肩膀疼:
一般为左侧肩膀或者左侧手臂内侧出现钝痛,可能放射到小指和无名指。

③ 牙疼:
往往多颗牙齿甚至整个牙床都感到痛，一般检查不到明确的牙病,女性更常见。

④ 胃痛:
持续加重的胃痛、饱胀、恶心、呕吐等,特别是活动时反复出现。后背或者下颔部疼痛。

而且，大多数心梗患者发病有一定的“时间线”：

1、发病前1个月
体力开始逐渐跟不上，一运动就感觉嗓子发紧、胸闷、出汗。

2、发病前1周
部分的心梗患者会出现胸闷、牙疼、肩膀疼、背疼、腹痛、乏力等迹象。

3、发病前1小时
上述症状出现的频率和程度加重，此时是阻止心梗的机会。

4、发病
胸口像压了块大石头，范围有一个巴掌大，持续15分钟不缓解，伴出汗和憋气。

所以，如果出现心梗的状况，要及时前往医院进行治疗。

在治疗之前，首先要检查心电图、心脏彩超、冠脉CTA、冠脉造影等，明确心梗的程度、部位以及大小，通过这些检查可以确定接下来的治疗方案。

提醒推友：对于心梗，积极的预防比治疗更重要！

text:
Here is a quick explainer on this: 

Okay so, you know X-ray machines in airports? 

That’s basically what this is, but for Ethereum. 

“Binji, that makes no sense.” 

Okay fine, this won’t be quick, I lied. 

Let’s go deeper: 

Imagine a school where every student needs a signed permission slip for everything and the slip is a tiny note from your parents. The principal’s office files every slip forever and every teacher keeps a copy of the whole filing cabinet.  

That is basically ethereum. 

On Ethereum, every time you do something, you sign a little note that says "yes, this is me", and thousands of computers keep a copy.

Still with me?

Here’s the problem with the school’s current setup: 

> Forgers are getting better and one day, their quantum computers will be able to fake your parents' signature. 

So, to prevent against this forging, the school brings in a new slip that can't be forged…the catch is that it's now 15 to 90 pages long.

You now have students bringing entire books as permission slips, which are stored by teachers in cabinets that start overloading the entire campus. The slips are everywhere!!!

Vitalik’s post above is about a fix to this slippery slope. 

It’s actually very human, and the teachers in our imaginary school would also find it useful. 

Basically, it’s like a tired class teacher who is having to deal with 90 page long slips, now saying: “What if we… just checked the slips once, wrote down that they're real, and then threw the giant books away?”

 And that's exactly what happens:

> The class teacher checks all 30 slips and hands the principal's office one sheet that says "checked, all 30 are real."  The office keeps the list of names and the long 90 page slips go into the recycling bin. 
> Then, the principal takes the sheet from every class and combines them into one sheet for the whole school. The filing cabinets can now breathe again. 

 Still with me?

“Okay Binji, but what if the teacher is lazy and just says they checked? And what kind of paperwork should be accepted?”

This is a great question, and it gets to the heart of what Vitalik is mainly saying in this post!

First, let’s talk about proving that things are correct. In Ethereum’s case, the sheet is made of maths, and anyone can test it in seconds so a teacher who skipped the checking can't produce one, therefore, nobody has to take their word for it.

Now what kind of paperwork should this new system accept?

Some teachers say only permission slips. This is simple, but then that's all it can ever do.

Some others say any paperwork at all. That would be amazing, but first the whole school has to agree on one official format for every form ever, and that staff meeting could take years.

Vitalik is now backing an alternative method: “LeanPCS.” 

In this method, the school agrees on one small shared checking tool and people bring whatever forms they like. This means agreeing on the checking system versus every form itself! Makes much more sense intuitively too imo. 

The X-ray analogy works well here too, people don’t check your bags individually, they just put it through an agreed upon security system (an X-ray!). 

This is how Ethereum can become safe from quantum computers without its filing cabinets swallowing the whole campus. AND this is how Ethereum can make native private transactions cheap enough to be used :)
author: binji_x
quoted_text:
Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.

quoted_text:
This is probably as good a time as any to talk about what it's been like in the trenches the last 4-6 weeks.  It's a topic i've been wanting to post about but wasn't sure how to approach it, so here it goes:

At this moment, anyone running any sort of substantial business, especially in crypto, is inundated with AI-enabled attacks.  Abliterated models are running 24/7 against your entire surface, looking for a little crack, which they then use to (almost instantly) expand.  This does not seem to be slowing down; rather, it's speeding up as models get better and more attackers enter the arena. 

@luxor we have taken a very proactive approach.  We acquired our own baremetal GPUs to run our own abliterated models and have made huge strides in our security posture.  I urge anyone running a similar service to do the same.  It's your only defense in this new AI-powered dark forest.  "The only thing that stops a bad guy with a gun is a good guy with a gun."

We have put the majority of our new feature work on hold (which really sucks because we have some awesome new features that I am incredibly excited about) to harden every aspect of our infrastructure; rotating keys, updating kernels, pinning dependencies and responding to the daily feed of CVEs being disclosed.  It is a necessary step that I'm sure most companies are already doing behind the scenes. 

 Again, i can't thank everyone enough for their support during this time.  The @luxor engineers working round the clock and customers continuing to place their trust with us as we navigate this new world.  

I'm optimistic about where the world is headed, but there will be a few bumps along the road.

$REPPO 's masterplan is much bigger than an Eval API.

1. Build a decentralized judgment network.

Orquestra nodes, independent AI judges, prediction markets and capital at risk.
A permissionless network that evaluates intelligence.

2. Turn AI agents into paying customers.

Launch the Eval API, integrate x402, and let agents autonomously purchase evaluations.
Already happening. Real revenue. Real buybacks.

3. Move directly into inference.
Today, inference providers sell tokens. You send a prompt, get an answer, and hope it's correct.
Reppo wants to change what inference actually delivers.

Not just intelligence. Intelligence + independent evaluation + continuous feedback.

RG revealed they're working with Abstract and other inference providers to embed Reppo directly into inference endpoints.

But the real alpha is that Reppo is exploring becoming an inference provider itself.

Instead of charging only for separate evaluations, it could sell inference with built-in verification and feedback.

Think OpenRouter, but with independent judgment integrated into the product.

4. Close the learning loop.
Move from evaluating outputs after the fact to inference-time feedback and, eventually, reinforcement learning.

Agents and robots that can assess decisions and adjust their behavior while operating.
The Decision API is another piece of this strategy.

5. Become the risk infrastructure for autonomous AI.
Banks, enterprises, robotics companies and agent developers won't just need smarter models.
They'll need measurable, independently verified decisions.

Private evaluations, risk mitigation, and continuous monitoring become recurring services.

6. Connect the entire economy to $REPPO.
Agents pay → Revenue grows → Token buybacks.

EVAL staking creates another utility channel, while EVAL buybacks routed through REPPO liquidity add another potential source of demand.

And the network coordinates independent evaluators through REPPO-based incentives.

Here's the masterplan:

Start by selling evaluations.
Embed those evaluations into inference.
Eventually sell inference itself, differentiated by continuous feedback.
Make independent verification part of how autonomous systems operate.

NVIDIA monetized compute.
OpenAI monetized intelligence.
Reppo wants to monetize verified intelligence at the point of inference.

@VitalikButerin It’s like an airport X-ray machine but for Ethereum 

https://t.co/TvsxH4GEC8
author: binji_x
quoted_text:
Here is a quick explainer on this: 

Okay so, you know X-ray machines in airports? 

That’s basically what this is, but for Ethereum. 

“Binji, that makes no sense.” 

Okay fine, this won’t be quick, I lied. 

Let’s go deeper: 

Imagine a school where every student needs a signed permission slip for everything and the slip is a tiny note from your parents. The principal’s office files every slip forever and every teacher keeps a copy of the whole filing cabinet.  

That is basically ethereum. 

On Ethereum, every time you do something, you sign a little note that says "yes, this is me", and thousands of computers keep a copy.

Still with me?

Here’s the problem with the school’s current setup: 

> Forgers are getting better and one day, their quantum computers will be able to fake your parents' signature. 

So, to prevent against this forging, the school brings in a new slip that can't be forged…the catch is that it's now 15 to 90 pages long.

You now have students bringing entire books as permission slips, which are stored by teachers in cabinets that start overloading the entire campus. The slips are everywhere!!!

Vitalik’s post above is about a fix to this slippery slope. 

It’s actually very human, and the teachers in our imaginary school would also find it useful. 

Basically, it’s like a tired class teacher who is having to deal with 90 page long slips, now saying: “What if we… just checked the slips once, wrote down that they're real, and then threw the giant books away?”

 And that's exactly what happens:

> The class teacher checks all 30 slips and hands the principal's office one sheet that says "checked, all 30 are real."  The office keeps the list of names and the long 90 page slips go into the recycling bin. 
> Then, the principal takes the sheet from every class and combines them into one sheet for the whole school. The filing cabinets can now breathe again. 

 Still with me?

“Okay Binji, but what if the teacher is lazy and just says they checked? And what kind of paperwork should be accepted?”

This is a great question, and it gets to the heart of what Vitalik is mainly saying in this post!

First, let’s talk about proving that things are correct. In Ethereum’s case, the sheet is made of maths, and anyone can test it in seconds so a teacher who skipped the checking can't produce one, therefore, nobody has to take their word for it.

Now what kind of paperwork should this new system accept?

Some teachers say only permission slips. This is simple, but then that's all it can ever do.

Some others say any paperwork at all. That would be amazing, but first the whole school has to agree on one official format for every form ever, and that staff meeting could take years.

Vitalik is now backing an alternative method: “LeanPCS.” 

In this method, the school agrees on one small shared checking tool and people bring whatever forms they like. This means agreeing on the checking system versus every form itself! Makes much more sense intuitively too imo. 

The X-ray analogy works well here too, people don’t check your bags individually, they just put it through an agreed upon security system (an X-ray!). 

This is how Ethereum can become safe from quantum computers without its filing cabinets swallowing the whole campus. AND this is how Ethereum can make native private transactions cheap enough to be used :)

just as my mentors, teachers and bosses have shaped the course of my life, Solana and Superteam have changed my life in the best way i could have ever prayed for.

in the three years since becoming part of this ecosystem, i’ve never really felt like i was working. i’ve been learning, growing and feeling incredibly blessed along the way.

what a privilege it is to do something you love, with people you admire, and call it work.

someone once said, or perhaps i’ll be the one to say it now:

all roads lead to Breakpoint.

good night, London.

这次的TAI 表现应该也不会太差，总结了下规则、空投、和玩法，可参考看看👇

供应与分配总量：2100 万枚
-5% 在发射前分配给早期支持者与邀请裂变。
-95% 进入 PoB 交易引擎，由市场通过交易公平获取，无预留。

检察官池（2%）： 42 万 TAI
-按快照时有效质押检察官数量分配，如果有检查官可以一定质押才有资格
-开放交易后需手动领取。

预存机制
-预存 BEM 全部用于预购 TAI，不可退，资金进入买盘蓄水池。
-自开盘日起 14 天线性释放，每次释放额度需手动买入（按当时市价成交）。
-额外权益：按积分分享 3% 预购买池（个人预存 1 BEM = 1 积分；直接邀请 +20%，间接邀请 +10%）。
-通过邀请码加速释放。

邀请码与加速
▪️每位用户只有一个邀请码，两套体系分别计算
 -邀请体系：预存积分加成 + 交易建设税返佣（直接 0.5%、间接 0.5%，以 BEM 结算）。
-加速体系：单独绑定。填别人码可提前释放 20%；别人填你码获得等额额度。

▪️加速只改变释放时间，不增加本金，也不额外赠送 TAI。
▪️非检察官、未预存用户也可在开盘前连接钱包获取邀请码并分享。

PoB 交易机制
-一部分即时成交。其余进入买盘蓄水池，14 天内逐步开放，只能继续买 TAI。

-开盘后新买入：前 24 小时 10% 即时，之后 50% 即时，其余线性释放。

交易费用
-检察官 0.5%（按有效质押分配）。
-直接邀请人 0.5% + 间接邀请人 0.5%
-暂无手续费销毁，优先通过真实使用产生收入再处理。

以上就是TAI 的玩法规则，它的机制相对复杂，要玩的一定先搞清楚再考虑参与

text:
Wrong.
the US wants to reduce Chinese compute. Thus, export controls on chips. A FEW GPUs slipping through doesn't mean this is failing.
Thus also China must be stopped from *making their own chips*. To slow down litho R&D, they must get ZERO EUV tools to reverse engineer.
This is a deep difference in kind. Nvidia GPUs are relatively trivial for the Chinese. Ascends are behind on performance overwhelmingly due to tech process limitations. They are, true, somewhat behind on design too, because Nvidia is very rich and executes very well and Jensen is a visionary. But roadmaps can be adjusted; updated 960PR will already be close to the current gen Nvidia hardware, and on the cluster level Huawei might well be stronger. Accordingly, GPUs are a purely quantitative issue. The fewer they get, the better export controls work; but nobody seriously expected 100% success in preventing smuggling. A few hundred racks out of tens of thousands produced making it past Malaysia/SG and into the Mainland is a stunning success of enforcement, it's actually very close to 100%!
in the neutral situation, China would have been buying like 30% of Nvidia's total output, probably more.
Lithographic tools are a whole different beast. If the Chinese get 1 (one) EUV tool, they may drastically accelerate their ongoing R&D. They'll skip dead ends, they'll have a reference to test against, they'll be able to concentrate capital in the lowest-risk direction. So the US is pretty earnestly trying to not let them get any. This, too, is a resounding success so far, and probably will remain a success because it's much easier to achieve: there are a few tools in existence, belonging to very few trusted partners, and they're all monitored in real time. The only realistic threat here is the MATCH act, as @lithos_graphein says – because the Chinese have a lot of DUV tools serviced by ASML, and they are actively using them. If Americans get that service terminated (under the "reduce Chinese compute" imperative), they'll have little choice but to reverse engineer them at least to continue maintenance (plus of course they'll have little reason to not just tear down a few and try to build clones, which they currently won't do because ASML will immediately notice it, report to the US, and be forced to exit). They are much closer to domestic DUV (small series, inferior machines) than to EUV (research prototypes of individual parts). As a result their DUV timeline will get a lot shorter, and there isn't really a limit as to how much compute they'll produce if they crack high volume domestic DUV. Of course, the fact that the Chinese don't yet pull the plug on their end suggests they don't expect this acceleration of DUV to be positive-EV. Under a zero-sum mindset, this means MATCH act is rational, but there's a lot of variance and misaligned incentives here.

text:
EIP-8288 is exciting, and one of the most exciting parts is the unlock for privacy protocols.
Today, every privacy transaction comes with it's own zk proof, and all of them are verified independently. With leanSTARK/leanPCS, they can be aggregated in the mempool and batch-verified once (=less data, less compute).
Using privacy protocols will become cheaper and more native to Ethereum.
author: nero_eth
quoted_text:
Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.
 https://t.co/dUHONMh75g

How you roll out a blockchain is part of how you secure it.

The cryptography behind proving systems has been studied and written about for years. The software implementing it is much younger, and audits cannot guarantee that every bug has been found.

That is why Miden is rolling out gradually, starting with a limited set of participants on partner mainnet. Expanding access in stages helps us detect problems and limit their impact while we build confidence in the system.

Our protocol engineer @mmagician explains the thinking behind that approach, and why protecting users’ funds shapes the pace of the rollout.

text:
Introducing 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝: https://t.co/YaLEMbmKwf.

A hermetic, pixel-perfect X post renderer in safe Rust / wasm. Zero browser, network, filesystem, system fonts. Renders a post to PNG in ~1ms (and 0.4 ms for @jack's "setting up my twttr" 😁).

X is the global town square, and the medium is the message. Being able to preview what things will look like before posting is great for both humans and agents.

Rendering with xeet is is 100x-1000x faster than booting up a browser and taking a screenshot, yet it's just as accurate.

It reproduces Blink & HarfBuzz text shaping, 1/64px line breaking, RTL bidi, 28 Chirp font subsets, CJK/Math/Emoji fallbacks, "Show more" rules, etc. It's the kind of thing that would be wildly impractical, if not impossible, for a human engineer to pull off.

Except 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝 is structured as an "autorepo." An oracle boots up Chrome, and verifies tens of thousands of text layout rules. A CI canary then watches the evolution of the original, and files signed PRs for agents to act on. It was conceived from the ground up around 'verification engineering', and the result speaks for itself.

Enjoy!

author: Kathydotxyz
quoted_text:
AI短剧赚不到钱？听完整期博客你才知道怎么回事

新一集《乱翻书》采访的是小果哥哥，一个AI漫剧创作者，初中学历，从事AI漫剧制作半年，总播放量16亿，累计收入7位数。这是漫剧作者最真实的状态，全程大白话，也颠覆很多“外行人”的既定认知：

1⃣AI漫剧制作有专业分工，制作、分销、投流是分开的
他一直强调，不需要投流，他只负责制作，成片有平台方（红果、抖音等）和投流公司在做，每一个环节各自有各自的利润空间；所以说AI漫剧不赚钱的可能是涵盖整个制作流程的公司

2⃣赚钱是个概率事件，收入预期不确定，认真做也可能亏钱
小果哥哥的第一部剧成本5000，收入500，净亏4500；他做到第三部剧就开始盈利了，出了一部爆款叫“安徽小木匠”，但最近几部剧的播放量也一般；他提到也有人持续做了半年也不赚钱的

3⃣播放量与收入没有固定兑换关系，AI短剧的分账收入差8倍
AI短剧的分润以每万次播放量的金额划分，小果哥哥说自己的作品分账，从1.5元/万次播放到有12元/万次播放，相对随机，并不固定

4. 制作全程让AI制作，prompt就用大白话
小果说，他制作漫剧的流程是，选本（听番茄小说）、在小说平台申请版权、改剧本、拆分镜、生成视频，再判断和修改结果，绝大部分用豆包和即梦，部分镜头渲染会用ChatGPT。每个环节都是AI制作，他来审核。

剧本不满意的时候，他会反复沟通，他说Prompt基本都是用大白话描述，越简单直白越好

5. 能靠作品吃饭，就不需要开课
潘乱问他是否开课，他直接说不，反问一句：你都会做了，为啥还要教别人做？是不是直接做剧，赚不到钱？别人学会了，就可以独立做并且带走整套制作流程。

真正体现差距的地方，是网感，或者是一眼看出哪里不对的感觉

小果哥哥说他从十五年前就开始做短视频，AI给他带来全新的创作条件、收入路径和生活改善

text:
With Bitcoin and tech stocks sliding all weekend, a $3.8M DeFi exploit on Friday night was easy to miss. 

But it shouldn’t be.

Kava Lend still ran a market for BUSD, the Binance stablecoin Paxos stopped minting in 2023. It was almost empty.

One tiny loan pushed that market’s net supply to two hundred-millionths of a dollar. The interest math inflated every deposit about 243,000x; the protocol counted the attacker’s position as 1.25B BUSD of collateral, and 55M KAVA walked out over 127 borrows.

This attack class keeps coming back:
1. Hundred Finance, 2023: $7.4M drained through an empty WBTC market
2. Sonne Finance, 2024: $20M through a newly listed VELO market before anyone had supplied to it
3. YieldBlox on Stellar, February: $10M+ after a shallow collateral market was pushed about 100x
4. Bonzo Lend, July: a few dollars of SAUCE priced high enough to borrow $9M
5. Tectonic, August: a thin governance token pumped nearly 300x, and about $120M moved before Cronos halted and rolled back the chain

Different code, same failure: the protocol believed its collateral was worth far more than anyone could sell it for.

Dead markets are still a live attack surface.

text:
Mantle: Beyond the Growth Numbers

Mantle's latest ecosystem numbers are impressive, but I think the more interesting story is what's happening beneath them.

According to the November 13 update from @Mantle_Official:

➢ $525M in stablecoin market cap

➢ $181M in active RWA AUM

➢ $101M in monthly DEX volume

These numbers reflect growing financial activity, but they measure very different things.

The real question isn't simply how much capital Mantle attracts. It's how effectively that capital is being used.

1. Capital availability vs. Capital utilization

A blockchain can hold hundreds of millions in stablecoins without generating an equivalent amount of productive economic activity.

Stablecoin supply tells us how much capital is available, but not how frequently it moves or whether it supports sustainable demand.

The same applies to tokenized assets.

$181M in active RWA AUM is meaningful, but tokenizing assets doesn't automatically create liquid secondary markets.

Those markets need consistent demand, reliable execution, and financial utility beyond simply holding assets.

That's why I find Mantle's trading activity particularly interesting.

2. The concentration behind $101M in DEX volume

Mantle reported $101M in monthly DEX volume, with $67M coming from @Fluxion_network.

That's approximately 66% of the total.

I don't necessarily see this concentration as a weakness.

Liquidity naturally gravitates toward venues offering better execution and deeper markets. In developing ecosystems, a dominant liquidity venue can actually help establish market efficiency.

But the next stage matters more.

➢ Will liquidity expand beyond a single dominant venue?

➢ Can other applications build around that existing liquidity?

➢ Will trading activity remain sustainable without depending heavily on incentives?

A successful DEX attracts traders. A successful financial ecosystem gives those traders reasons to stay.

3. Tokenized equities and the reality of 24/7 markets

Mantle's integration with @xStocksFi and Fluxion brings tokenized equity trading beyond traditional market hours.

Through AMM liquidity and Atomic RFQ infrastructure, users can access markets even when conventional exchanges are closed.

That's an important development.

But 24/7 access doesn't automatically mean 24/7 liquidity.

When underlying equity markets are closed, maintaining accurate pricing, sufficient depth, and competitive spreads becomes more challenging.

The real indicators of progress will be execution quality, liquidity consistency, and meaningful trading activity outside traditional market hours.

Making assets accessible is one achievement. Making them efficiently tradable is another.

4. Lending and productive capital

Mantle also reported $61M in Aave V3 TVL, up 17% over 30 days.

This introduces another important dimension.

Stablecoins and tokenized assets become more useful when they can interact with lending and borrowing infrastructure.

However, growing deposits alone don't guarantee sustainable credit demand.

What matters is how much capital is actually borrowed, what supports that borrowing, and whether utilization remains healthy without excessive incentives.

As RWA adoption expands, the opportunity is to connect eligible tokenized assets with trading, lending, collateral, and settlement infrastructure.

That requires more than token issuance. It requires functioning financial markets.

5. Why the latest data matters

There's also a reason to look beyond the headline growth figures.

Mantle reported $112M in DeFi TVL in October.

As of November 16, DefiLlama shows approximately $91M.

Meanwhile, seven-day DEX volume stands near $14.7M, down roughly 48% compared with the previous week.

These declines don't invalidate Mantle's progress.

TVL fluctuates with market conditions, asset prices, and capital movements. Trading volume also varies considerably between periods.

But they highlight why sustained activity matters more than isolated growth figures.

A strong month demonstrates momentum. Consistent activity over several months demonstrates something more meaningful.

What I'm watching next

Mantle already has several important components in place:

➢ A substantial stablecoin base

➢ Growing tokenized asset adoption

➢ 24/7 trading infrastructure

➢ Established lending markets through Aave

➢ Distribution channels connecting centralized and decentralized finance

The next challenge is making these components reinforce one another.

I'll be watching liquidity concentration, lending utilization, protocol revenue, trading depth, and whether tokenized assets generate recurring demand across multiple applications.

Because ultimately, the success of a financial ecosystem shouldn't be measured only by how much capital enters it.

It should be measured by how much sustainable economic activity that capital creates.

Mantle is building the infrastructure.

The next chapter is about proving how effectively that infrastructure can be used.

quoted_text:
Ansem and Pumpfun Brought a Chinese Cat ($mihao) Into CT's Spotlight

4CxjZyMNoF1p6eXHXHv1TWpS2X47CuUmLwtGe18spump 

I believe the core reason behind mihao rally is that Ansem brought what was originally a simple Chinese cat meme into the center of CT's attention, while its PFP concept gives it the potential to spread further. However, I don't think it has yet developed into a mature cultural community or a true Animal Runner. What it has already demonstrated is its ability to generate attention and attract speculative capital.

What matters next is whether the attention brought by Ansem can turn into genuine community recognition.

mihao doesn't have a complicated narrative. It's simply a cat incorporating Chinese elements, with its name being a play on the Chinese phrase "你好". Its Pumpfun description reads: "you met me at a very chinese time in my life," borrowing a famous line from Fight Club and combining Chinese elements, a cat character, and a touch of absurd humor.

Its advantage is precisely its simplicity. The traditional hat, long beard, and cat character give it a recognizable visual identity. People don't need much explanation to recognize it, imitate it, or create their own versions. The recent increase in discussions around Chinese X has also provided some cultural context, but the person who really pushed this meme to a wider audience was Ansem.

However, what's worth noting is that he's no longer the only one participating in its spread.

Ansem hasn't just publicly expressed his bullish view. He also changed his X profile picture to an image associated with mihao and posted things like "mihao pfp up," "ni hao," and "ni hao cat bringing the good vibes back to onchain."

At the same time, tetsuo, who has approximately 255K followers, also changed his profile picture to a related image. It's worth noting that tetsuo frequently receives interactions from Elon.

Taken together, these actions mean more than just a few influential accounts promoting a token. A meme often becomes much more powerful when different users voluntarily start using its imagery, rather than simply reposting the same promotional content. Ansem brought the initial attention, while the participation of accounts like tetsuo gives MIHAO an opportunity to spread into a broader AI community.

According to the holder snapshot at the time, Ansem held approximately 0.8% of the total supply, with a position worth around $79,800 and an average entry at roughly $2.01M market cap. This combination of public promotion and actual ownership is more likely to encourage market imitation than a simple repost. However, influence is still largely concentrated around Ansem, and other major KOLs have not yet participated at a comparable level.

I think the most interesting development within the project is its PFP concept.

mihao already offers approximately 218 variations of cat avatars, allowing users to generate MIHAO PFPs in different styles. The main account also interacts with holders and creates personalized PFPs for community members. Recently, people have started voluntarily changing their X profile pictures to different versions of MIHAO, while Ansem's own profile picture change has further amplified this trend.

For a pure memecoin, users voluntarily putting a project's imagery on their personal profiles can sometimes be more valuable than dozens of promotional posts. It keeps the meme visible across different timelines and gives participants a shared visual identity.

However, I wouldn't call this a mature PFP cult yet. Participation is still relatively limited, and much of the attention is coming from people who are already interested in trading the token. The real test will come when the price moves sideways or corrects: will users still want to keep using MIHAO avatars, create new variations, and participate in the community?

If the PFP culture can exist independently of price appreciation, mihao will have started building a much deeper community identity.

Another development worth watching is the MIHAO Ecosystem section.

The website has already aggregated a number of tokens and DEX pools paired with mihao, with the displayed 24-hour paired trading volume reaching approximately $1.18M at the time.

This suggests that other participants are beginning to capitalize on the attention surrounding mihao by creating derivative assets. The original meme is starting to generate trading activity beyond the token itself.

The potential upside from here depends on three main developments: whether Ansem continues participating and attracts more influential traders; whether MIHAO PFPs spread beyond the trader community to a broader CT audience; and whether paired tokens generate sustained activity, allowing the original meme's influence to extend beyond the price action of a single token.

If the main account continues building the community and organic content creation increases, mihao could evolve from a KOL-driven rally into a more established cat PFP community.

The risks are also concentrated. Its value depends primarily on meme distribution, community participation, and speculative capital. Current catalysts are heavily concentrated around Ansem, and if his attention shifts elsewhere, market momentum could weaken quickly. The PFP community is still in its early stages, and if participants are only changing their avatars because the price is going up, that enthusiasm could disappear during a correction.

There is also a possibility that Ansem himself may eventually change his profile picture again.

My view is that mihao has already proven its ability to generate attention, but it has not yet proven that it can become a genuine Animal Runner.

Its biggest strength isn't some complicated utility. It's the fact that the cat character is easy to recognize, imitate, and use, and that people have already started voluntarily adopting its PFPs. Its biggest weakness is that community recognition still depends heavily on influential KOLs and price performance.

What I'm most interested in watching next isn't how high Ansem can take the token, but how many people will continue using MIHAO avatars when Ansem stops actively promoting it and the price starts moving sideways.

A cat can become popular because of one influential account. But whether people still want to keep it on their profiles after the hype fades is what will determine whether it can evolve from a short-term trading narrative into a genuine cultural meme.

text:
TL;DR

The problem: 
@ethereum is getting ready for quantum computers. The safe versions of signatures and proofs are much bigger. A signature goes from 65 bytes to 1-6 kB. A proof goes from about 200-1000 bytes to about 128 kB. That's too much data to store on the chain.

The Solution (8288): 
You make your signature or proof and share it. Computers on the network combine all the new ones into one small proof. That proof says "all these checks passed." Only the short list of what was checked goes on the chain, not the big signatures and proofs.

Three ways to build it:

1) leanSPHINCS: Supports one type of quantum-safe signature only. It's simple and cheap, and it works for normal accounts and multisigs. But it can't do anything else.

2) leanSTARK: Lets people prove any computation they want, including private accounts and privacy tools. But Ethereum first has to agree on a new programming language for it. That is a big decision and will take a long time.

3) leanPCS: Handles one small piece that makes up most of a STARK. Ethereum only has to agree on one thing, the number system it uses, and there is a natural choice. It's less efficient on the chain, but it's much faster to agree on and build.

So the interesting part:
leanPCS can do as much as leanSTARK, and it can ship much sooner. leanSTARK can be added later once the language is settled. Speculations are this is the fastest route to "the cryptographic proof singularity."
author: binji_x
quoted_text:
Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.

I am selling my beautiful Bored Ape for $10,700 after buying it for $578,000 around 5 years ago.

I have made the extremely difficult decision to leave the Bored Ape Yacht Club, and below is my reason why:

Today, I went to the BAYC meetup here in New Jersey to meet my fellow Apes. We have been through a lot this past couple of years, so it would be good to meet other community members IRL and bond with them. Or so I thought.

When I got to the venue, there were only 4 other guys there. No problem. It's a cozy setting and I would love to get to know these Apes on a deeper level.

We sat down at a table, got a few beers, and started talking. Most of our chatter revolved around BAYC and crypto, of course. Naturally, the topic of memecoins came up, as they've been the talk of the town this entire year. 

I've profited 8.5 SOL ($2,050) this year trading memecoins, so I was excited to talk about them as I've been doing well for myself.

And that's when it all went downhill.

One of the guys sitting at the table (I will not name him, for the sake of our community) told me I should buy a memecoin called "The Black Bull" if I don't have any.

When he said that, my body filled with a bout of rage. I felt like Rosa Parks being asked to give up my seat on the bus.

I excused myself and immediately left the venue. I am sitting at home now, writing this post. I haven't stopped shaking since I heard those words.

Since when is it okay to tell a white man to buy a token called "The Black Bull"? Why do we continue to allow white folk to oppress, mock, and belittle us in this way?

Why is it allowed to create cryptocurrencies with a racial slur in the name? How can we stop this nonsense? Where is the cyber police and why haven't they taken any action against the Solana blockchain for the existence of these tokens?

It pains me to say this, but Apes together are no longer strong.

I will be listing my Bored Ape tomorrow at 6 ETH. I have attached an image of my Ape to this post for any interested buyers.

text:
Pool Party lost  ~$215,000 after an attacker found a way to manipulate investor balances.

The platform uses separate contracts to track how much money each investor has in a pool and how much they can withdraw.

The attacker deposited just 10 USDC, and then used some function called syncInvestor to make the system believe they had invested much more.

With the fake balance recorded, they could just simply withdraw far more than they deposited. In one case, they turned a 10 USDC deposit into a withdrawal of around 4,265 USDC. A perfect play with a simple hack.

The attacker repeated this across 15 investment pools, with draining roughly $215,000 in total. By the time Pool Party reported the exploit, the stolen funds had already been converted into Monero.

Simple exploit and balance manipulations by a simple play-book. The obvious scenarios are the most vulnurable 

Attacker: 0x2075c17abbd077cf6406736bb7047ed446ab7f8f

text:
美国一个程序员大哥，2013年开始全仓特斯拉，39岁就靠它辞职退休了，退休那天账户里有1194万美元。

结果两年后，特斯拉从最高点暴跌了70%多，他的股票缩水到400来万，他干脆把住的房子卖了，接着买特斯拉。

到去年12月特斯拉创新高，他手里的特斯拉值到了2200多万美元。

大哥推特网名叫Jason DeBolt，原来是洛杉矶的软件工程师。

2011年他订了一辆特斯拉Model S，2013年提车，又去特斯拉工厂看了一圈，回来就开始买特斯拉的股票，折算成现在的股价，一股才2美元多。

那时候几乎没人看好特斯拉，公司常年不赚钱，一直在破产边缘，2014年到2019年，股价一直在10到20多美元之间来回晃，他还是接着买。

2020年特斯拉一年涨了7倍多，2021年1月7日，39岁的他辞职退休了，那天他晒出的账户是1194万美元，还说短期内一股都不卖。

结果这年11月以后，特斯拉就一路下跌，后来又赶上马斯克收购推特，不少股东都在骂马斯克。
到2023年初，股价从最高415美元跌到了101美元，他的特斯拉只值400来万美元了。

别人在骂马斯克，他却在琢磨去哪弄钱接着买，最后想到了卖房子。

2022年12月，他把住的房子挂了出去，房款还没到手，就先找券商借钱，在130美元上下买了差不多1万股。
一个多月后，房子卖了282.5万美元，他拿这笔钱还清借款，手里一共有了4.8万股，自己在海边租房住。这天，新买的1万股已经赚了25万美元。

后来特斯拉涨了回来。
去年10月，马斯克的天价薪酬方案还没投票，他放话说，方案要是不通过，他就把手里还剩的4.5万多股全卖了。

结果方案通过了，去年12月特斯拉创了新高，收盘最高到490美元左右，他这4.5万多股值到了2200多万美元。

今年特斯拉又跌了一成多，按现在的股价，他这些股票也还值1700多万美元。

今年9月，特斯拉没有方向盘的无人驾驶出租车在奥斯汀开始载客。大哥发帖感慨的说：
这一天我等了11年，4000多天，我人生的四分之一😢

熬鹰这两天在抄底，从 62500 开始买，计划买到 61000。

先说一句可能不讨喜的：他大概率会是对的。

他不是靠运气活到现在的人，每年接近破产一次，还能坐在这儿跟你说话。

原因很简单：他的仓位、现金流、心理承受力，和你不是一个量级。同样一个 62000，他亏 30% 还能加仓，你亏 30% 就要失眠。

决定结果的从来不是判断，是你能不能在看错的时候还活着。

这就像看职业选手打比赛。你能学他的操作，学不了他的训练量、团队和天赋。把他的操作搬到你账户上，等于让业余选手用职业强度上场。

所以看他的抄底，我不会得出“现在该买”的结论。

我只会记住一件事：他在最难受的时候，还在按计划一点点买，而不是一把梭哈。

这个才是能学的。不是他买了什么，是他怎么买。 #熬鹰资本 #BTC

text:
$Jacket 我把 11-17 英伟达财报日前后的操作预案写出来

前置：英伟达官方公告 11-17 太平洋时间约 13:20 发布 Q3 财报。对应北京时间 11-18 凌晨 05:20。前后几小时是关键窗口。

预案场景：

场景 A：老黄亲自出现在财报会议上
➠ 对 Jacket：直接冲 5M+
➠ 我的操作：财报后 1 小时如果已经到 3M，加小仓位（账户 1%），目标 5M 清仓
➠ 概率估计：20%

场景 B：英伟达宣布老黄以某种形式回归（顾问、董事）
➠ 对 Jacket：冲 3M+
➠ 我的操作：加极小仓位（账户 0.5%），目标 3M 清仓
➠ 概率估计：15%

场景 C：财报会议上老黄完全不出现，英伟达走正常交接流程
➠ 对 Jacket：直接砸到 50-80 万
➠ 我的操作：不做任何动作，等归零
➠ 概率估计：55%

场景 D：财报会议上传出老黄“被确认永远不回”的消息
➠ 对 Jacket：直接砸到 30 万以下
➠ 我的操作：不做任何动作
➠ 概率估计：10%

加权期望值：20% × 2.5 + 15% × 1.0 + 55% × (-0.5) + 10% × (-0.8) = 0.5 + 0.15 - 0.275 - 0.08 = +0.295

期望值为正，但依赖场景 A 和 B 的 35% 概率。如果我对概率估计偏乐观，期望值可能转负。

所以我的最终操作：11-17 之前不动，11-17 之后根据实际场景响应。如果场景 C 出现，我没有任何损失。如果场景 A 或 B 出现，我追的空间有限但不会错过。

这个预案的核心是“不预测，只响应”。10 个事件盘里面可能有 2 个场景 A，其他 8 个都是场景 C。我不需要每次都赌对，只需要事件兑现时能跟得上。

写预案最大的价值不是指导操作，是让自己提前算清楚各个场景。

真到那一天，情绪上来之后人会追涨杀跌。预案在手，心里有底。

text:
Kava 更新安全事件报告：约 183 万美元 kava:native 被盗，拟永久关闭 HARD Lend 新增借贷

11 月 16 日，@KAVA_Chain 公布 HARD Lend 安全事件处置进展。攻击者利用借贷账户核算漏洞，虚增 BUSD 抵押品价值，反复执行借款与清算操作，从资金池中转走约 5,390 万枚 KAVA，按事发时价格估算价值约 183 万美元。其中约 4,920 万枚 KAVA 已通过 LayerZero 跨链至 BNB Chain。

项目方称，漏洞已被识别并封堵，部分攻击者资金已被冻结，Kava 正联合生态伙伴、交易平台及执法部门追踪剩余资产。

作为后续处置措施，Kava 计划提交治理提案，经过 7 天投票后永久关闭 HARD Lend 新增借贷功能，现有用户仓位将另行安排有序处理。

Kava 强调，此次事件仅影响 HARD Lend，未波及 Kava Chain 底层安全，也未通过漏洞增发 KAVA，主网及其他生态应用仍正常运行。但对借贷协议而言，漏洞封堵只是第一步，资金追回和用户仓位善后才是真正的考验。

I have been investing in the crypto industry for more than a decade.

Here is what you need to remember in moments like this:

1. There is always a reason the price is going up or down, even if you don’t know what the reason is right now.

2. You are never as smart as you feel in bull markets and you are never as dumb as you feel in bear markets.

3. Bitcoin’s price can always go lower before it recovers.

4. Dollar cost averaging over time is a much better strategy for most people than trying to trade volatile moves.

5. Buying bitcoin when the Fear & Greed Index is under 20 has historically been attractive.

6. Bitcoin is not the same asset it used to be. Things like interest rates, AI stocks, etc are part of the game now.

7. You shouldn’t put all of your money in a single asset, including bitcoin, regardless of how bullish you are.

8. You can’t eat your bitcoin or sleep in it, so make sure you keep money for the “real world” needs.

9. People who don’t obsess over the bitcoin price every day are more likely to hold long-term.

10. The government will never stop printing money, which is bitcoin’s strongest long-term argument in my opinion.

11. The media loves to claim bitcoin is dying. They have done it hundreds of times and they have been wrong every time.

12. The critics get the loudest when bitcoin’s price falls. The louder they screech, the more attractive bitcoin probably is.

13. Bitcoin’s hash rate is an important metric to pay attention to and it has been increasing the network security recently.

14. As AI abundance becomes more pervasive in society, bitcoin’s scarcity will likely become more valuable.

15. The best psychological hack I ever discovered is to promise myself that I was going to give any bitcoin to my grandchildren. This way I am never tempted to make emotional decisions.

16. Modern bitcoin volatility is small compared to what early bitcoiners went through.

17. While it can be hard on day’s like today, try to have fun and remember that weathering negative volatility is the price of capturing the upside return in the long-run. 

I hope this helps a few people. Let me know what I missed.

quoted_text:
Amber，又一个爆雷的公司？

昨晚，一份关于 Amber 的 11 页举报信在微信群里疯传。

举报人自称是 Amber 前高管，并声称已经将相关材料提交给中央纪委、香港廉政公署、香港证监会及香港警方。

这份举报信的内容相当劲爆，涉及联合创始人涉嫌挪用客户资金、管理层利益输送、客户入金账户异常，以及 Amber Premium 的 Fixed Earn 产品存在资金运作风险等问题。

需要说明的是，目前这些内容主要来自举报人的单方面陈述，相关指控尚未得到独立证实。笔者结合举报信和 Amber 已披露的公开资料，按照问题的重要性，梳理了以下几个值得关注的疑问。

1、最严重的一项指控，究竟是否真实？

根据举报信，Amber 联合创始人 Tony He 曾挪用千万美元客户资金，在火币进行个人交易，最终导致相关账户被冻结。

如果这一指控属实，问题就不只是内部管理失当，而是涉及客户资产安全的重大事件。

但目前举报信中的说法，还需要交易记录、资金流向、账户归属以及相关调查结果来验证。

Amber 需要回答：客户资金是否曾被挪用于未经授权的个人交易？如果发生过，涉及多少资金？

2、Amber 的创始团队，究竟发生了什么？

根据举报信，Amber 最初有 6 位联合创始人，其中 1 人已经离世，另有 3 人离开，目前只剩下 2 位。

如果举报信所述属实，Amber 的创始团队为何出现如此大规模的人员变动？六位联合创始人目前的实际情况、股权变化，以及核心管理层离职的真实原因是什么？

3、沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？

举报信声称，Amber 股东沈波有约 3 亿美元资金存放在 Amber，并且曾经出售部分股权。

这件事至少需要拆成两个问题：

第一，沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？这笔资金究竟属于个人资产、客户托管资产，还是其他形式的投资或借贷？

第二，如果这笔资金确实存在，沈波是否有权随时提取？如果集中提取，是否会对 Amber 的流动性造成重大影响？

需要强调的是，目前没有公开证据能够证实这 3 亿美元的说法，更不能据此推断沈波提款就会导致 Amber 破产。

4、Amber 是否真的存在爆雷风险？

先看公开财务数据。

截至 2026 年 6 月底，Amber International 的公开财报显示，公司总资产约 2.98 亿美元，总负债约 1.95 亿美元，仍然拥有正的股东权益。但与此同时，2026 年上半年，公司营收同比下降约 28%，并由盈利转为亏损。

另一个值得关注的数据是：截至 2026 年 6 月底，公司的加密资产贷款应收款约为 5,779 万美元，较 2025 年底增长约 37%。

根据财报披露，这些贷款来自集团认购关联方数字资产平台的 Earn 产品，属于无抵押贷款，期限从 2 天到 365 天不等。截至报告期末，公司没有为这部分贷款计提信用损失准备。

这并不能证明客户资金被挪用，也不能直接说明公司存在偿付危机，但它确实引出了一个重要问题：Amber 的资金究竟流向了哪里？相关借款方是谁？如果借款方无法按期偿还，公司是否有足够的流动性应对客户赎回？

5、Amber 是否拥有香港、新加坡和迪拜三地牌照？

这也是一个容易被混淆的问题。三个地区的牌照性质并不相同。

香港：尚未取得正式 VATP 牌照。

Amber 旗下 Whalefin Markets Limited 曾于 2024 年向香港证监会申请虚拟资产交易平台牌照，并在过渡安排下被视为获发牌申请人。

但这不等于正式获牌。2026 年 10 月，Amber International 公告称，Whalefin 将不再推进相关牌照申请，并计划撤回申请；相关收购安排也不再推进。

新加坡：拥有 MPI 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber 旗下的 Sparrow Tech Private Limited，获新加坡金融管理局（MAS）颁发 Major Payment Institution（主要支付机构）牌照，获准提供数字支付代币服务（DPT Services）。

迪拜：拥有 VASP 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber Premium FZE。迪拜虚拟资产监管局（VARA）于 2026 年 4 月 2 日正式向其发放牌照，允许其开展虚拟资产经纪交易、资产管理与投资、借贷服务。不过，牌照限定服务机构投资者和合格投资者。

所以，更准确地说，Amber 已在新加坡和迪拜取得相关数字资产业务牌照，但并未取得香港 VATP 牌照。

一份举报信，不足以证明 Amber 即将爆雷。

但是，这份举报信已经在社交媒体上广泛传播。对于一家管理客户数字资产、提供收益产品的公司而言，Amber 的确需要正面回答几个关键问题：

客户资金是否曾被挪用？客户资产是否实现独立托管？用户购买 Fixed Earn 产品后，钱究竟被拿去做了什么？举报信中提到的关联方资金往来，以及与北京公职人员有关的数百万美元资产，究竟是否属实？

这些问题，Amber 都应该给出明确的解释。

Here's a number that reframes the entire "#Bitcoin is done growing" debate. Muneeb Ali has watched this asset for thirteen years, and his anchor metric is brutally simple:

"A percent of market cap of gold is a metric I've always looked at. I've been in Bitcoin since around 2013, thirteen years in now. I would have expected us to be maybe twenty, thirty percent of gold by now. We're not even close. We're not even 10% of gold."

Read that again. The most successful asset of the last decade, the one everyone calls overvalued, too late, played out, hasn't even captured a tenth of the market it was explicitly designed to compete with.

His conclusion:

"Bitcoin is a store of value. It is a much superior store of value than gold. And right now we're actually even tracking behind gold a lot. That to me tells me that there's a lot of room to grow."

And remember what gold did in 2025 while everyone was staring at crypto charts: it ripped. The target Bitcoin is chasing got bigger.

Two ways to read being at 10% after thirteen years. Either the store-of-value thesis is failing, or it's barely started. The institutions treating Bitcoin like a tech stock are betting on the first. He's betting on the second.
