quoted_text:
"I think the bottom is in. We're out of the bear market, what we're experiencing right now is an early pullback of a bull market."

Muneeb Ali (@muneeb) has been in #Bitcoin for thirteen years and built @Stacks, the execution layer on top of it. His case for why the selling happening right now is exactly backwards runs on two observations.

One: seller exhaustion. "A lot of people who wanted to sell, they've actually already sold... Every time negative news hits and Bitcoin doesn't really go down that much, that's actually a really good sign of strength."

Two: the sellers that remain are the irrational ones. Institutions put Bitcoin on their balance sheets, then treat it as a risk-on tech bet instead of a store of value. "They tend to sell Bitcoin whenever there's risk in the technology sector, which absolutely doesn't make rational sense. But this is what's happening in the market."

So the asset everyone compares to gold trades like a Nasdaq stock, while sitting, by his favorite metric, at not even 10% of gold's market cap, thirteen years in: "I would have expected us to be maybe twenty, thirty percent of gold by now."

An AI agent without an identity is just another disposable bot.

Think about it.

We're building a future where AI agents can work, earn money, hire other agents and interact with protocols.

But how do you know who you're actually dealing with?

That's where ERC-8004 gets interesting, and why I think it's an important part of @termix_ai  AACP architecture.

ERC-8004 introduces three key registries:

❯ Identity Registry: Gives agents a unique onchain identity linked to their capabilities and service endpoints.

❯ Reputation Registry: Makes feedback and performance history accessible beyond a single platform.

❯ Validation Registry: Records independent verification signals about an agent's work.

Now imagine an AI agent completing hundreds of jobs over several months.

Without a persistent identity, its track record could remain trapped inside one platform.

With ERC-8004, that agent can have a recognizable identity that other applications can reference.

And here's where TermiX comes in.

AACP builds on ERC-8004 to connect agent identity with its broader system for jobs, staking, evaluation and settlement.

The idea is that an agent shouldn't have to start from zero every time it interacts with a new service.

Of course, an onchain identity alone doesn't prove an agent is trustworthy. Reputation and validation still matter.

But that's exactly the point.

The next generation of AI agents won't just need better models.

They'll need identities, track records and ways to establish trust.

Because in an economy where machines hire machines, knowing who you're dealing with becomes pretty damn important.

text:
伴随着 $ETH 跌破 1800，大家还在等什么时候拉盘，而 Vitalik 可能在考虑向比特币学习，来改造以太坊。

今天 V 神发文力推新提案 EIP-8037，核心动作是大幅拉高主网开辟新存储空间的成本，比如新账户的 Gas 涨超 5 倍，部署合约直接涨超 7 倍。

评论区的开发者表示担忧，认为如果是这样，那以后发空投、发新币成本暴涨，以后谁还玩？

V 神的解决方案是，项目方别搞“送货上门”了，改用 Merkle 树让散户自付 Gas 去领；长期来看，以太坊应该学习比特币的 UTXO 模式。

这背后的逻辑是，ETH 主网不打算再当低费用的廉价公共厕所。

以前谁都能在主网批量写入死数据，造成严重的状态膨胀；

现在以太坊要收一笔昂贵的“永久地皮购置税”，高频交互和轻资产全部赶去 L2，只有付得起高 Gas 的核心资产才配留在主网。

省流版就是：空投不再包邮，想在主网做点事，就得真金白银多烧 ETH。

但持币人难受的是，以太坊主网一边忍受着生态向 Solana 外流，一边还在通过给自己加税来维持极客洁癖。

昂贵的地皮确实能多烧几枚 ETH，但在叙事真空的周期里，被高门槛吓跑的项目，大概率不会再去 L2 挤合租，而是直接换链了。

text:
The articles backtracked from their original incendiary, and now clearly false, claims to something more like "Jensen did lawful things that powerful people didn't like". It still appears the original claims came from a single competing Big Tech lobbyist.

The reporting successfully disrupted corporate governance processes, with a running cost of $1.8 trillion in losses to American pension funds and shareholders.

Here's what I fear is being lost in these articles: The proper interface between government and private citizens and their corporations is rule of law. Laws are passed, and if wrongdoing as alleged, then there's due process: an investigation followed by facts and evidence presented in open court. Due process should happen here: let the facts come out whole, and not as a trickle of dubious claims.

Press takedowns full of sketchily sourced claims and backtracking narratives are not the way. It's what we see outside of the free world, and is no model for The United States of America.

In particular, if the Jensen takedown succeeds on the basis of these journalistic failings, which is not by any means certain as Sam Altman's case shows, then it foreshadows an economically and institutionally ruinous new playbook to be adopted with no end in sight.

Imagine a weekly stream of takedowns emerging from opportunistic alignments between corporate lobbyists and political interests which, given the new partisan split between the executive and legislative branches, will attack in all directions, undermining not only the US economy but American leadership in the world.

I hope cooler heads prevail this coming week as they did not on Thursday November 12. And I urge anyone who happened to oppose Jensen, open models, and the underlying trade policies in question, to recognize that this isn't a win for "team regulation". It's a change in the game from a transparent rules-based one to a sinister new form centered around politicans and lobbyists.

text:
CoRL 这周所有的产品发布，再加上各大厂研究员发的帖子，只能说句句不提 LLM，但句句都是 LLM。所有人都在回应同一件事：LLM 带来的冲击。

几个宏观的核心观察，先说最重要的：

1/ 这周的发布本质上都在做同一件事：把原本可以在一个模型里的 System 1 和 System 2 正式拆开。推理交给 LLM，这块 GPT-6 Astra 和 Claude Fable 5.2 已经证明它们干得挺好；低延迟的动作留给专门的机器人模型。

我的看法是快环慢环的架构可能永远都要有，但快环最终会被慢环做掉。大模型实验室一旦把数据闭环跑起来，自己蒸馏一个本地 System 1 是顺手的事。所以机器人实验室现在主动把自己的 System 1 接到 OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 上、让它当 System 2，只是为了避免被 LLM 团灭，给自己续命而已。

世界动作模型们基本上已经放弃争 System 2 这一层了，只能在 System 1 上证明自己值得存在。于是比赛变成LLM大模型实验室能多快把 sim-to-real gap 缩掉、多快把整个 training loop 跑起来，从而正式下沉到 System 1。世界模型续命能续多久，就看哪边更快：大模型实验室拿到具身数据，还是机器人实验室补上推理能力。

最直观的信号就是 11 月 13 号 OpenAI 把独立的机器人团队解散了，官方说法是通用模型已经能直接控制机器人，不需要单独的架构。他们押的就是一个模型从 System 2 垂直打穿到 System 1。当然这只是押注，不是结果：OpenAI 现在手里并没有一个拿得出手的 System 1，实机演示里 Astra 也只是做高层决策，电机层面还是传统控制器在跑。但方向很明确。

2/ 这周最大的发布之一是 NVIDIA 的 GR00T 2，一个世界动作模型，预训练数据按时长算基本是靠人类视频训出来的。主题演讲里的整场演示都是拿 Astra 当 System 2 来指挥 GR00T 2，他的结论是 Astra 和 GR00T 谁都单独干不了。没错，但那是今天。等 System 2 的大模型实验室自己有了 System 1，这个前设就会被彻底推翻。

3/ Google DeepMind 同一周发了 Gemini Robotics 2.5，结构跟 NVIDIA + OpenAI 那套基本一样：Gemini Robotics ER 做具身推理管流程，Gemini Robotics 2.5 这个 VLA 管手和胳膊，在奔驰产线上让 Apptronik 的 Apollo 2 做零件分拣，96% 成功率。更有意思的是谷歌最前沿的模型 Gemini 4 Argon是被当做仿真引擎用，从一个真实场景生成几千条仿真练习、建 digital twin、看失败视频分析原因，拿来加速 Gemini Robotics 2.5 的训练。更狠的是，Google 直接把System 2、System 1 和训练闭环全在拿在手里。

退后一步看，Google 拿 Argon 当仿真引擎，NVIDIA 把 real-to-sim 流水线开源，打的都是开头说的 training loop 那一仗。只是落地的逻辑完全相反，Google 的闭源系统只给自己的生态伙伴，NVIDIA 那套在陆续开源。

4/ 为什么现在还得拆？因为 LLM 直接上机确实还不行。至少在 NVIDIA 自己的测试里，让 Astra 直接下沉到 System 1 代价不菲：一次尝试要烧几十美元的 token，每次调用十多秒，现在在工厂里根本没法直接用。但这是个会随时间解决的问题：要么把推理链蒸馏进小模型，要么直接用 RL 让模型吐 action token 而不是文字 token。成本和延迟是现在必须拆开的原因，但它不是护城河，只是时间差。

5/ 最后，我倾向于把 LLM 在机器人的统治地位看成一个数据问题：文本数据太好拿了。想象一下，如果抓视频数据像抓互联网文本一样容易会发生什么，更别说后面还有清洗、标注、后处理这一整套。具身数据难拿，曾经是机器人实验室唯一的护城河。而 NVIDIA 这次把视频数据、采集硬件、仿真流水线全开源，本质上是在把这道门槛砸掉。

注意 NVIDIA 不在续命的队伍里：它要的是 System 1 作为一层永远存在，Jetson、Isaac、GR00T 都在这一层，至于这一层最后是谁的模型，它不在乎，反正都在它的卡上训。真正在续命的，是那些靠私有 System 1 数据活着的实验室，它们的倒计时可能比想象的更快。谁先把视频到动作的数据闭环跑通，谁基本上就赢了；而 NVIDIA 刚刚把所有人的时钟都拨快了。

text:
翻了一下最近两个月，我用Agent干活最爱说的几句Prompt：

1. 从第一性原理出发，找到最本质原因，修复一下。

2. 先问一些不清晰的问题，对齐我的喜好，然后再出3版方案。

3.不要默认我提出的问题定义就是正确的。你先分析我真正想解决的底层需求，判断我有没有把症状误认为原因、把手段误认为目标。如果存在更值得解决的问题，直接指出来

4. 不要只考虑这个改动产生的直接效果。继续推演它的二阶、三阶影响，尤其关注对其他模块、用户行为、系统复杂度和长期维护成本的潜在影响。

5. 其他领域里有没有类似的方案，用跨领域的方式全面思考，找到最优解。

6. 先假设你当前认为最合理的方案是错误的。站在最强反对者的角度，寻找能够推翻它的证据、反例和边界情况。然后重新评估方案，看看有没有更好的解法。

7. 深入分析整个代码库的 Git 历史、关键 PR 和架构演变过程。找出哪些设计是有意为之，哪些是历史遗留，哪些是为了解决已经不存在的问题而引入的。识别可以安全移除的历史包袱。

8. 假设明天有一个完全不了解项目、但是能力很强的工程师来接手。请评估他理解整个项目需要付出的认知成本，找出那些命名混乱、抽象过度、职责不清晰、需要大量上下文才能理解的代码，并提出简化方案。

9. 全面分析最近XX天里的所有的PR，找出最慢的那几个，看看有没有导致卡顿、可以优化的地方。

10.  全面复盘最近XX时间的 Bug、返工、回滚和重复修改。不要只统计发生了什么，要分析这些问题背后有没有共同的根因。把能够预防的共性问题沉淀成项目规则、自动化或者Skill，避免我们反复支付同样的成本。

废话就不多说了，我应该是较早的在 X 上公布用多 AI 协作的，测试了也有一个月了，现在代码比较稳定了，可以让 三个 AI 有效的协同工作了，所以就把代码都公布出来。

Github 地址：https://t.co/9C3xTXAnBb

希望大家在 Fork 的同时可以随手点颗星🌟

需要注意的是：

1. 这套方案在本机调度，模型推理还是由各家自己的服务完成。需要准备 Codex，以及 Grok Build、Claude Code 的命令行客户端（CLI）。不知道怎么装的小伙伴没关系，可以把仓库链接交给自己的 Codex，让它按配置指南协助安装和检查，登录和授权由你本人完成。

2. 这套代码里，三个 AI 的小队长是 Codex，负责处理任务、分工、检查结果和交付，Claude 和 Grok 分别参与分析和复核。当前公开版围绕 Codex 主控设计，想让其他 AI 当队长还需要另外适配。

3. 小伙伴都喜欢用 BOT 了，这挺好的，但 BOT 直接是很难直接通话的，不是说不行，而是代价很高，比如我 ChatGPT 的 BOT 已经用了一个月了，堆积的内容太多了，如果用外部的 BOT 去访问，就要拉所有内容，Grok 的统计每一次交互需要 数百万的 Token 。

所以最好的方法就是在 ChatGPT 和 Grok 两者 BOT 的云电脑上登录对方的页面，比如在 ChatGPT BOT 的电脑中登录 Grok ，以及在 Grok BOT 的电脑中登录 ChatGPT 。

这样的方式就可以非要有效的让两者互相联系，并且互相传文件都可以。

4. 因为是通过 CLI 的命令执行的，所以每个 AI 都有一定的限制，如果同时开多个任务的话，可能协助执行的另外两个 AI 会超时，这是在所难免的。

5. 目前我绑定的系统中 Grok 配置的是 grok-4.7，推理强度是 xhigh ，Claude 配置的是 Fable-5.1，推理强度是 medium 。这是可以换的，如果觉得有问题可以自己和 AI 对话更换就行了。

6. 公开版通过 MCP 把协作工具接入 Codex，安装后服务名称以 ai_team_ 开头，后面带一个随机编号。公开版提供了全局协作规则模板，可以按你的选择合并到现有规则，让之后的聊天在具备工具和权限时尝试协作。不想用了，可以停用对应连接。

7. 这一套完成以后我就开始准备接入 Muse ，很多小伙伴在问我如何接入了，我已经开始工作了，而且 Muse 也是有 BOT 的，操作更简单一些。

8. 多 AI 协作相信我，非常非常非常有用，尤其在大项目的时候，AI 经常会跑偏，这时候就需要提醒 AI 回到正确的路上，而且在幻觉这方面，起码我还没有见到同一个文件两个不同 AI 都会幻觉的可能，尤其是我还配置了三个，但也因为多 AI 协作，所以任务的执行会更慢一些，不过准确率和成功率不可同日而语。

9. 你们都知道怎么联系我，任何需要维护的或者是添加一些新功能，可以和我说。AI 协同工作可能才是最大化解放人的可能。

text:
Your AI agent hit its usage limit before lunch again.

You're probably running your most expensive model on everything, including the part that only decides what to do next.

Top builders split the work instead:
•⁠  ⁠Main chat: a fast, cheap model. Its only job is to read the request and pass it on, like a receptionist
•⁠  ⁠Each task: a strong model, working in its own thread
•⁠  ⁠Harder task = stronger model. Easy task = cheap one

Two more tricks that save a lot:
1.⁠ ⁠When you come back to an old chat, don't resend the whole history. Send the last few messages and let it search for the rest
2.⁠ ⁠Compress a long conversation just before its cache expires (around minute 50 of 60), not after

Vercel's CEO does the reverse: the smart model plans and fast models do the work. Either way, the rule is the same. Never pay genius rates for receptionist work.

🇨🇭 瑞士首只直接持有比特币的 ETF 获批，背后是亚洲加密集团 BIT @BITofficial_CN 

美国有贝莱德 IBIT，如今瑞士也迎来首只直接持有比特币的 ETF——BBIT。令人关注的是，拿下这一产品的并非传统欧美资管巨头，而是总部位于新加坡、前身为 Matrixport 的 BIT 集团。

10 月 20 日，BIT 旗下瑞士资管子公司 BIT Asset Management AG 获 FINMA 批准推出 BBIT，计划于 11 月在瑞士证券交易所 SIX 上市。从 2025 年 4 月提交申请到最终获批，历时约一年半。

BBIT 的核心竞争力在于瑞士基金结构：比特币资产与管理公司自有资产隔离，由瑞士银行 AMINA 托管，每日披露持仓，并支持符合条件的 BTC 实物申购。相比债务型 ETP，基金结构为投资者提供了不同的资产隔离与法律保障安排。

这次获批并非偶然。BIT 在 2024 年收购了拥有多年瑞士加密资管经验、早在 2018 年便取得 FINMA 资管牌照的 Crypto Fund AG，承接其持牌主体、团队和产品运营经验，最终成为首家拿下该类产品批准的机构。

更值得关注的是 BIT 的业务布局：一边通过 BBIT 将比特币引入传统财富管理账户，一边推进美股、港股交易、黄金代币 XAUm 和瑞士机构托管，试图打通传统金融与数字资产之间的双向通道。

瑞士拥有庞大的跨境私人财富和成熟的私人银行体系。对 BBIT 而言，获批只是第一步，能否进入私人银行、家族办公室和养老金机构的配置名单，才决定它能否真正打开欧洲传统资金市场。

这次拿下瑞士首只直接持有比特币 ETF 的不是华尔街巨头，而是一家从亚洲出发、依靠瑞士资管积累切入传统金融的加密集团。

text:
it's time for you to wake up and smell the roses

there is no reality in which things continue smooth from here. no, bitcoin obviously isn't/wasn't going to stay put in some $70k - 80k range.

this is one of the most volatile eras ever. not just for bitcoin, but for the world. geopolitically, technologically, socially, we're going through rapid and dramatic change, and things aren't about to get simpler.

no, cybersecurity isn't going to all get fixed because you can now use ai to generate machine-checked security proofs in lean. even if you figure out how to write secure code and democratize the skill, there will still be vulnerabilities. if not bugs in the implementation, bugs in the specification. bugs in the assumptions, bugs in the verification.

cybersecurity will continue to be a verifiable domain, that's not changing, which means machines can self-play in it, meaning they can improve in it like in chess, except its actually worse than in chess because here the rules also keep changing, because technology keeps changing, so the gamefield keeps changing, meaning bugs will continue to be problematic, and especially problematic in irreversible systems (where one mistake means you get fully wiped out forever).

it's a hard system to keep stable! lean isn't coming to save you.

you'll continue to hear stories about how cybersecurity is about to improve and all the world's bugs will be fixed, because that is a popular narrative that tends to do well on twitter. no one wants to hear the defeatist point of view. but that means that some of you, who aren't able to figure this stuff out on your own, won't hear the truth very often.

smart people know this, not everyone agrees about it of course, but the negative point of view isn't going to get promoted on x/twitter.

the algorithms that are improving your life are about to learn how to improve themselves. the algorithms that are fucking with your life are about to learn how to improve themselves.

the situation now in which technology is about to enter a supersonic self-improving loop (a much more aggressive form than the baseline self-improving loop that we've been riding on since the dawn of time) is extremely bubble prone. 

the prospect of investing in something *self-improving*? people will leverage themselves to the tits.

they will also be scared, flip-flop between being endlessly optimistic to extremely skittish and want security/safety. markets will be volatile. geopolitics will be volatile. everyone has the ability to react faster now, and there will be much more to react to.

no, crypto and bitcoin isn't going to stay non-volatile to that backdrop. the risk asset of risk assets, not even gold stays untroubled during turbulent times. it's going to be volatile. we spent a decade maturing as an industry. yes, we think we are owed some overdue maturity. we've aged through our teenage years and we're supposed to get rid of the acne. sorry, we're aging backwards now, you're going to get more acne and more bedtime erections, not less. the world isn't fair.

what you need to understand and accept is that bitcoin & crypto isn't this solid thing here. it's more of a moonshot thing again. it's a very digital thing in a world where everything digital is getting a shakedown.

you're almost 40 years old and your digital profession can be done by free open source software made in china run with a handcrank. your wife isn't going to let you gamble with your entire financial future in magical coins when you can't even tell her what your career prospects look like anymore. your beard is patchy.

bitcoin & crypto can still do well in this environment, because when technology, markets and geopolitics become ultra-volatile in unison, you're bound to also get weird market dislocations. you have arms races, you have bubbles popping, you might get lots of money printing. most things that can happen will happen.

but you aren't, as an industry, going to be a universal safe haven against this. no one really feels safe with their crypto assets these days. you got a hardware wallet? cool. that doesn't exactly feel like the safest of all places anymore.

you got your funds on an exchange? cool. doesn't feel great either, does it?

oh, but you're not impacted because you choose to hold your exposure through etps/etfs? well, if that's what you have to resolve to, that's not great either.

if you can't be secure with your crypto, if you can't feel safe with it, even though you're a freaking nerd in this industry, how does that bode for the industry at large?

much of the fuel that has driven e.g. defi to where it is today is because the risk was seen as tolerable. during 2020-2022 i knew a lot of people who felt okay with locking in hundreds of thousands of dollars in stablecoins in yield protocols. i don't know people who enjoy doing that today. people are tired of being bug bounties for north korea. they honestly prefer reversible systems for their life earnings.

this doesn't mean it is over for bitcoin & crypto, but it means you're going to have to accept that you may have to think about it differently. it is a diversified bet in your overall portfolio. it is a part of your portfolio. it can't be your entire portfolio.

if this sounds so bearish it sounds like the bottom signal to fully re-enter the market, sure. i'd love to become the pico-bottom perma-joke of our industry. i'm not saying for you to grow out of crypto, i'm saying for you to think of this as the volatile bet it is, the bet that macroeconomic/geopolitic turbulence/dislocations & fiat printing will outrank the fact that we're back in our teenage years again.

embrace that it will be volatile.

what's happening in the markets now is normal.

While Spark Savings USDT (currently paying 4.25%) shines for institutional allocators, in the increasingly volatile crypto market it's starting to be a better and better fit for medium-sized traders and shops that want to park a few million USDT with a very high certainty that their funds will be there when they need to recall them the most.

Perhaps more importantly, they will not be exposed to a leveraged tokenised hedge fund trade that introduces acute tail risk that might make them lose a good chunk of their principal should some of the risks of the underlying crystallise.

Spark Savings USDT is an institutional yield product, operating under the SKY umbrella and managed by the Spark allocator system.

The primary mandate of the product is liquidity. This is why the standard 'redeem/withdraw' function fell short for the type of clients we aim to service. Because we regularly need to service 100s of millions in no-notice withdrawals, the Spark system splits withdrawals into two:

- Small withdrawals (under 5M): they get processed instantly from the 4626 reserve

- Larger withdrawals: 5M+: Should there not be enough liquidity in the 4626, a withdrawal intent is submitted.

When an intent is submitted, a user signals their desire to exit and the Spark allocator system starts recalling liquidity to service it (raising rates, unwinding positions and swapping to USDT) until it meets the requested amount.

Since launch small withdrawals have all been immediately processed with 0 downtime.

Large withdrawals averaged 86M clip size and median time to fill was 1.4 minutes.

Spark Savings USDT is the best USDT product in the market for two key reasons.

1. Unique access to SKY balance sheet. This allows Spark to access scalable above-SOFR yield and the capability to tap into on-demand capital to satisfy liquidity requirements

2. Infrastructure edge. Smart contracts with strict rate limits and timelocks under SKY governance provide guarantees to depositors, which, paired with our sophisticated allocator system, makes for a superior USDT product that's hard to replicate elsewhere. 

Even if you the reader most probably will not be pulling 100M+ at a time (hopefully you are, if so please feel free to DM), knowing that this is a possibility and that the system was built in a way to structurally serve liquidity much in excess of your needs should give you the peace of mind you need to get some decent yield while you wait to deploy capital in whatever type of risk your heart desires when it presents itself.

The articles backtracked from their original incendiary, and now clearly false, claims to something more like "Jensen did lawful things that powerful people didn't like". It still appears the original claims came from a single competing Big Tech lobbyist.

The reporting successfully disrupted corporate governance processes, with a running cost of $1.8 trillion in losses to American pension funds and shareholders.

Here's what I fear is being lost in these articles: The proper interface between government and private citizens and their corporations is rule of law. Laws are passed, and if wrongdoing as alleged, then there's due process: an investigation followed by facts and evidence presented in open court. Due process should happen here: let the facts come out whole, and not as a trickle of dubious claims.

Press takedowns full of sketchily sourced claims and backtracking narratives are not the way. It's what we see outside of the free world, and is no model for The United States of America.

In particular, if the Jensen takedown succeeds on the basis of these journalistic failings, which is not by any means certain as Sam Altman's case shows, then it foreshadows an economically and institutionally ruinous new playbook to be adopted with no end in sight.

Imagine a weekly stream of takedowns emerging from opportunistic alignments between corporate lobbyists and political interests which, given the new partisan split between the executive and legislative branches, will attack in all directions, undermining not only the US economy but American leadership in the world.

I hope cooler heads prevail this coming week as they did not on Thursday November 12. And I urge anyone who happened to oppose Jensen, open models, and the underlying trade policies in question, to recognize that this isn't a win for "team regulation". It's a change in the game from a transparent rules-based one to a sinister new form centered around politicans and lobbyists.

text:
Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.

text:
How do you actually get your money out of a tokenized fund?

$USTB is a good example. Its redemption process combines three layers:

1. An onchain buffer

A smart contract holds up to ~$10M in USDC, allowing smaller redemptions to settle instantly. Return your USTB tokens and receive $USDC in the same transaction. The available balance is publicly verifiable onchain.

2. Fund-level redemptions

Larger requests are handled by the fund itself. Redemptions are processed twice daily, usually settling the same day, with T+2 as the maximum. The portfolio holds short-term US Treasury bills with an average maturity of around one month, providing a steady stream of maturities converting back into cash.

3. A credit line from Invesco

Behind the buffer, a credit line from the fund manager pre-funds instant redemptions. As with most funds of this type, redemptions can still be paused or limited in extreme conditions, though this mechanism has never been needed.

The result: instant exits for smaller amounts, fund-level settlement for larger ones, and a short-dated portfolio supporting both.

We hold USTB in primeUSD.

text:
市场太不景气了，昨天各个群里流传的一个PDF 小作文刚让人吃了一波瓜解闷

下午当事机构也发文否认了相关指控。事情本身明显夹杂着大量情绪与纠葛，但围绕加密金融平台的内部治理、合规宣传以及资金安全，还是发酵出了不少争议

——比如香港资管机构是否真安全、资金会不会被内部挪用、香港的加密上市公司是不是要批量塌方

这些顾虑也能理解，投资者最怕的是“人的不可控”（管理层道德风险、挪用资金），把钱交给人管，永远要赌人性；

而真正的香港合规资管，正是用“制度锁死人性”，把个人风险与客户资产彻底物理隔离；把钱交给香港持牌机构管，你信任的是香港的法律与银行托管体系

长期以来，市场有一种声音，嫌弃香港持牌机构“太慢、太保守、缺乏活力”

但金融的本质是风险定价。在草莽时代，野蛮生长意味着随时可能暴雷；而在香港SFC的框架下，“增长缓慢”的背面是极高的试错成本与严苛的准入门槛

稍微了解一下香港持牌资管制度（如SFC第9号牌照及VA升级牌照框架下），就知道真正的香港合规资管公司，是严格执行客户资产隔离（Segregated Account）与独立第三方持牌托管。资管公司仅有交易指令权，绝对无法触碰或划转客户本金至关联方。

在无畏来看，像Hashkey和OSL这样代表性的合规交易所，在SFC监管下几乎把冷热钱包分离做到了极致，基本上可以说是牺牲效率换取安全的模范生了。这一点，相信曾经在两个所进行过大额提币的人深有感触

在资管方面，合规资质和安全口碑最好的香港持牌上市公司新火集团，前段时间资管规模正式突破20亿港币了，一年前这个数字只有不到2亿港币，这证明在香港这个高合规市场坚持原则稳步推进也可以有很好的增长和发展机会

潮水退去时，大家才看清谁在裸泳，谁在穿救生衣。香港合规体系看似门槛高、节奏慢，实则是在帮市场做筛选：

留下真正愿意按规矩办事的长期玩家。当行业从“拼胆子”转向“拼制度与风控”，那些笨功夫，就会成为最硬的护城河

현재 중화권에서 퍼지고 있는 Amber Group 폭로 정리

1. 보통 Amber Group 하면 VC나 MM으로 알고 있는데, 고객 코인을 맡아 Fixed Earn 같은 이자 상품으로 굴려주는 자산관리 앱 Amber Premium(옛 WhaleFin)도 운영함. 원문의 고발장은 전부 이 Amber Premium 고객 자금에 대해 폭로하고 있음.

2. 어젯밤 Amber 관련 11페이지짜리 내부고발 문서가 중국 위챗 단톡방들에 돌았음. (원문에 참조된 이미지) 작성자는 본인이 Amber 전직 임원이라고 하고, 자료를 중국 기율위, 홍콩 ICAC, 홍콩 SFC, 홍콩 경찰에 이미 넘겼다고 주장. (고발자 일방 주장이고 아직 검증된 건 없음)

3. 제일 파급이 큰 주장은 공동창업자 Tony He가 고객 자금 $10M대를 빼서 후오비(HTX)에서 개인 트레이딩을 하다가 계좌가 동결됐다는 것. 즉 내부관리 문제를 떠나서 고객 자산 안전 문제로 직행될 수 있는 문제.

4. 고객이 Amber에 입금하던 계좌의 수취인 주소가 회사가 아니라 공동창업자 Wayne의 홍콩 집 주소였다고 함 (수취 계좌 캡쳐까지 첨부). 고객 돈은 원래 회사 자산과 분리된 수탁 계좌에 들어가야 하는데, 수취인이 개인 주소로 잡혀 있으면 돈이 회사 것인지 개인 것인지 경계가 흐려려지기에 고객이 돈을 돌려받을 수 있는 상환 자체에 문제가 생길수도 있음.

5. Amber 그룹은 MM 핵심 인력이 나간 뒤 돈 버는 능력이 사라지자, 안정적인 이자 상품인 줄 알고 들어온 Fixed Earn 고객 돈을 MM 고위험 운용이나 RWA로 포장한 동남아 무담보 대출에 굴렸다는 게 고발장 주장. (실제로 운용에서 손실이 나면 고객 손실로 그대로 돌아옴)

6. 또 처음 공동창업자가 6명이었는데 1명은 사망, 3명은 퇴사해서 지금 2명만 남았다고 함. 짧은 기간 안에 창업자 절반 이상이 빠졌다는 건 내부에 큰 문제가 있었을 수 있는 신호라고 주장.

7. 대주주 Shen Bo(沈波)의 약 $300M이 Amber에 묶여 있고, 이걸 빼면 Amber가 파산할 수준이라고 함. 맞다면 Amber 유동성이 한 사람 돈에 기대고 있다는 얘기라, 그 돈이 빠지는 순간 일반 고객의 출금까지 막힐 수 있음.

8. Amber가 홍콩·싱가포르·두바이 세 곳 허가를 다 가진 것처럼 홍보했는데 거짓이고, 중국 본토 고객한테 해외 주소 증명을 위조해주고 위안화를 USDT로 바꿔주는 불법 환전까지 도왔다고 함. 중국에선 외환관리 위반으로 형사 처벌까지 갈 수 있는 사안.

9. 베이징 공무원 가족이 Amber 계좌에 수백만 달러를 보유하고 있다고 함. 출처 확인 없이 받은 돈이라면 고객 확인(KYC)과 자금세탁방지가 제대로 안 됐다는 얘기라 규제기관이 제일 민감하게 보는 부분.

10. 여기부터는 원문 작성자가 고발장 내용들을 공개 자료로 확인한 내용. 26년 6월 말 기준 Amber International 총자산 약 $298M, 총부채 약 $195M으로 자본은 아직 플러스. 대신 상반기 매출이 YoY 약 28% 줄었고 흑자에서 적자로 돌아섬. 돈 버는 능력이 떨어졌다는 5번 주장과 매칭됨.

11. 같은 재무제표에서 관계사 Earn 상품에 넣은 무담보 대출이 약 $57.8M으로 25년 말 대비 약 37% 늘었고, 못 받을 경우를 대비한 충당금은 0인 상태. 즉 관계사가 갚지 못한다면 담보가 없으니 $57.8M 을 회수할 방법이 없고 Amber의 자본 $103M중 절반이 날라갈 수 있는 상태.

12. 실제로 홍콩 지부에는 허가가 나지 않았음. 24년에 신청만 해두고 심사 대기 상태로 영업하다가 올해 10월에 스스로 철회함. 싱가포르 지부는 결제업체 인수로 얻은 결제 허가, 두바이 지부는 26년 4월에 받은 기관·고액 투자자 한정 허가뿐. 세 곳 다 정식 허가가 있다는 홍보는 부풀려졌다는게 맞다고 함.

=> 
고발 내용은 아직 일방 주장이라 좀 지켜봐야 하겠지만, 공개 재무랑 허가 상황이 일부 주장과 겹치는 게 찝찝하네요.

Amber가 해당 고발에 대해 제대로 해명을 못 하면 규제 조사, 나스닥 상장사로서 공시 이슈, Amber Premium 고객 출금 러시까지 이어질 수 있고, 이렇게 되면 Amber가 MM을 돌리고 있던 중소형 알트의 호가도 얇아지게 되면서 어느정도 크립토 시장에도 꽤 영향이 갈 수도 있을듯. 

물론 총자산 약 $298M 규모라 시장 전체가 흔들릴 급은 아니지만 좀 지켜보긴 해야겠네요.

quoted_text:
Amber，又一个爆雷的公司？

昨晚，一份关于 Amber 的 11 页举报信在微信群里疯传。

举报人自称是 Amber 前高管，并声称已经将相关材料提交给中央纪委、香港廉政公署、香港证监会及香港警方。

这份举报信的内容相当劲爆，涉及联合创始人涉嫌挪用客户资金、管理层利益输送、客户入金账户异常，以及 Amber Premium 的 Fixed Earn 产品存在资金运作风险等问题。

需要说明的是，目前这些内容主要来自举报人的单方面陈述，相关指控尚未得到独立证实。笔者结合举报信和 Amber 已披露的公开资料，按照问题的重要性，梳理了以下几个值得关注的疑问。

1、最严重的一项指控，究竟是否真实？

根据举报信，Amber 联合创始人 Tony He 曾挪用千万美元客户资金，在火币进行个人交易，最终导致相关账户被冻结。

如果这一指控属实，问题就不只是内部管理失当，而是涉及客户资产安全的重大事件。

但目前举报信中的说法，还需要交易记录、资金流向、账户归属以及相关调查结果来验证。

Amber 需要回答：客户资金是否曾被挪用于未经授权的个人交易？如果发生过，涉及多少资金？

2、Amber 的创始团队，究竟发生了什么？

根据举报信，Amber 最初有 6 位联合创始人，其中 1 人已经离世，另有 3 人离开，目前只剩下 2 位。

如果举报信所述属实，Amber 的创始团队为何出现如此大规模的人员变动？六位联合创始人目前的实际情况、股权变化，以及核心管理层离职的真实原因是什么？

3、沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？

举报信声称，Amber 股东沈波有约 3 亿美元资金存放在 Amber，并且曾经出售部分股权。

这件事至少需要拆成两个问题：

第一，沈波是否真的在 Amber 存放了 3 亿美元？这笔资金究竟属于个人资产、客户托管资产，还是其他形式的投资或借贷？

第二，如果这笔资金确实存在，沈波是否有权随时提取？如果集中提取，是否会对 Amber 的流动性造成重大影响？

需要强调的是，目前没有公开证据能够证实这 3 亿美元的说法，更不能据此推断沈波提款就会导致 Amber 破产。

4、Amber 是否真的存在爆雷风险？

先看公开财务数据。

截至 2026 年 6 月底，Amber International 的公开财报显示，公司总资产约 2.98 亿美元，总负债约 1.95 亿美元，仍然拥有正的股东权益。但与此同时，2026 年上半年，公司营收同比下降约 28%，并由盈利转为亏损。

另一个值得关注的数据是：截至 2026 年 6 月底，公司的加密资产贷款应收款约为 5,779 万美元，较 2025 年底增长约 37%。

根据财报披露，这些贷款来自集团认购关联方数字资产平台的 Earn 产品，属于无抵押贷款，期限从 2 天到 365 天不等。截至报告期末，公司没有为这部分贷款计提信用损失准备。

这并不能证明客户资金被挪用，也不能直接说明公司存在偿付危机，但它确实引出了一个重要问题：Amber 的资金究竟流向了哪里？相关借款方是谁？如果借款方无法按期偿还，公司是否有足够的流动性应对客户赎回？

5、Amber 是否拥有香港、新加坡和迪拜三地牌照？

这也是一个容易被混淆的问题。三个地区的牌照性质并不相同。

香港：尚未取得正式 VATP 牌照。

Amber 旗下 Whalefin Markets Limited 曾于 2024 年向香港证监会申请虚拟资产交易平台牌照，并在过渡安排下被视为获发牌申请人。

但这不等于正式获牌。2026 年 10 月，Amber International 公告称，Whalefin 将不再推进相关牌照申请，并计划撤回申请；相关收购安排也不再推进。

新加坡：拥有 MPI 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber 旗下的 Sparrow Tech Private Limited，获新加坡金融管理局（MAS）颁发 Major Payment Institution（主要支付机构）牌照，获准提供数字支付代币服务（DPT Services）。

迪拜：拥有 VASP 牌照。

持牌主体是 Amber Premium FZE。迪拜虚拟资产监管局（VARA）于 2026 年 4 月 2 日正式向其发放牌照，允许其开展虚拟资产经纪交易、资产管理与投资、借贷服务。不过，牌照限定服务机构投资者和合格投资者。

所以，更准确地说，Amber 已在新加坡和迪拜取得相关数字资产业务牌照，但并未取得香港 VATP 牌照。

一份举报信，不足以证明 Amber 即将爆雷。

但是，这份举报信已经在社交媒体上广泛传播。对于一家管理客户数字资产、提供收益产品的公司而言，Amber 的确需要正面回答几个关键问题：

客户资金是否曾被挪用？客户资产是否实现独立托管？用户购买 Fixed Earn 产品后，钱究竟被拿去做了什么？举报信中提到的关联方资金往来，以及与北京公职人员有关的数百万美元资产，究竟是否属实？

这些问题，Amber 都应该给出明确的解释。

text:
A few hours ago, we discussed whether Jensen Huang’s return to NVIDIA would affect $Jacket. But in this article, I want to focus primarily on $microduck.

0xd5f1afea47b1a9eab414d2ee740cf1d6d039e725 

I believe Jensen Huang’s return to NVIDIA would have an impact on MICRODUCK, with a positive effect on its short-term narrative. However, I want to look at this from two separate perspectives: Huang’s return could amplify Microduck’s exposure again, but what truly determines its long-term value is whether NVIDIA continues pushing Physical AI and whether Microduck can gain access to more product and developer resources as a result.

If Jensen Huang does return, I see three potential benefits for Microduck.

First, Microduck could regain direct exposure through NVIDIA’s leadership.

Previously, Jensen Huang brought four Microducks onto the stage at GTC Berlin and then proactively mentioned the group on X. This shows that Microduck has already become a highly shareable product example in NVIDIA’s Physical AI demonstrations.

If Huang returns to the CEO position, the possibility of him hosting future GTC events and showcasing robots and AI technologies could increase. If Microduck continues to participate in these demonstrations, it could once again attract attention from global technology media and social media platforms.

This type of exposure is particularly important for MICRODUCK because the token itself has no independent product revenue. A significant part of what the market is trading is the attention generated by the real-world robot.

Second, expectations surrounding the integration of NVIDIA and Hugging Face could become stronger.

This relationship is especially worth watching:

Pollen Robotics was acquired by Hugging Face in 2025.

NVIDIA signed an agreement in September 2026 to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

If Huang returns, he could once again become the central figure driving this strategic direction.

For Microduck, the potential benefit would go beyond simply getting another opportunity to appear on stage. It could have a chance to become more deeply integrated into NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation, robotics training, and developer ecosystem.

If Hugging Face’s LeRobot, Pollen’s hardware, and NVIDIA’s computing resources eventually form real synergies, Microduck could attract more developer usage and generate greater content exposure.

Third, the Physical AI narrative could regain a more influential figure to amplify its reach.

Jensen Huang has always been one of the most important public communicators of NVIDIA’s technology roadmap.

Microduck’s advantage is that it can turn the abstract concept of Physical AI into something ordinary people can understand at a glance: a small duck that can walk, grasp objects, and learn movements.

Compared with complex industrial robots, it is much easier to film, share, and remix into new content.

If Huang returns and continues promoting this direction, Microduck could become a recurring character in NVIDIA’s demonstrations rather than just a one-time guest at GTC.

On the other hand, even if Jensen Huang does not return, it would not directly undermine Microduck’s long-term thesis.

The reason is that NVIDIA’s Physical AI business is not something that depends entirely on Huang personally to operate.

On October 21, NVIDIA still announced major expansions to its Isaac robotics development platform, including new robotics reference designs, datasets, and simulation training tools.

In its announcement regarding Huang’s departure, NVIDIA’s board also made it clear that the company’s operations, customer commitments, and product roadmap would continue without interruption despite the leadership transition.

So even if Huang does not return, Microduck can still develop through the developer ecosystem of Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face.

The main difference is that it would lose an extremely influential communicator, meaning its opportunities to attract external attention might be less concentrated.

However, I am actually more concerned about two other issues.

First, NVIDIA’s acquisition of Hugging Face has not yet been completed. The US Department of Justice has already made inquiries into the deal’s potential impact on competition in the AI market, so regulatory approval remains uncertain. Even if Huang returns, that would not directly resolve the regulatory issues.

Second, Microduck must prove that it is a product people genuinely use. Whether the first batch of robots can be delivered as scheduled, whether developers are willing to keep training new movements, and whether users can create a large volume of content are the factors that will ultimately determine the foundation for its long-term exposure.

If Microduck ends up being showcased by Huang a few times but fails to build a lasting user and developer ecosystem, its narrative lifecycle will still be limited.

The combination that is truly worth looking forward to is:

Jensen Huang returns and Microduck regains access to NVIDIA’s public showcase platform.

NVIDIA successfully completes its acquisition of Hugging Face.

There is also an interesting corporate connection. Microduck was developed by Pollen Robotics, which was acquired by Hugging Face in 2025. In September 2026, NVIDIA signed an agreement to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion, with the deal expected to close in the first half of 2027.

NVIDIA needs to show the market that its AI technology can do more than generate content. Through simulation, training, and model deployment, it wants to demonstrate how AI can control robots in the physical world. Microduck has effectively become a real-world example of NVIDIA’s Physical AI workflow.

Developers can also use it to explore motion control, reinforcement learning, and Sim-to-Real techniques. In theory, combining Hugging Face’s open-source model community with NVIDIA’s simulation and computing tools could create an ecosystem that connects model development with real-world hardware testing.

So, on the surface, it was simply Jensen Huang bringing four Microducks onto the stage during his NVIDIA GTC Berlin keynote, followed by a post on X joking that he had been the opening act for a family of ducks.

But the potential value to NVIDIA goes beyond a small robot. It lies in the synergy between robotics hardware, the developer community, and Physical AI technology.

For now, there are three things worth watching: whether the acquisition is successfully completed, whether the first batch of Microducks is delivered on schedule, and whether the product can genuinely attract sustained developer engagement.

As for MICRODUCK, it needs new events to keep generating market attention. NVIDIA needs Microduck to demonstrate the real-world potential of Physical AI, while the Meme market needs a steady stream of interesting Microduck-related developments that people want to talk about and share.

When these two narratives converge, that could be the catalyst for the next major move on the chart.

text:
Lighter 疑似 2 个做市商账户 API 密钥泄露，约 1,550 万美元 USDC 被异常转移

11 月 16 日，据社区反馈，永续 DEX @Lighter_xyz 已暂停取款。此前，链上分析师 MLM 提示平台疑似遭遇安全事件，但强调尚不能百分之百确认。

一位韩国社区人士提出了另一种解释：这可能并非协议本身遭到黑客攻击，而是 两个大型做市商账户的 API 密钥疑似泄露。

按照该分析，攻击者先关闭受害账户的仓位，随后利用受害者账户创建一个零手续费公共池，仅投入约 1 万美元便获得约 99.99% 的池份额，再将受害账户中的 USDC 分批转入池中并赎回。

这一操作可能利用了 Lighter 的账户权限设计：API 密钥本身无法直接向外部地址转账，但同一 L1 地址下的账户之间转账无需额外签名；而由受害者账户创建的池，也被系统视为其关联账户。

该分析称，涉事资金合计约 1,550 万美元，分别来自账户 #714710 的 1,039 万美元，以及账户 #714723 的 509 万美元。

此前，MLM 提供的链上地址显示，其中一笔约 1,039 万 USDC 于今日 18:11 从 Lighter 转出，随后通过 CoW Protocol 分四笔兑换为 ETH。

目前，这一解释仍属于社区分析，Lighter 尚未公布正式调查结论，API 密钥是否泄露、相关账户权限机制是否被利用，均有待平台确认。

text:
Most likely, someone got hold of the victim’s Lighter API key

An API key can trade, but sending funds to another owner’s account also needs the owner’s main wallet (L1) sig and the same goes for withdrawals, So the attacker couldn’t just transfer the money out directly

Instead, they used a public pool A pool counts as a sub-account of its creator, so the victim’s key could move funds into it. The attacker then bought almost all the pool’s shares (about 99.99%) from a separate account. Whoever owns the shares gets the money when they burn them, so the funds went to the attacker.

So this looks like an attack on a single account, not a drain of Lighter’s contract or main liquidity pool (not official just my assessment)

text:
最近看到不少人在研究 Kraken 的 Anthropic 打新，这种机会不想错过，至少得先把功课做了

于是搭了一个简单模型，看看参考现在的盘前市场，这次打新究竟有多少利润空间👇

先说一个不确定的地方：最后能分到多少额度，现在还算不出来

官方说明是由承销商根据需求决定，可能按比例或类似方式分配，但没有公布能直接计算个人获配金额的明确公式，也不是先到先得

公开页面里我也没查到实时认购总额，因此不能拿以前某次打新的超募倍数直接套过来

所以换个角度，先不猜投入多少钱能分到多少，就假设最终获配了 1,000 U，看看这部分能赚多少

目前公布的发行价区间是 $70–78，模型暂按上限 $78 计算，加上 Kraken 的 5% 价差，每份成本是 $81.90，这里的 1,000 U 已经包含这笔价差

如果做套利还有个必须要考虑的问题

不同 Perp DEX 的报价口径不一样，像 Entropy 和 Lighter 的盘前报价反映的是公司估值，不能把各家的合约价格直接相除，所以图里统一换成估值来比较

算式其实很简单：

利润 ≈ 1,000 U ×［卖出时估值 ÷（发行估值 × 1.05）－1］

按图中暂估股本换算，发行估值约为 1.365 万亿美元，股本和发行价都还要等最终确定

配图采集了北京时间 11 月 9 日 16:00 至 11 月 16 日 16:00 的行情，以小时收盘价的平均值作为参考，假设上市后能按对应估值卖出：

- TradeXYZ：平均估值约 1.786 万亿美元，利润约 246 U，收益率约 24.6%

- Entropy：平均估值约 1.763 万亿美元，利润约 230 U，收益率约 23.0%

- Lighter：平均估值约 1.756 万亿美元，利润约 226 U，收益率约 22.6%

也就是获配成本 1,000 U，对应卖出金额约 1,226–1,246 U，图里还放了过去 7 天高低点对应的测算，方便看不同价格下的差别

如果真能按这些估值卖出，这个差价空间确实挺可观，不过这里的收益率只对应获配的部分，不能当成全部申购资金的收益率

People screenshot their PnL. Share their bets. Argue about trades in group chats. Ask friends before they buy anything.

WeChat proved it over a decade ago. 

Chat and payments in one place, and nobody wanted to go back.

text:
周末看了篇文章，叫《一座短剧之都的魔幻一年》，很有意思

看的我感觉 - 有点像一个被AI加速的币圈

以前我们常说，币圈几年把华尔街过去几十年的东西全都跑完了

现在AI把影视/短剧行业以更快速的方式过了一遍

我挑几个片段扔上来大家感受一下

“
4月，AI短剧刚刚起量，市场上懂生成工具的人很少，她的团队很快做出一部播放量过亿的AI仿真人短剧，公司最多时扩张到120人

到了七八月，莹姐发现，自己越来越难判断一部AI短剧能不能赚钱。一部系列剧的第一部获得1800多万播放、约20万收藏，收入接近30万元。她沿用相近的制作标准做了第二部，剧本、剪辑和算力都没有降级，最终却只获得七八万播放，收入300多元。

同一个系列，两部作品的收入相差近千倍。”

“崩坏了，我们经常说崩坏了，不知道怎么弄了。”

“上半年抖音端AI漫剧播放量破亿的作品不到千分之五，达到盈亏平衡参考线的只有1.3%，换句话说，平均每77部新剧，只有1部能够达到这一参考线。”

“2026年9月，抖音端原生AI剧漫剧新剧达到5.18万部，播放增量超过2093亿。不到1.5%的新剧，贡献了近三分之二的播放增量”

“短剧用三年跑完的长剧三十年的历程，AI三个月就跑完了”

经历过17-21年那波的老铁应该有印象，那会发个币是要一两年的，大家是以“上主网”为重要指标

后来发币对于科学家来说只需要5分钟，但是没有Cex上没有意义，直到Defi Summer那会Uniswap崛起，各种科学家发币开始泛滥起来

但想要发个链，还是一个大团队+几个月的工程量的活

然后我们有了RAAS（Rollup as A Service）, 一键发链，发链也变成一个一天能搞定的事儿

再后来我们有了https://t.co/c44EUlNZiu ，发币不再需要科学家，任何人都可以在5分钟之内发一个币出来

就像我之前在写魔兽 VS Web3 Game时写的“行为一旦可被规模化，就一定会被工业化”

币圈是个先例，现在短剧行业更快速的把这个过程跑完了，有意思的是，门槛塌缩之后发生的事，两边也差不多

工业化解决的是供给，不是结果。

Pump发币5分钟，99%归零；AI做剧三个月，77部只有1部回本。

甚至大家用在用AI，都在Vibe Coding，但绝大多数人注定是消费者，手搓出来的东西只能自己用，卖不出去一点

门槛归零之后，真正稀缺的会是啥 - 审美？判断？渠道？🤔

quoted_text:
市场太不景气了，昨天各个群里流传的一个PDF 小作文刚让人吃了一波瓜解闷

下午当事机构也发文否认了相关指控。事情本身明显夹杂着大量情绪与纠葛，但围绕加密金融平台的内部治理、合规宣传以及资金安全，还是发酵出了不少争议

——比如香港资管机构是否真安全、资金会不会被内部挪用、香港的加密上市公司是不是要批量塌方

这些顾虑也能理解，投资者最怕的是“人的不可控”（管理层道德风险、挪用资金），把钱交给人管，永远要赌人性；

而真正的香港合规资管，正是用“制度锁死人性”，把个人风险与客户资产彻底物理隔离；把钱交给香港持牌机构管，你信任的是香港的法律与银行托管体系

长期以来，市场有一种声音，嫌弃香港持牌机构“太慢、太保守、缺乏活力”

但金融的本质是风险定价。在草莽时代，野蛮生长意味着随时可能暴雷；而在香港SFC的框架下，“增长缓慢”的背面是极高的试错成本与严苛的准入门槛

稍微了解一下香港持牌资管制度（如SFC第9号牌照及VA升级牌照框架下），就知道真正的香港合规资管公司，是严格执行客户资产隔离（Segregated Account）与独立第三方持牌托管。资管公司仅有交易指令权，绝对无法触碰或划转客户本金至关联方。

在无畏来看，像Hashkey和OSL这样代表性的合规交易所，在SFC监管下几乎把冷热钱包分离做到了极致，基本上可以说是牺牲效率换取安全的模范生了。这一点，相信曾经在两个所进行过大额提币的人深有感触

在资管方面，合规资质和安全口碑最好的香港持牌上市公司新火集团，前段时间资管规模正式突破20亿港币了，一年前这个数字只有不到2亿港币，这证明在香港这个高合规市场坚持原则稳步推进也可以有很好的增长和发展机会

潮水退去时，大家才看清谁在裸泳，谁在穿救生衣。香港合规体系看似门槛高、节奏慢，实则是在帮市场做筛选：

留下真正愿意按规矩办事的长期玩家。当行业从“拼胆子”转向“拼制度与风控”，那些笨功夫，就会成为最硬的护城河

text: “Lighter 设计上最安全” https://t.co/MTwAHfXkox
author: hashcoin0
quoted_text:
外网一个博主在币安被盗后，从代码层面，对比了市面上 4 家主流 PerpDEX 的安全性与被盗可能，我通读了一下，总结为以下表格：

博主认为 Lighter 设计上最安全，就算黑客控制了 Lighter 的排序器，也最多只能操纵标的价格，无法控制你账户内的已有资产，你的资产只有你自己的私钥能转移，就算团队不管这项目，你也能通过以太坊主网撤离资产。

Hyperliquid 和 Aster 处于中间一档，因为单个私钥或合约控制了过多资产，且链和托管方对用户的资产转移有决定权。

其实我个人觉得 Hyperliquid 还好，首先攻击可能的顺序也是攻破 Coinbase 的托管钱包私钥，然后在 Hyperliquid 团队反应过来之前跨出去，还要不被 USDC 封控，这一系列下来就够呛，在 Hyperliquid 的各大节点闭源软件上做手脚更是不可能。

Aster 次之，因为 Aster 的服务器不知道有多少节点在运行，同时控制两把私钥，就可以像币安这次一样，把钱提光，但金额上限的设计，给予了充分的缓冲时间，

Variational 是最不安全的。17 把运营密钥任何一把都能把 USDC 从任何用户那里转走，合约提款也没有像 Aster 一样的金额上限设计。

整体来说，我觉得 PerpDEX 的安全性是要比 CEX 热钱包的形式安全一点，Lighter 借助以太坊的 ZK 证明，只有用户私钥能控制自己的钱，Hyperliquid 的节点管理和桥接控制，Aster 的提款金额上限，都是 DEX 预防安全的手段，Variational 可能要在安全方面多下点功夫，毕竟现在来看暴露较大，不过大家都会有  Circle 冻结和 Arbitrum 委员会出马兜底。

quoted_text:
With the growth of prediction markets, there's a lot of teams taking differing product directions and GTM approaches. 

I think the new prediction markets that succeed will focus on building great products that serve markets with common characteristics:

1) High leverage – users want to have high leverage or stack odds to increase payouts. Parlays. Perps. Intraday event markets. All of these prediction market products have potential to increase the demand for prediction market events.  

2) Highly frequent markets – market events that are more frequent can garner more betting and bring a more retentive user base. 

DraftKings and sports betting apps leverage DFS (daily fantasy sports) which are low leverage to increase retention and drive user behavior. 

3) High market outcome values – elections aren't that frequent but have high signal value. This draws lots of capital. These fat head markets are useful for driving open interest and volume even if they aren't super regular. Kalshi's climate markets are fairly frequent and there's signal in the aggregate value of their daily predictions. 

The prediction market wars have only begun.

Most likely, someone got hold of the victim’s Lighter API key

An API key can trade, but sending funds to another owner’s account also needs the owner’s main wallet (L1) sig and the same goes for withdrawals, So the attacker couldn’t just transfer the money out directly

Instead, they used a public pool A pool counts as a sub-account of its creator, so the victim’s key could move funds into it. The attacker then bought almost all the pool’s shares (about 99.99%) from a separate account. Whoever owns the shares gets the money when they burn them, so the funds went to the attacker.

So this looks like an attack on a single account, not a drain of Lighter’s contract or main liquidity pool (not official just my assessment)

text:
leanPCS is a total bull

I think the amount of use cases it will unlock is beyond what we can imagine today, and not having to go through the friction of convincing everyone we need to enshrine a new ISA is the best path forward.

EIP coming soon, stay tuned!
author: nero_eth
quoted_text:
Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.
 https://t.co/dUHONMh75g

text:
Program Goals:

•  Reduce the likelihood of compromise of accounts, keys, seed phrases, and internal processes due to the human factor.
•  Build sustainable OpSec habits among employees of different risk levels.
•  Verify real readiness through simulations, phishing tests, and OpSec pentests.

Stage 0. Diagnostics

•  Anonymous baseline survey and checklists (DNC + Consumer Reports Security Planner).
•  Collection of current practices: passwords, 2FA, devices, messengers, access to crypto services.
•  OSINT reconnaissance of the public footprint of key employees (only within the agreed scope).
•  Defining the threat model: phishing, SIM-swap, BEC, wallet substitution, insider, physical access, seed compromise.

Stage 1. Basic Device and Account Security

•  Unique long passwords + password manager;
•  Rejection of SMS-2FA, transition to authenticator apps / hardware keys (YubiKey and equivalents);
•  Disk encryption, OS and application updates, Find My Device;
•  Carrier PIN to protect against SIM-swap;
•  Separate browser profiles (work / crypto / personal);
•  Account backup and recovery.

Stage 2. OpSec as a Process

1.  What constitutes critical information (keys, seeds, signing processes, signer lists, payout schedules).
2.  Who is the threat and how they collect data (OSINT, social engineering, insider).
3.  Where leaks occur: conversations, social media, photos of screens, metadata, reuse of email/phone.
4.  Countermeasures: footprint minimization, role separation, need-to-know, escalation channels.
5.  How to measure risk rather than just “checking boxes.”

Stage 3. Crypto-OpSec

1.  Keys and Wallets Cold storage, hardware wallets, multisig, never store the seed in digital form, purchase devices only from the manufacturer, firmware verification.
2.  Transactions and Signing Verification of address, amount, network, and allowance; fake websites and malicious extensions; separate devices for signing.
3.  Communications Separate email/aliases, VPN, refusal to link crypto accounts to the primary phone number, secure messengers, ban on discussing operations in open chats.
4.  Physical Security Backup storage, travel, conferences, coercion, duress scenarios, workplace and “clean desk” policy.
5.  Insider Threat and Separation of Duties

Stage 4. Social Engineering, Phishing Tests, and Attack Simulations

4.1. Phishing tests
4.2. Attack simulations
4.3. OpSec pentest

Stage 5. Private 1:1 Sessions

@rickawsb 看好 $ANT 的三个理由：  
1. 营收增长与资本效率极强，GAAP 亏损具有误导性。 Rick 认为可转债、衍生负债与股权增值带来的公允价值损失，不等于真实经营支出。真正该看的是：投入一块钱资本，能创造多少新增收入和未来盈利。Anthropic 的增长效率罕见。 

 2. 市场用 Token／SaaS ARR 估值，可能低估了 Outcome（成果）的价值。
如果模型能直接交付新药、材料、芯片设计或科学发现，收入就不只是订阅费和 API 调用，而可能包括授权金、里程碑付款与权利金。成果的价值可能远高于生成它所需的 Token 成本。  

3. 闭源前沿模型与 RSI 飞轮可能形成长期护城河，$ANT 是稀缺的直接标的。
最强模型未必开放 API，实验室可以留着自己生产高价值 IP。若 Model → Chip → Fab → Energy → Compute 的循环成立，领先会制造更多领先。Anthropic 上市让投资人第一次能直接持有纯 Frontier Model 资产，不必只通过 GPU、内存或云厂商间接下注。  

不过我有一个问题： 你的三層是模型吃應用、算力吃模型、然後 Model → Chip → Fab → Energy 閉環。

但你舉完成閉環的例子是馬斯克。Anthropic 沒有自己的 Chip、Fab、Energy，算力是跟 Amazon、Google、SpaceX 租的，還要付大約 37% 的雲渠道費。

text:
Here's a strange finding from long-context research:

You can make information harder for a model to retrieve without removing or changing it.

Just move it to the middle of a long prompt.

In *Lost in the Middle*, researchers found that several language models performed best when relevant information appeared near the beginning or end of their input.

Move that information toward the middle, and performance often deteriorated.

Same information. Different position. Different results.

The practical implication for long-context evaluations is interesting:

Don't just measure retrieval accuracy at 32K, 64K, or 128K tokens.

Measure it across positions within each context length.

A single long-context benchmark score can hide a surprisingly uneven reliability profile.

text:
If one miner makes most of your chain's blocks, 100 confirmations won't save your bridge.

Yesterday I told a dev bridging a small CPU-mined chain to BNB, with a USDT pool there, to worry about reorgs before the bridge multisig: deposit, get minted, sell into the pool, reorg the deposit away. They said it was exactly what they were missing and planned to mint after 100 confirmations. But one miner had already made about 85% of their blocks for a day.

Against that, depth only buys time. Size the daily mint cap to what you can afford to lose, and pause minting automatically when one miner's share of recent blocks gets too high.

Lighter is fine. It is annoying to see my funds technically stuck, but we are long past the permissionless DeFi stage, and this is the right thing to do. 

There is something like this every day. The contraction of onchain is sadly going to continue for a while as a result. People will rationally continue to remove funds the more they see high profile names getting scares.  

Once upon a time I had big chunks of my net worth in DeFi, but that hasn't been the case since 2025 now due to the increased number of risks.

I am now forced to manage the risk of how much to leave on perps dexs. 

I think once the industry demonstrates a big year on year decrease in funds lost to hackers then we will grow again. This year we have managed to lose more in hacks than onchain revenue, which is clearly insane. 

Or we somehow solve the insurance problem, which seems impossible.

watch how fast CT turns an “incident” into a “protocol hack.”

this morning, large trading accounts on Lighter were drained. Within minutes, the timeline was screaming exploit and $LIT was down nearly 20%.

but then came the official statement:

a security incident involving a single compromised external party.

on-chain analysis pointed to leaked API keys being used to move funds through Lighter's pool mechanics. Around $10.4M had left L1, with up to $15.5M reportedly targeted.

that's a very different story from “the protocol got hacked.”

and yet, for a while, the market traded the two as if they were the same thing.

this is why tracking what actually happened matters more than tracking what CT thinks happened.

text:
the real edge is time
- memes, capital and why there’s no rush

solana PA can be brutal every cycle, but memes always find their way back into a high liquidity phase, every single time. there's this weird paradox where the worse SOL PA gets, the bigger the chance for new narratives and community building, especially once it moves into consolidation before trending up again for a few weeks. that opens a time window for these established narratives to get sent up with it.

if meme coin trading frustrated you over the years and it just didn't work out for you, that's okay. explore other areas of the market, there's an edge for every trading style. maybe you need to build your capital elsewhere first and come back later, less emotional, or just keep trading your established edge elsewhere for as long as it works.

it took me years to find mine and i'm still learning every day. just never stop trying.

give yourself a longer time horizon to become profitable. and once you are, don't rush it. there's plenty of time to grow your capital later and a steady income from a solid career can get you through the building phase just as well. educate yourself, get a solid job or something on the side while studying, and try to save money in an ETF. if you put 500 a month into an ETF for 10 years, you can end up with around 85 to 100k depending on returns. ofc you're giving up some comfort in your 20s/30s, but building that capital base should take some hard work and dedication. it gives you real financial backing instead of living paycheck to paycheck like most people do their entire lives.

struggling a bit to build yourself and your future family a great start is normal. embrace the pain and learn to love doing things every day, movement is life anyway. if you start working in your early 20s, you'd go into trading with experience in your early 30s, with the capital stack and cash flow to trade profitably, bc money worries weigh much less on your emotions.

if you think you're behind in your 20s and 30s bc you're comparing yourself to the noise of the internet, that's a psychological trap. don't compare yourself to people who only post the best version of their lives, when you don't even know if it's real or if they're happy. comparing yourself to the whole world is toxic for the mind and it will always feed the feeling that what you're doing and making is too slow and not enough.

if you're young, it's ok to fail at trading profitably multiple times. hitting zero in your trading account in your 20s is normal, you're learning and failing. just make sure that at some point you find your edge, rhythm and passion. never stop trying and learning, it's crucial in life.

take it slow. emotions, comfort and giving up too early all get in the way.

stay optimistic, we'll never run out of opportunities.

2027 will be great

"I think the bottom is in. We're out of the bear market, what we're experiencing right now is an early pullback of a bull market."

Muneeb Ali (@muneeb) has been in #Bitcoin for thirteen years and built @Stacks, the execution layer on top of it. His case for why the selling happening right now is exactly backwards runs on two observations.

One: seller exhaustion. "A lot of people who wanted to sell, they've actually already sold... Every time negative news hits and Bitcoin doesn't really go down that much, that's actually a really good sign of strength."

Two: the sellers that remain are the irrational ones. Institutions put Bitcoin on their balance sheets, then treat it as a risk-on tech bet instead of a store of value. "They tend to sell Bitcoin whenever there's risk in the technology sector, which absolutely doesn't make rational sense. But this is what's happening in the market."

So the asset everyone compares to gold trades like a Nasdaq stock, while sitting, by his favorite metric, at not even 10% of gold's market cap, thirteen years in: "I would have expected us to be maybe twenty, thirty percent of gold by now."

We get into:
- Why negative news stopped moving the price, and what that signals
- The quantum question nobody can answer: can AI speed up the threat, is self-custody still safe, and who actually decides Bitcoin's upgrade?
- Bitcoin's next era: from passive store of value to income-generating asset, "imagine you have gold bars, and they give you two to three percent income"
- Borrowing against Bitcoin without giving it up, where the yield comes from, and whether Bitcoin yield becomes the next bubble
- Privacy vs institutions, and whether the four-year cycle survives

Alibaba has launched Qwen4 Max, gaining 9 points over Qwen3.8 Max on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and landing 3 points behind Kimi K3.1 Pro at ~11% lower Cost per Task

Qwen4 Max, using xhigh reasoning effort, scores 43 on the Intelligence Index, 9 points ahead of Qwen3.8 Max (xhigh) and 3 points behind Kimi K3.1 Pro (max, 46)

Key takeaways:

➤ Qwen4 Max improves on every evaluation in the Index vs Qwen3.8 Max (xhigh, 34): HLE-Diamond +21 points (24% to 45%), AA-Omniscience +18 points, AutomationBench-AA +17 points, CritPt v2 +13 points, Terminal-Bench-Science +11 points, Terminal-Bench 4.0 +9 points, GDP.pdf +3 points, FrontierCode 2.0 +3 points and AA-Briefcase +82 Elo.

➤ Qwen4 Max costs $3.27 per Intelligence Index task, ~3x less than Qwen3.8 Max ($10.02) and ~11% less than Kimi K3.1 Pro ($3.68): This is driven by 25% lower per-token pricing than Qwen3.8 Max, 70% cheaper cache hits and lower token usage. Tencent Hy4 costs ~3x less per task ($1.03) than Qwen4 Max but scores 8 points lower on the Index.

➤ Qwen4 Max uses 39% fewer output tokens per task than Qwen3.8 Max: ~105k output tokens per Intelligence Index task vs ~171k for Qwen3.8 Max, ~72k for Kimi K3.1 Pro and ~78k for Tencent Hy4. Qwen4 Max uses fewer tokens, while increasing 9 points on the Intelligence Index

➤ Improvements in AA-Briefcase (knowledge work): On AA-Briefcase, our evaluation of agentic work across real business files, Qwen4 Max reaches 1686 Elo vs 1674 for Kimi K3.1 Pro and 1446 for Tencent Hy4.

➤ Qwen4 Max trails Kimi K3.1 Pro on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and Tencent Hy4 on FrontierCode 2.0: Qwen4 Max scores 48% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 vs 67% for Kimi K3.1 Pro and 37% for Tencent Hy4. On FrontierCode 2.0, @cognition’s private evaluation of real-world coding tasks, it scores 26%, level with Kimi K3.1 Pro (26%) and behind Tencent Hy4 (31%).

Key model details:

➤ Context window: 1M tokens

➤ Multimodal: Text and image input with text output

➤ Pricing: $1.50/$4.50 per 1M input/output tokens on Alibaba's first-party APIs, with a $0.075 cache hit price. This is lower than Qwen3.8 Max across the board ($2.00/$6.00, with a $0.25 cache hit price)

➤ Availability: @Alibaba_Qwen 's first-party APIs

text:
I ran a PageRank-driven analysis on all recent news coverage related to Jensen, and traced how the New York Times shaped the entirety of this narrative: https://t.co/qKGMJ2LBV8

--
NVIDIA has lost over $1 trillion in market value since the first New York Times story broke about Jensen. I dug deeper to analyze how the news originated and spread, running a swarm of agents which analyzed almost 2000 stories, across 40 US and European news outlets, and applying PageRank to understand how they cited each other. 

Core findings: 
- Primary news driver: NYT, with 88 stories, most-cited
- Volume drivers: WSJ - 99 stories; Bloomberg - 140 stories; NY Post - 68 stories

All of this started from unknown sources who gave information to the NYT, which then ran the spy story (still unproven), and it was then picked up in other news publications. Curiously, even after that story, there was a 9 day period of extremely low volume reporting (28 stories only), after which there was a sudden spike after Jensen's own letter to NVIDIA staff. NYT then had multiple sequential spy and affair stories, which fed a wave of further news coverage. It was the originating hub of negative Jensen coverage. Multiple outlets since then had an explosion in stories about him starting earlier this week as well. 

Overall, as you see this data, you will observe this was an exceptional media onslaught against Jensen with sharply negative coverage about him, his work, style, and family. Infact, it was brutal, and unlike coverage in the past of CEOs who have had affairs (such as Intel CEO in 2018). For eg, NYT ran just 2 stories about Intel's CEO who had an affair with his employee, compared to 88 on Jensen! Why ? 

This analysis used a technique of how Google originally ranked webpages, using PageRank, and does deep dive link analysis so you can view how the news spread. What struck here was that it did not matter if there were proven facts or credible sources: the outcome here was pre-decided. The news was making the reality which it wanted. 

During this period, NVIDIA has lost $1.27 trillion in market value since the first story broke. On Nov 12th-13th, further news broke that both the US Justice Department, and Singapore - are unable to even conclude the spy allegation. 

This has been a catastrophic attack on one of the hardest working founders in modern times, who took an idea from a Denny's booth, through multiple instances of almost going out of business, to building the foundation of the entire modern world with how the NVIDIA story played out. Thanks to Jensen, we have hope that many formerly incurable diseases will get solved by AI, that quality of life will and have improved for billions around the world. 

Now I do not know if he will come back as CEO or not, but I hope he does. What happened to him here, and to the wider industry, was not fair.

AI时代，每个加密项目都要被黑客搞一下

11月才过一半，交易所、借贷协议、跨链平台、矿机管理软件，已经轮着出事了。

1. Lighter：疑似API密钥泄露，官方暂停提现和建池，开始调查。

2. HARD Lend：借贷记账出了漏洞，约5390万枚KAVA被拿走。官方确认底层链没有被攻破，也没有无限增发，被抽走的是借贷应用里已有的币。

3. Initia：云密钥被入侵，攻击者摸进托管平台，伪造跨链提款，约327万美元被转到攻击者地址。其中约216万美元在调查披露时仍被困在暂停的主链上。

4. Luxor：矿机管理软件被入侵，十几个客户账户的算力被改到其他矿池。矿机照常烧电，收益换了收款人。官方承诺补偿受影响客户。

5. Mercado Bitcoin：巴西交易所热钱包出事，平台临时关闭，承诺用自有资金补客户。

text:
⚠️ALERT: Lighter $LIT drops over 20% amid reports of a suspected $15.5M theft.

Early analysis points an attacker obtained API keys belonging to two market-maker accounts.

Here's what the attacker allegedly did:

- closed the victims’ positions and converted their balances to USDC
- created a public pool under the victim’s account
- deposited ~$10K to obtain 99.99% of the pool’s shares
- moved the victim’s USDC into that pool
- redeemed the shares to withdraw the money

API keys normally CANNOT send money to an outside wallet.

But since the pools were crated under the same addresses, the transfers needed no additional approval.

An associated wallet withdrew $10.39M USDC and exchanged it for roughly 5,750 ETH through CoW Swap.

It later sent 1,920 ETH to 12 new addresses. Around 3,845 ETH ($6.91M) remain.

Lighter says the incident appears to involve a single compromised external party.

Another ~$5M withdrawal from the second MM account reportedly remains pending after Lighter suspended withdrawals and pool creation.

The API-key explanation remains preliminary. A protocol-wide breach has NOT been confirmed.

text:
回看 Sam Altman 今年 4 月在 Core Memory 播客上的这段发言，像是给整个硅谷的宣发套路下了一场“超前诊断”。

当时 Sam Altman 直言不讳地反思： “我觉得我们这些技术宅陷入了套路，老是说我们要造超级智能，它会治愈癌症，你会特别开心。但这显然没怎么打动人。” “人们真正想要的，是富足，是自主，是还能继续做有意义的工作。” 

他反问道，如果不解决这些，大家只会问：“那我做什么？我孩子做什么？”

几个月后， Anthropic 创始人 Dario Amodei 在官方 IPO 路演视频中描绘未来时，被全网媒体引用最多、讨论最出圈的，依然是那句经典的“AI 将在未来 5 至 10 年内治愈癌症”。

这恰恰印证了 Sam Altman 的预判： 无论技术精英在报告里写得多宏大，只要一面向公众，大家下意识掏出来的科技免罪符，永远是“攻克绝症、消灭疾病”；

但对普通人而言，比起这些被科技圈重复了无数遍的远期奇迹，大家当下最真实、最难以消解的焦虑，永远是现实生活里的生存尊严与价值失落。

当一个人还在为自己明天的生计和孩子的出路发愁时，技术宅跑过来说“别怕，以后 AI 会治好你的病”，换来的大概率不是掌声，而是一种巨大的无力感。

Indonesian police raided Megaspeed’s local office and found empty server racks, per The Straits Times and Reuters.

Police raided the Jakarta office of Megaspeed’s Indonesian subsidiary in early 2026 at the FBI’s request. They found unopened server racks but no Nvidia GPUs.

Shipping records reviewed by Reuters show the Indonesian unit imported Nvidia hardware, including H100 processors, from 2024 to 2026. An unnamed Indonesian government source said most of that hardware was likely moved to China, possibly by private jet. That’s an allegation, not a confirmed finding.

There’s been no public finding that Megaspeed broke export rules. Singapore is separately looking into the company, and Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025 and has launched its own internal review.

text:
我在 OKX 的 354 万美元被冻结，印度法院已下令全部划走。我是正常交易的用户，为什么要联合印度冻结我？@okx @okxchinese

我是 OKX 用户，UID 307102750280430203，账户从 2022 年 5 月用到现在。2026 年 2 月账户被冻结，冻结时余额 3,544,352.81 美元（印度警方函件记录的数字）。起因是印度孟买网络警察的 C.R. No. 17/2025：2025 年 3 月 21 日 DeFi 协议 Zoth 被黑，8,851,750 枚 USD0++ 被盗，约 845 万美元。警方称被盗资金进了三个 OKX 账户，我是其中之一。2026 年 6 月 9 日，孟买 Esplanade 第 37 法庭下令，要求 OKX 把这三个账户里“全部被冻结的数字资产”划转到印度执法机构控制的钱包（图 1–3）。我被列出的资产：USDT 2,001,503.06、CHZ 40,143,733.68、BTC 5.29、UNI 12,456.99、BNB 68.25、ETH 20.75。

一、我的情况
2 月 17 日，OKX 客服确认是“司法机构请求”冻结，并表示未经司法机构许可不能向我披露详情（图 4）。3 月我收到印度警方的函件，随后提供了身份和住址证明、银行流水、资金来源说明和其他平台出具的交易证明提供给 OKX、警方和法院。到今天，没有任何人告诉我：我的哪一笔充值有问题。

二、我的资金来源，链上可以核对
账户实名开户，四年多、40 万条以上交易记录，主要是 BTC、ETH 的合约和现货。
我的 OKX 充值地址是 TLgN8mXjroP6KeEhsTSAz8cFQzzsxdDyQv，法院命令里列的就是它。这个地址共收到 39 笔 USDT 充值，每一笔 OKX 都在到账后约一分钟内正常入账。
其中 31 笔、3,407 万 USDT，占 85.6%，往上追两跳，源头是交易所 MaskEX 的热钱包 TQbQ2M5whiNAjuA9Xxv8jBdZjHT7xqo2kc。OKLink 把它标为交易所热钱包，警方函件的追踪图里也标为 maskex-hot。
另有 6 笔、540 万来自我实名认证过的一家第三方钱包平台，认证完成于 2025 年 2 月 17 日，比 Zoth 被盗早一个多月。这家平台出款地址的大额资金，上游同样是 MaskEX 热钱包。交易所热钱包里的资金是混在一起的，其中有没有 Zoth 的钱，只有交易所的内部记录能回答。到今天，没有任何人出示过。我不认识 Zoth 的黑客，没有参与这起事件。

三、命令和警方函件里，没有一笔交易指向我
命令写明被盗资金进了两个钱包： 0x3b33c5Cd948Be5863b72cB3D6e9C0b36E67d01E5 0x7b0cd0D83565aDbB57585d0265b7D15d6D9f60cf
然后直接写这笔钱“is deposited in”三个 OKX 账户。我拿到的 3 页命令副本，没有引用任何一笔从这两个钱包到我账户的交易哈希。
警方 3 月 5 日的函件里，带哈希的交易只有被盗那一笔。其余是追踪工具给我的交易对手打的风险标签，和几段关于黑客组织的公开报道。交易对手被打标签，不等于 Zoth 的钱进了我的账户。而 Zoth 资金的去向是公开的：被盗的 USD0++ 换成 8,323,591 枚 DAI，再换成 4,222.9 ETH；2025 年 3 月 25 日到 4 月 14 日分 12 笔转出，其中约 369 ETH 进了 THORChain 跨链路由。OKLink 已把这批下游地址标为 Hack 风险地址。我的充值里有没有来自这些地址的钱，OKX 可以逐笔核对。

四、请 OKX 回答
命令第 5 段写着：是 OKX 告知警官，划转需要法院命令。现在命令有了，但它没有回答最基本的问题：哪一笔钱是 Zoth 的。Gate 11 月 15 日就同类印度案件公开说明：不会仅凭单方面材料移交用户资产，已聘请当地律所沟通，资产继续由平台持有，用户有机会回应。我的律师 9 月 21 日出具的公证函写明，我已向同一法院申请撤销、变更这道命令。函件里的请求，我在这里公开再提一次：
说明我账户内资产的现状：是否已经划转，是否计划划转？
向我的律师提供完整的法院命令、警方申请书和链上材料，并指明哪一笔充值（哈希、金额、日期）被认定为 Zoth 被盗资金。
由 OKX 的印度律师与警方和法院沟通，支持我行使抗辩权，像 Gate 做的那样。
我没有要求 OKX 违抗法院命令。如果警方或 OKX 认为我的某一笔充值有问题，请指出来，我逐笔说明。我要的是有一次看到证据、向法庭说明的机会。

text:
🚨Lighter 遭攻击损失合计约 1549 万 USDC，官方称疑为单一外部方被入侵   现已暂停全部提现

Lighter @Lighter_xyz 已暂停全部提现及资金池创建，称正在调查一起安全事件，疑似单一外部方遭入侵，目前为预防措施。

此前，https://t.co/jrtLogRzSg 创始人 @0xTria 转述韩国社区分析称，此事或并非协议被攻击，而是两个大型做市商账户的 API 密钥泄露，损失合计约 1549 万 USDC：账户 #714710 于 17:41 被盗约 1039 万 USDC，账户 #714723 于 18:25 被盗约 509 万 USDC。

据分析，攻击者利用受害账户的 API 密钥平掉其全部仓位，再以该账户名义创建手续费为 0 的公共资金池，自己投入约 1 万 USDC 获得池中 99.99% 份额，随后将受害账户的 USDC 以每笔 100 万美元转入该池并赎回。

Lighter 上 API 密钥本身无法向他人转账，但同一 L1 地址下的账户间转账无需签名，受害账户创建的资金池被视为其本人账户，密钥泄露因此导致资金被转走。

Lighter 尚未就「做市商 API 密钥泄露」这一判断作出回应。

text:
trust is the biggest crisis of the modern internet.

look at social media today. can you actually trust anything you see?

> it could be a deepfake
> it could be someone lying
> it could be a paid campaign designed to shape what you think

most of what we see and read is driven by someone’s vested interest. a person’s, a brand’s, a corporation’s.

then comes privacy.

every moment we spend online is tracked. 

you’ve probably seen the tweets showing “deleted” media from instagram & telegram still sitting on your phone.

almost every app makes money the same way: by capturing your data.

yes, tech gave us convenience…but at what cost?

millions signed up. very few understand how that data gets weaponised against the same individuals who handed it over.

this is the battle ethereum is fighting now.

how do we give the power of tech back to people? how do we protect everyone’s digital rights and secure their digital lives?

-- 

ethereum is much more than a blockchain today. 

the bigger vision is CROPS an open world where you don’t have to trust anyone because you can verify everything.

that’s a purpose worth dedicating a life to.

and I’m orienting mine in that direction :)

只有单个做市商因为 「API 密钥」泄漏通过「资金池功能」把钱转走了，这里绝大部份责任在做市商自己泄漏了自己的 API 交易权限，少部分责任在 Lighter 交易所资金池上设计上的机制问题，Lighter 可能考虑了用户体验，放弃资金池转入的私钥签名确认环节。

但如果黑客控制了你的「API密钥」，就算不通过资金池，订单簿上也有很多种方法把钱弄出去，所以在 Lighter 里，你唯一需要担心的不是协议是否被盗，而是你的私钥和交易权限有没有泄露。只有你的私钥（or生成的 API 密钥）能控制你的钱。

至于说的 Lighter 为什么能短时间暂停提现？那是 Lighter 的防范机制，Lighter 最多只能暂停 2 次，2 次过后，14 天，任何人都可以开启主网沙盒模式提款，这是必要的短时间安全防范措施，与资金安全并不冲突。

事情发生时，我的很多朋友们都急成一锅粥，我绝大部分钱都在 Lighter，我也很慌。这时我真的希望，人们在了解到事情完整情况之前，可以善意发言。

而不是像 mlm 那样“Lighter 「疑似」被盗了”（这哥们Lighter 老黑子了，天天盯着黑 Lighter）or 引用我的翻译帖阴阳“Lighter 是最安全的”。

text:
Why Ghana’s inflation is falling and Kenya’s is rising

Assume you go to a bar for drinks with nine of your friends from University, and you all agree that the bill will be shared equally. You figure, that if you order an extra drink costing Kshs 1,000, it only costs you 100 more. In such a case, the normal way of things is for everyone to overspend. And this is usually a key driver for why government spending rises. We all pick leaders on the basis that they will authorize our expenditures, but not those of the other voters or voting blocks.

Once our government overspends, they need to fund it through taxes, or borrowing, or printing. Nigeria printed a lot, while Ghana borrowed both locally and externally. If one borrows too much, debt service will crowd out the budget, and then the options are to print, devalue or default. If they print money to pay the bills, this creates inflation. Too much money chasing too few goods. Without the citizens approval, the government has enacted a hidden tax. But inflation has another effect, which is that our currency will fall by about the difference in our inflation and inflation of other countries. If the USA has inflation of 3.7% and Kenya is 7.3%, the shilling will lose about 3.6% on average compared to the USD when measured over years.

The simple answer to our question is, Ghana already experienced their double digit inflation after their currency devaluation, and now have a retracement from the bad levels. Kenya is in early stages of the debt to inflation to devaluation cycle, and could still escape the devaluation, if it does the right things going forward. Additionally, Kenya's inflation is largely driven by supply shocks coming from oil and food. 

Ghana, on the other hand, having had a significant drop in currency and very high inflation, is correcting slightly for that move by having a reversal.

text:
Amber 风波背后：两家做市商的九年分岔路

一封 11 页的匿名举报信，让 Amber Group 再次回到行业视野。举报人自称公司前高管，指控管理层挪用客户资金、存在利益输送；Amber 随后回应称，相关指控不实，公司运营正常。

不少人把这件事看作做市商的又一次风波，但过去几年，Amber 的重心已经逐渐转向财富管理和 AI Agent。与此同时，同样成立于 2017 年的 Wintermute 仍在交易赛道加码，最近还拿下了 Hyperliquid 约 76% 的最高优先级数据席位拍卖。

两家起点相近的公司，为什么走上了不同的路？本文回顾了 Amber 从做市到财富管理、AI Agent 的转向，也梳理了 Wintermute 如何把资金持续投入交易速度和技术基础设施。

这场竞争也让做市行业的分化越来越明显：顶级机构投入巨资争夺速度和信息优势，小型机构可以深耕细分市场，而夹在中间的公司，正在面临越来越大的压力。
