text:
10 trades to watch into $NVDA earnings.

The ultimate guide to the @aleabitoreddit portfolio, part two: what Tuesday’s print means for each name’s fundamentals.

TL;DR
- $NVDA reports Tue 17 Nov at about 21:20 UTC. Consensus is $109.1B of revenue, $101.8B of it data center, and $124.7B for the January quarter. Options imply a 7.8% move.
- The selloff since Oct 6 was multiple, not numbers. $NVDA’s forward P/E went from 19.8 to 13.5 while its revenue estimates did not move.
- We scored each of Grok’s ten from 0 to 100 on how far $NVDA’s fundamentals reach its own: revenue exposure, plus how much of $NVDA’s estimate upgrade since July showed up in its estimates. Chart attached.
- Price damage and that score do not line up. The two biggest losers, $AAOI and $SIVE, sit in the bottom half.

1. $COHR (84). Datacenter and communications is 82% of revenue. Next-year revenue estimates are up 7.5% since the top and the P/E has halved to 18.5.
Watch: the January-quarter guide against $124.7B. Optics ship with the racks.

2. $NBIS (83). Over $40B of contracted revenue, chiefly Microsoft and Meta. This year’s revenue consensus fell 3.6% last week on late capacity.
Watch: $NVDA’s cloud service agreements, $29B last quarter, its own commitments to rent capacity.

3. $LITE (65). Two customers were 37% and 11% of revenue last quarter. Being acquired by Marvell at 4.5 shares.
Watch: the 18% gap to deal value, and any date for $NVDA’s co-packaged optics switches, where Mizuho has $LITE as sole source.

4. $AXTI (50). No disclosed AI customer, yet next-year revenue estimates are up 34% since July. China is 55% of sales.
Watch: whether $NVDA still says supply is constrained through fiscal 2028. Substrates are part of that.

5. $POET (50). $570K of revenue in the June quarter. Consensus goes from $6.4M this year to $82M next.
Watch: that 13x step. Nothing in the print pays for it.

6. $MU (39, a floor). Bloomberg estimates $NVDA at 17% of $MU’s sales and $MU at 14% of $NVDA’s costs. Forward P/E 4.4.
Watch: $NVDA’s supply and purchase commitments, $279B last quarter from $119B the one before. Memory is inside that number.

7. $AAOI (29). Data center is 58% of revenue, cable TV 41%. Next-year revenue consensus is down 10% since the top, the only real cut in the ten.
Watch: that estimate, $2.35B. A good $NVDA print does not put the 10% back.

8. $SNDK (22). Datacenter was 44% of last quarter’s revenue. Forward P/E 3.5.
Watch: $NVDA’s data center line against $101.8B. Flash follows the servers.

9. $RKLB (15). Backlog of $3.57B, up 52% in a quarter, with the US government at 42% of revenue.
Watch: nothing in the print. Its number is the third of backlog due inside 12 months.

10. $SIVE (0). Photonics revenue was SEK 15.9M in the June quarter, down 8%, against a $1.2B non-binding pipeline.
Watch: the first production order out of that pipeline. Redeye has Jabil at beta builds for the first half of 2027.

What ties them. $NVDA has beaten revenue consensus eight quarters running, by 1% to 5%, so a beat is the base case. Estimates in most of the ten are higher than at the top, on roughly half the multiple. What Tuesday can change is the guide and the $279B.

Serenity, which line are you watching?
author: D2_Finance
quoted_text:
The ultimate guide to the @aleabitoreddit portfolio, post semi blowup.

D2 desk note, Wed 11 Nov 2026. Ten names from Grok's list, not a disclosed book. Returns are since $NVDA's record close on Tue 6 Oct. For scale: $NVDA -29%, $SOXX -25%, basket median -47%.

1. $AAOI (-63%). One customer carries it: Microsoft was 28.8% of 2025 revenue.
Watch: Microsoft's 2026 capex consensus, $153.5B. It is the only one of the five hyperscalers lower than in July, and Microsoft says neocloud delays are why.

2. $SIVE (-56%). The AI laser story is ahead of the invoices. Bloomberg's customer list is led by Verizon at 3% and AT&T at 2%.
Watch: the first hyperscaler line above Verizon's 3%. Until then $568M of market cap rests on design wins.

3. $AXTI (-53%). Two steps from the capex line: it sells substrates to the laser makers, who sell to the buyers. Bloomberg shows no customer above 0.1%.
Watch: any datacenter-linked customer disclosed at 10% or more. Without one the demand read is second hand.

4. $LITE (-48%). Its largest customer is 26.6% of revenue, which Bloomberg names as Alphabet. Agreed on Mon 2 Nov to merge into Marvell.
Watch: Alphabet's 2027 capex consensus, $325.5B, the largest of the five and $24B higher than in July.

5. $SNDK (-48%). NAND is a pricing business first. Datacenter was about a quarter of fiscal 2026 revenue.
Watch: that 25% share. The rest is priced by phones and PCs.

6. $NBIS (-46%). A neocloud buys the GPUs and rents them out, so it is a funding story. CoreWeave is the template.
Watch: CoreWeave's interest expense at 2.2 times adjusted operating income in Q3, $846M against $379M.

7. $COHR (-37%). The least direct of the optical names. Bloomberg's top customers are Dell, Cisco and HPE at 23% combined, with $NVDA at 3.75%.
Watch: that 3.75%. The AI link has to show up in the customer list.

8. $POET (-34%). $877M of market cap and no customer data on Bloomberg at all.
Watch: the first reported customer above 10% of revenue.

9. $MU (-31%). The one large cap here, $820B, and the only one in $SOXX.
Watch: $NVDA's data center revenue on Tue 17 Nov against $89B last quarter. Bloomberg estimates $NVDA at 17% of $MU's sales.

10. $RKLB (-16%). Not an AI capex name: the US government is 42% of revenue.
Watch: that 42%. Its budget is set in Washington, and it still correlated 0.85 with $SOXX through the break.

What ties them. On Jul 30 we wrote "Do not fade Jensen, until you do", with roughly 48% of $NVDA revenue on six customers' capex lines. Today's pull is 48.4%: Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle, CoreWeave. The spending has not been cut. Consensus capex for five hyperscalers in 2027 is $1,173B, $119B more than on Jul 30. What moved is the cost of funding it. $NVDA's own 5-year CDS is near 140 bps, more than triple June, and CoreWeave owes $66B.

Serenity, which of the ten is the diversifier?

text:
天冷了，不知道穿什么，就穿皮夹克吧💪

顺便在预测市场下单一下黄仁勋回归（？）

半夜也是拷问了 AI 公司章程，试图找到回归的最小阻力路径，分享一下拷问成果

🦾【阻力最小的回归方式】

如果真要回来，阻力最小的大概是“外部顾问”这类角色，比如以咨询协议的形式做技术或战略顾问，或者在某家子公司挂一个顾问职位。

原因有四点：

• 不需要股东投票，也不需要提交 8-K 披露任命高管。

• 不担任董事或高管，就不承担受托责任，董事会也不用为他的行为承担同样的连带风险。

• 可以在协议里写明限制，比如不管理员工、只就特定事项提供建议、随时可以终止。

• 这已经满足 @predictdotfun  盘口的规则，里面明确把“正式顾问”和“子公司职务”等算作回归。

🦾【前提条件】

这种安排至少需要三个条件同时满足：

• 独立调查的结论比较轻，比如没有发现泄密或安全问题，误导高管的说法也没有被坐实，或者情节不严重。

• 继任者的搜寻不顺利，或者新 CEO 和关键客户明确希望他参与。

• 股东的压力持续存在，比如 Altimeter、Atreides 这类大股东继续公开推动，或者在明年的股东大会上用反对票向董事施压。

⚠️⚠️⚠️反过来，如果调查结论坐实他误导了法务或高管，或者确实涉及国家安全问题，那么任何正式职位都很难成立，因为这会让董事会直接面对股东诉讼和监管风险。

（我理解，如果这 part 出了问题，那么回归就几乎不可能。至于是否会走到这一步就要看各方的博弈了）

————————————————

注意，以上是让 @bot 根据章程规则和一般公司实践做的推断，不是公司的说法。目前公司唯一相关的表态是 NBC 转述的发言人那句“他不会以任何身份为英伟达工作”，这和上面的情景是相反的。

text:
🇯🇵Japan’s economy shrinks. Is a rate hike still on?

Japan’s economy unexpectedly stalled as rising prices squeezed household spending, Reuters report.

Japan’s GDP fell 0.1% annualised in July–September (0.02% QoQ), versus 0.3% growth expected. 

Preliminary data showed the FIRST contraction in FOUR quarters.

The numbers show an UNEVEN recovery:
- Household spending fell 0.3% as higher living costs hurt purchasing power.
- Business investment rose 1.6%, supported by AI projects and labour-saving technology.
- Net trade cut 0.6 points from growth as energy imports rebounded.

But weaker growth may not stop the Bank of Japan from raising rates again.

A weak yen and expensive energy are keeping inflation pressure high.

Many analysts still expect another hike as soon as December, following increases in June and September, though some say this data makes the call harder.

Japan faces a difficult balance. Higher rates could help support the yen and ease import costs, but they also risk putting more pressure on an already weak economy.

text:
the key facts in the jensen huang story:

us intelligence has not concluded that alice huang is a spy. the cia is not convinced the intercepts prove she funneled information to beijing, officials at odni call the spy label "not entirely accurate and over-torqued," and the attorney general says on the record that no conclusions have been reached.

singapore flatly denied the wsj's claim. it never investigated alice huang for espionage, and its officials never concluded she was a spy.

jensen huang never received a defensive briefing. he was surveilled, unmasked in intelligence reporting, and briefed about to the president twice, and he was never told any of it. he did not know alice huang was an alleged spy.

nvidia's chip sales were legal. there is no evidence the company broke the law. the diversion allegations target megaspeed and other third parties, and none of them is proven.

nvidia's board opened an investigation on november 8 and said the same day it had no reason to believe that either national security or nvidia secrets were compromised. 3 days later, it accepted huang's resignation, before the investigation reported. the filing announcing his departure gives the public no reason at all.

for two weeks, the ft, the nyt and the wsj ran intense, near-daily character assassination built almost entirely on anonymous sources. the central allegations have not been independently verified, and not one outlet has corrected or retracted any of it.

the treasury secretary is now publicly demanding an outside ceo and a "dramatic shake-up," effectively a government say in who runs nvidia next.

You don’t have to sell your house to access its value, you can borrow against it.

Tokenized stocks are starting to offer a similar option.

24/7 trading is already gaining traction. Bitquery found that 64% of DEX trading in Robinhood’s stock tokens happens outside regular U.S. market hours.

But there’s a catch: by Sunday evening, those tokens reflected only 4% of the price move seen at Monday’s open.

Being able to trade on Sunday doesn’t mean Sunday’s price reflects where the market will open on Monday.

Tokenized assets need to work as collateral. Otherwise, 24/7 trading is just a longer window to sell at the wrong time.

Meanwhile, tokenized stocks deposited into DeFi have grown 24x in a year, reaching $300M, per @tokenterminal. Holders are increasingly putting their assets to work beyond trading.

An oracle request is not complete when the first transaction succeeds.

In our public Golden Grid review, we found a VRF flow where `draw()` locked the protocol in a pending state and only the later callback could unlock it. If that callback reverted, future draws could remain blocked.

The fix was not “trust the oracle more.” It was an explicit, timeout-gated recovery path.

For every async flow, test three states: requested, completed and recoverable.

text:
Anthony, the "spy" story appears to be as fake as Russiagate. Here are the facts as I understand them.

(1) First, Alice Huang was at a company called Megaspeed[1], which everyone agrees bought Nvidia chips to sell to Southeast Asian companies called neoclouds. This is in itself completely legal under US law.

(2) However, some both inside and outside the admin didn't like this. They want to block Chinese nationals from accessing cloud services with Nvidia GPUs even if those servers are located outside China. Fine, but the so-called Remote Access Security Act (RASA) to block this has passed the House but not the Senate, and is not law[2].

(3) Singapore's government also looked into this when Alice Huang was on their soil[3] and didn't find any evidence that Megaspeed was actually selling chips to China illegally — let alone that she was a "Chinese spy." They did give her an entry ban, but that's like a visa denial.

(4) The related point is that it's not actually illegal to sell Nvidia chips to China! Since the Biden admin, there has been a complex and constantly-shifting set of export restrictions on chips. As of right now, Nvidia is allowed to sell H200s[4] to China, and indeed has designed these to comply with applicable law.

(5) But you know what...China actually also doesn't want Nvidia chips in China [5,6], because they want to build up their homegrown chip industry. The Nvidia chips are so good that China doesn't want to remain dependent on American chips, or vulnerable to possible US backdoors.

(6) The broader point is that this is an argument between nationalists and capitalists. Nationalists argue that US companies shouldn't even get close to selling to China, and shouldn't even be selling to neoclouds, even if it's "technically" legal. Capitalists argue that it's impossible for American companies to dominate world markets without, you know, being allowed to dominate world markets by actually competing in them. And that it's one thing to restrict physical sales to China, and quite another to require proof-of-citizenship for every single cloud access.

(7) Here's the thing: it doesn't make sense for one of the (few!) industries where America has a trade surplus with China to be summarily cut off, if you're worried about trade surpluses. It doesn't make sense to remove your number one AI CEO, if you want to be number one in AI. And it truly doesn't make sense to do to Jensen Huang what the communists did to Jack Ma[7], if your goal is fighting communism.

(8) So, to summarize: there's no proof of spying, as Blanche at DOJ has admitted[8], which rebuts your FBI/DOJ points. The Wachtell investigation you raise is just an in-house thing[9] ordered by the Nvidia board. And so all that's left is some affairs, which society has agreed is not disqualifying, given the realities of both Clinton and Trump.

In short: do you want a communist society like China, where Jack Ma's company can be stolen from him overnight on false pretenses? Or do you want some semblance of rule of law? If so, you should support the restoration of Jensen Huang to the company he built.

Citations follow in the next tweet.

text:
Stock LPs are quietly turning into one of the more interesting building blocks in DeFi.

You park liquidity in stock token pairs, and whenever someone routes a trade through your pool, you earn swap fees.

@paboxoxyz adds a nice twist here: some LP positions can also be used as collateral, so you can borrow USDG without pulling your liquidity. Right now we are testing and supporting SPY and NVDA LPs.

The idea is simple. Composability should feel like everyday convenience. If you need cash, you should not have to unwind an LP position just to access value.

That extra flexibility also makes the LP value prop stronger. A position that both earns fees and backs a loan is easier to size up, because the same capital can do more.

And when more capital shows up, liquidity usually gets deeper and more reliable, which improves execution for traders. Those improvements tend to compound over time.

One grounding note though. Stock LPs still have IL, your exposure shifts as price moves, and if you go out of range the fees can dry up. Once you add borrowing, you are also taking on interest expense and liquidation risk.

Make sure you understand exactly how it works before using it.

Why did we buy back solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu?
Crypto as an industry is in an unusual position. When you buy a company’s shares, the law gives you rights: you can vote for the board, hold directors to account, and claim a portion of what’s left if the company is sold or wound down. Tokenholders have no such rights. Without a legal claim on the business, buybacks are one of the few ways the value a protocol creates can reach its tokenholders directly.

However, for an early-stage company, every dollar spent buying tokens is a dollar not spent on hiring, product development, or growth. A young company in most other industries would rarely use its cash this way.

We don’t think buybacks should be a default. They make sense only when they’re the highest-return use of our capital. This is often, though not always, the case when a token’s market cap is low relative to the protocol’s expected future cash flows. In June, SANC’s market cap fell below $7 million, at one point trading close to the value of our treasury. In effect, the market was pricing the business itself at nearly zero despite our products and our revenue. We thought that was wrong, so we began buying back tokens.

Why burn the solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu?
We considered holding the bought-back solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu in the Strategic Reserve to preserve optionality. But the reserve is already sufficient for grants, incentives, and team compensation for the foreseeable future. While we’ve never sold from the reserve despite multiple OTC offers, we may do so in the future if it’s in the protocol’s long-term interest. Burning makes the buyback irreversible: those tokens can never return to the market.

Will there be future buybacks?
We have no fixed buyback program. This buyback was done on a discretionary basis and we may or may not do so again in the future.

Addendum: Update to Circulating Supply
We previously declared our circulating supply assuming full distribution to team and investors (250M team + 130M investors). However, since some of the buybacks came from departing team members and investors, that is no longer accurate.

In the interests of transparency, we will calculate circulating supply directly from on-chain data with three carveouts:

1. We count vested-but-unclaimed tokens in the Magna vesting contract as circulating.
2. One investor’s 30M solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu vests through Anchorage rather than Magna, so it isn’t visible as locked on-chain. We manually exclude the still-locked portion.
3. We hold 15M solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu in the Strategic Reserve on behalf of an investor who hasn’t provided a claim address. We manually include the unlocked portion as circulating, since it belongs to them and not to Sanctum.

The accurate circulating supply calculation can be found at https://t.co/ZumhIwaRvI

text:
i'm back from London after one of the most intense weeks in my 15 years in the space

I first came to DAS London in 2021. Back then the room was full of institutions exploring and expo halls full of custodians. I was there pitching the IPOR Index (our original product) and interest rate swaps for users 2 to 5 years down the road

Fast forward to 2026 and the conversations are about actual onchain capital allocation in size.

2021 was explorers and PoCs. 2026 is allocation. And honestly you can feel the gap opening up between institutions moving real capital onchain and those still testing the waters. The suits now come with targeted and precise questions about onchain and I'm always up for those conversations as the worlds converge

Compared to Token2049 in Singapore which was a mix of crypto natives and institutions, London was purely institutional. As regulation takes clearer shape the conversations are moving back to the major financial centers like London, New York and Paris

There was one key recurring topic: collateral. Liquidity and speed, flash loans vs delayed settlement and what changes when assets trade 24/7. Neither crypto nor TradFi has fully worked through the knock-on effects yet. Liquidity is a double-edged sword and that's the dynamic I'll be watching most closely

Summing up: institutions are here and they made up most of the rooms. That means capital coming onchain at scale. And it will scale at speed with infrastructure that meets their TradFi standards and regimes, with clear mandates, verifiable rules and capital that only goes where it's allowed to go. That's the bar we build IPOR Fusion vaults (our flagship product line) to and I can feel the interest in our product growing from one event to the next

thank you @LaserDigital_ @TheBigWhale_ @blockworks and @stable_summit for having us. And to our Head of Product @lukaszmuzyka for working the floor with me even if we only crossed paths three times all week 😊

if you're building or allocating onchain my DMs are always open

text:
11月16日—11月22日全球宏观指引：12月加息预期锁定，未来Fed政策节奏成为关注点！英伟达财报迎来AI盈利终考，APEC首脑聚会是否可以改变世界走势！？

本周三大核心主题：

中国APEC峰会，三大首脑聚集能否再次改变世界格局？（涉及地缘、贸易、经济多方走向，影响能源，黄金与风险资产走势）

宏观定价，12月加息预期锁定，本周10月议息会议记录公布，市场根据10月会议纪要+近期Fed官员讲话，判定未来Fed政策节奏！

Q3财报收尾，英伟达财报本周18日凌晨公布财报，算是本季度财报的收尾，Q3美股财报季整体情况比较坎坷，虽然行业基本面依旧健康，但是受到政治不确定性、利率不确定性因素压制，估值出现较大调整。而英伟达作为龙头企业，财报更是决定了市场信心，能否对抗宏观压力逆转趋势

接下来整体解读三大主题的：

第一主线——中国APEC峰会，中美俄三大首脑会晤，能否改变世界格局？北京时间11月19日

1，地缘格局，本次期望值最大的就是看本次峰会能否让持续了几年的俄乌战争进入谈判和平阶段，这将会有助于全球经济，贸易以及地缘局势的稳定性

2，美伊局势，如果俄乌出现重大和平转机，其实对美伊局势不太乐观，没了俄乌拖住美国的精力，特朗普很有可能将压力重新给到伊朗

3，坡脚总统，失去国会两院特朗普未来两年在政策是必然是跛脚的，从刚上任的意气风发，到现在的跛脚总统，面对国内政治压力，看特朗普是否会选择对外妥协，尤其是对俄罗斯放松制裁，对中国放松贸易对抗，提升自己在国内的支持率。

4，从地缘，经济与贸易角度来看，如果本次三方可以谈的愉快，短期起码可以提振股市，核心政策的乐观可以为风险市场带来一定信心，尤其是对中美股市，短期是有提振效果，但是能否逆转趋势，还是要看峰会后中美双方官方是否公布相关的积极政策信号

5，峰会期间中美股市节奏，峰会前开始反弹，期间看是否有乐观信号出现加速反弹，峰会后回落，然后等待准确政策信号进行定价

第二主线——宏观定价，10月FOMC会议纪要11月19日凌晨03:00（北京时间）与零售数据！

1, 截止目前，12月加息基本上板上钉钉，市场不在关注12月是否加息，而是在通过更多的信息来预期12月加息多少，以及到2027年3月份加息几次的节奏

2，10月会议纪要成为重要政策观察点，10月利率决议中有两位理事支持加息50BP，所以市场需要通过这份10月的会议纪要来看当时Fed官员对通胀对利率的态度，然后结合近期多位发言的官员言论以及宏观数据对未来政策预期进行在定价

3，这份会议纪要要解决五个关键问题：

a，10月暂停到底是等待数据，还是认为金融条件已经足够紧缩？如果多数认为金融条件不够紧，必然增加后续加息的预期，
b，否有更多官员支持连续加息？美银在预期到2027年3月份有三次加息，目前数据支持，如果会议纪要显示更多官员支持连续加息，将会进一步加重连续加息预期
c，Fed如何评价能源冲击？如果Fed认为能源冲击已经向核心商品、工资与服务价格扩散，那么仅靠Brent下跌未必足以改变政策方向。
d，关于Fed政策“反身性”，如果高长端收益率、信用利差扩大与风险资产下跌已经明显抑制需求，那么Fed继续加息的边际必要性可能下降。
e，Fed调整了2027年2028年议息会议时间，节奏，10月会议纪要中是否体现出讨论情况，有助于预期后续沃什政策能否落实，尤其是对减少议息会议，取消点阵图等重要事项

4，美国10月零售数据，11月17日21:30（北京时间），零售数据本周影响权重增加，如果过强，意味着当前利率并未压制需求，可能会让Fed有更多的加息政策施展空间，所以本周零售数据重点看整体零售销售、剔除汽车、Control Group（控制组）以及实际消费能力

零售温和走弱，对风险资产以及加息预期最有利，过强则增加加息风险，过弱会有衰退风险，后两者对风险资产都属于负面

第三主线——英伟达财报成为AI产业链关键验证，能否扭转高利率下的估值压力？

1，本周三凌晨英伟达公布财报，算是为本季度财报画上一个句号。Q3季度美股财报整体来看，行业基本面依旧稳定，但是受宏观与政治不确定性因素干扰，企业资本开支过快，盈利能力较弱成为估值调整的核心

2，英伟达财报作为收尾也是行业龙头，关乎行业信心，所以本周财报关注数据中心收入、Blackwell平台需求、毛利率、订单交付、下一季度指引及客户资本开支持续性

3，重申一下Q3财报季之后美股企业的验证逻辑变化为：AI资本开支增长 → 订单兑现 → 收入增长 → 利润增长 → 自由现金流改善 → 投资回报得到验证，而对于英伟达财报来说，可以验证算力供应商是否赚钱，但是不能单独证明所有购买GPU的云厂商都获得了理想的AI投资回报，这需要注意

4，本周英伟达财报需要回答市场五个问题：

a，数据中心收入能否继续超预期？如果收入增长继续加速，说明AI基础设施采购仍然强劲。
b，毛利率能否保持稳定？收入高速增长但毛利率下滑，可能意味着产品组合、成本、竞争或者客户议价能力发生变化。
c，下一季度指引是否足够强？估值是交易未来增长，所以未来指引对估值影响更大
d，Blackwell平台订单和交付是否健康？看需求是否增长，是否有供给瓶颈，以及客户订单与最终收入确认的情况
e，云厂商资本开支能否持续？这点本季度几大云厂商的财报已经给了答案，英伟达财报二次验证即可

5，英伟达三种财报的可能性：

a，收入超预期+毛利率稳定+指引上调，意味着需求与盈利同时改善，有助于提振科技股估值修复
b，收入强+毛利率一般+指引一般，意味着保持增长，但是估值要求提高，对目前来说并不乐观
c，收入与指引都不及预期，AI需求增长叙事信心下降，英伟达估值进一步调整

6，英伟达临时换帅，导致估值提前调整，尤其是失去黄仁勋的加持之后，一份普通财报好像是无法满足市场对估值的信心，如果黄仁勋有回归的可能性，则可以忽视财报中的一些瑕疵

辅助线——美伊局势

本周美伊局势不作为重点，参考上周的逻辑，特朗普应该是要集中精力在三方首脑会晤中解决俄乌问题，如果俄乌方面乐观，美伊和平预期变差，如果特朗普无法促成俄乌和谈，则可能对伊朗做出缓和态度！

整体总结：

本周对美股对加密都是一场重要考验，市场下跌中信心不足，筹码稳定性变差，此时如果全球局势，地缘，贸易不确定性继续增加，如果AI叙事再出关键问题，那么对市场来说就是一场灾难，当然我依旧认为未来是乐观的！

11月9日—11月15日全球宏观指引：就业重新加速，通胀具备粘性，Fed具备政策空间，谁来削弱12月加息的可能性？

本周三大核心主题：

a，就业韧性与通胀粘性是否形成共振？
b，美伊谈判能否真正降低能源风险？
c，美债与AI估值能否承受更长时间的高利率？

本周定价逻辑：截止目前，宏观市场处于什么环境？

9月的CPI PCE 已经告诉我们过去的通胀压力非常大，同时10月的就业数据过热告诉我们就业市场正在重新加速，两者结合之下，给了Fed更多加息的理由以及可能性！

目前12月加息概率提升至80%，已经进入充分定价阶段，也就是说当前的金融市场的波动已经在考虑12月大概率加息，意味着风险市场被加息在压制

而接下来从本周开始到12月9日的议息会议，我们只需要关注一件事就好，谁（什么数据，事件）可以削弱12月加息概率即可！

本周10月CPI ，10月PPI ，11月25日10月PCE，这是12月议息会议之前市场可以看到的有限数据，尤其是通胀端，虽然Fed更加关注PCE，但是CPI足够对通胀具备一定的前瞻性，所以本周10月CPI可能会成为议息会议前的关键定局！

当然，CPI PCE 代表这过去的通胀，而Brent 价格才代表未来通胀预期，在关注数据的同时，如果美伊局势和解，Brent 跌破90美元下方，可以有效对冲10月通胀数据差带来的利空效果

第一主线：10月CPI迎来关键审判，12月加息能否从预期走向锁定？

1， CME 12月加息概率目前是82.5%，已经进入充分定价区间，本周看通胀数据能否将概率推向90%，进入90%在概率上算是预期锁定（但是依旧并不代表100%加息）

2，本周通胀数据组合要看整体，CPI是看能源是否推动居民整体称呼成本上涨。核心商品，看运输、进口成本与企业定价压力是否开始传导？住房与核心服务，看内生通胀是否仍然顽固。环比变化，看最新通胀动能是否正在加速，而不是只受基数效应影响？

3，按照目前CPI的预期来看，最好的结果是数据全面下降，通胀压力降温，但是根据19月份油价表现，这种可能性极低。所以理性判断最好的结果是整体CPI保持粘性过热，但是核心CPI出现放缓，只要解除内生通胀压力，名义通胀压力可以由Brent价格下跌来抵消

第二主线：12月加息如何计价？对市场影响如何！

1，目前CME对12月加息概率计算为82.5%，已经进入充分计价阶段，概率上，过60%进入初步定价，过70%加速定价，80%充分定价，90%概率锁定，本周的核心就是看CPI能否让12月概率锁定

2，其次关注2027年Q1再次加息风险，一旦12月加息概率打满，通胀反弹更严重，能源不跌，可能会增加下次加息的概率，当连续加息预期较弱的时候，明年3月份加息的可能性更大

3，市场定价逻辑，本周12月加息概率进入80%充分定价阶段，金融市场走势都在对此定价，所以如果本周CPI让加息概率进入90%锁定期，那么后续操作就要开始抄底。因为在预期上，一旦市场锁定预期进行充分定价，一旦加息确定，反而会迎来反弹，如果12月加息概率变弱，市场加速反弹。

第三主线：美伊谈判进入实质性条件博弈，Brent能否真正跌破100美元？

1，能源定价依旧是目前通航预期的核心，通胀预期的背后则是Fed政策定价逻辑，所以能源价格依旧是大主题

2，目前Brnet跌破95美元，未来通胀压力放缓，一旦有效跌破90美元，就要注意对12月加息概率的削弱

3，中期选举之后共和党失势，特朗普对伊朗态度明显放缓，多个斡旋国家开始访问德黑兰开始积极斡旋，美伊局势进入关键性条件妥协阶段，一旦促成，双方可以回顾和谈迹象。

4，现在关键卡点是谁先执行，谁才能打破僵局，开始促进谈判。于此同时，虽然特朗普降低了对伊朗打击的可能性，但是依旧作为有效保留，对伊朗的海运封锁以及经济封锁依旧存在。能源价格不妥协，宏观依旧存在压力

第四主线：辅助线，美债拍卖情况！

1，本周三次美债拍卖，11月9日，11月10日，11月12日，分别拍卖3年期，10年期与30年期美债，分别涉及金额580亿，420亿与250亿，

2，为什么要关注本周美债拍卖的情况，因为过去几周我们一直在关注高收益率究竟会吸引更多资本进入美国国债，还是投资者会因为财政赤字、期限溢价与通胀风险而要求更高收益率？

3，本周的10年与30年美债拍卖直接可以反应需求侧的反应如何，尤其是30年美债对长期通胀预期、财政可持续性、养老金及保险机构久期需求更敏感。

4，中期选举之后，财政约束与政治僵局开始重新进入债市定价，财政支出、政府预算与债务上限以及AI监管，这些对债市都会产生一定影响。

第五主线：AI财报确定进入分化阶段，从需求增长转向盈利与现金流质量，财报影响走弱！

1，Q3财报至今，很多小伙伴已经清晰了本季度的定价逻辑，尤其是宏观压力之下，高利率，高能源冲击以及高通胀预期，导致利空因素放大，估值调整加深

2，接下来缺乏重要财报，本周关键财报看Cisco Systems与Applied Materials，前者看网络基础设施与企业AI需求，后者看半导体设备资本开支。

3，AI财报本周进入弱势定价期，财报权重走弱，定价逻辑更倾向于宏观，不过财报好坏，还是决定了行业基本面信心。

本周总结：

本周美股财报进入弱势阶段，核心看12月加息概率，目前已经到了80%的充分定价阶段，如果再进一步进入90%概率锁定期，那么接下来及时逐步解压，抄底进场阶段

随着12月加息预期打满，市场对12月加息充分定价，后续能源价格跌破90美元下方，逐步的削弱12月加息概率，越弱越多，反弹越快，尤其是能源跌破90美元后12月议息会议落地，反弹更强

宏观视角下，本周开始，到12月9日，对美股，对 #Bitcoin ，将会出现一个很好的抄底区间！

text:
SteveWillDoIt refused to give away a $10,000 Rolex after a Nigerian won his giveaway on X

He literally said “Call me racist but I’m picking again.”

the founder of a rival crypto casino stepped in and sent the winner $10,000.

This is what happened: 

– On November 14, SteveWillDoIt (popular influencer who promotes crypto casino Gamdom) hosted a Rolex giveaway on X.

– The winner was @bannks_, a Nigerian user selected through a random picker.

– But Steve refused to give him the watch.

– He publicly posted that a guy from Nigeria had won and that he was picking another winner.

– The post reached 3 MILLION views

– The winner responded, asking Steve to respect the original result.

– He even claimed he had already told his 70-year-old mother about winning the Rolex and that she cried from happiness.

– Then Skel the founder of rival crypto casino MetaWin, saw what happened.

– He offered to send the Nigerian winner $10,000 in cash.

– Another user from Stake added $500.

– Steve eventually sent the winner $1,500 himself.

– He later explained that he didn’t want to reward people who only participated in giveaways without actually supporting him or using his casino referral code.

Which actually makes sense 

But the winner had already been selected randomly.

So In total, the Nigerian user reportedly received approximately $12,000.

Goldman Sachs forecasts the 10-year Treasury yield will decline to 4.6% by December 2027, from approximately 5.13% currently.

The bank expects:

🔸 Fewer Fed rate hikes than markets currently price in.
🔸 Cooling inflation to reduce pressure for tighter monetary policy.
🔸 Stronger Treasury returns as yields decline and bonds regain their appeal as a risk hedge.

Goldman sees improving inflation dynamics supporting U.S. government bonds despite recent market volatility.

text:
EIP-8288 is exciting, and one of the most exciting parts is the unlock for privacy protocols.
Today, every privacy transaction comes with it's own zk proof, and all of them are verified independently. With leanSTARK/leanPCS, they can be aggregated in the mempool and batch-verified once (=less data, less compute).
Using privacy protocols will become cheaper and more native to Ethereum.
author: joshrudolf
quoted_text:
Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data once, the chain learns the answer, and then we never need to see that data again. This sounds very specific, but it includes most "heavy" things happening on Ethereum:

* Signatures
* STARKs
* Merkle branches
* FHE computation
* ...

Really the first two are the most important.

Once we go quantum-safe, signatures get bigger (65 bytes ECDSA -> 1-6 kB WOTS/SPHINCS depending on params) and ZKPs get much bigger (200-1000 bytes with groth16, PLONK, etc -> 128 kB with STARKs). This is unsustainable to put on chain, and 8288 fixes this.

8288 works by aggregating STARKs in the mempool. First, you as a user generate the STARK or SPHINCS signature or PCS opening (more on that last one later), and publish it. Then, each node listens. Each tick, each node takes all of the new objects that it has seen, and generates a STARK containing a list of "claims":

"pubkey P has signed message M"
"program X run on data D has output Y"
"p(X) = Y for some polynomial P whose hash is H"

and a proof that it has seen a signature, STARK or PCS opening verifying those claims. So the only information getting re-broadcasted is:

(i) hashes of inputs and outputs (~64-96 bytes per claim)
(ii) a single STARK proof per tick

These aggregate proofs themselves get re-aggregated, and eventually you get to a single "master proof" in the block, that verifies that all of those statements are true. And so the only other data that has to actually go on chain is the statements (the (P, M), (X, D, Y), (X, Y, H) tuples I described above), not the actual signatures or proofs. This gets put into a specialized frame type.

Now, let's get into the leanSPHINCS vs leanSTARK vs leanPCS part.

The core distinction is: *what is the underlying object that the user is creating?*

In leanSPHINCS, it's a signature, and specifically this particular type of purely-hash-based signature: https://t.co/HOazliHq9N

If we add leanSPHINCS, then users will be able to make quantum-safe accounts, and pay only a little bit of gas (4096 for the 64 bytes) for each signature. So we get scalable quantum-safety for regular accounts, multisigs, etc. But it's only one specific signature scheme, you can't do anything else.

In leanSTARK, it's a STARK. This means it's fully general: the user runs whatever computation they want, and publish a STARK of it. So you can use it for:

* Any signature scheme (including eg. lattice-based ones if you like those)
* A multisig that hides its internal logic
* Privacy protocols
* Private account abstraction: authorization logic that depends on some value hidden elsewhere in the state, so you can have one key that controls all your accounts without publicly linking them to each other

Basically, it's a free for all, in the same way the EVM is a free for all.

But leanSTARK has a practical downside. The protocol would have to specify the language in which users write their programs (we call this the "ISA"). So we would have to agree on that language. This is a really big deal - it's the first big case of "Ethereum moving beyond the EVM" - and so it's likely to take time to agree on the details of it, especially since the ISA would be hard to upgrade. There are benefits to taking longer on this, figuring out the ideal ISA, and then even giving access to it inside regular contracts.

LeanPCS is the third option. PCS stands for "polynomial commitment scheme": a proof that P(x) = y. The most important thing to know about PCSes is that they are by far the most important "hard" component of a STARK (see here: https://t.co/EEQWMU0gAf ). If you have a "magic PCS oracle" (which from the EVM's point of view, 8288 is), you can verify a STARK in ~20-40k gas.

The most important gain with PCS is that there is far less that we need to choose. Specifying a PCS only requires specifying a field, and there is a natural option: the 128 bit binary field (technically, we can go more general than that, and say the 2^k-bit binary recursive tower field, going up to 256)

LeanPCS is less efficient than leanSTARK onchain, because you would have to put multiple claims to prove one thing. But it's arguably more efficient offchain, because you have much more flexibility to choose proof systems.

But most importantly, leanPCS gives you the same generality as leanSTARK, in a way that could potentially be implemented very quickly. And once we figure out the ISA, we can add leanSTARK later.

So there is a route to getting "the cryptographic proof singularity" much faster than any of us expected, and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.
 https://t.co/dUHONMh75g

author: watchingmarkets
quoted_text:
the real edge is time
- memes, capital and why there’s no rush

solana PA can be brutal every cycle, but memes always find their way back into a high liquidity phase, every single time. there's this weird paradox where the worse SOL PA gets, the bigger the chance for new narratives and community building, especially once it moves into consolidation before trending up again for a few weeks. that opens a time window for these established narratives to get sent up with it.

if meme coin trading frustrated you over the years and it just didn't work out for you, that's okay. explore other areas of the market, there's an edge for every trading style. maybe you need to build your capital elsewhere first and come back later, less emotional, or just keep trading your established edge elsewhere for as long as it works.

it took me years to find mine and i'm still learning every day. just never stop trying.

give yourself a longer time horizon to become profitable. and once you are, don't rush it. there's plenty of time to grow your capital later and a steady income from a solid career can get you through the building phase just as well. educate yourself, get a solid job or something on the side while studying, and try to save money in an ETF. if you put 500 a month into an ETF for 10 years, you can end up with around 85 to 100k depending on returns. ofc you're giving up some comfort in your 20s/30s, but building that capital base should take some hard work and dedication. it gives you real financial backing instead of living paycheck to paycheck like most people do their entire lives.

struggling a bit to build yourself and your future family a great start is normal. embrace the pain and learn to love doing things every day, movement is life anyway. if you start working in your early 20s, you'd go into trading with experience in your early 30s, with the capital stack and cash flow to trade profitably, bc money worries weigh much less on your emotions.

if you think you're behind in your 20s and 30s bc you're comparing yourself to the noise of the internet, that's a psychological trap. don't compare yourself to people who only post the best version of their lives, when you don't even know if it's real or if they're happy. comparing yourself to the whole world is toxic for the mind and it will always feed the feeling that what you're doing and making is too slow and not enough.

if you're young, it's ok to fail at trading profitably multiple times. hitting zero in your trading account in your 20s is normal, you're learning and failing. just make sure that at some point you find your edge, rhythm and passion. never stop trying and learning, it's crucial in life.

take it slow. emotions, comfort and giving up too early all get in the way.

stay optimistic, we'll never run out of opportunities.

2027 will be great

基本确认，Lighter 不是被盗，协议没问题。

只有单个做市商因为 「API 密钥」泄漏通过「资金池功能」把钱转走了，这里绝大部份责任在做市商自己泄漏了自己的 API 交易权限，少部分责任在 Lighter 交易所资金池上设计上的机制问题，Lighter 可能考虑了用户体验，放弃资金池转入的私钥签名确认环节。

但如果黑客控制了你的「API密钥」，就算不通过资金池，订单簿上也有很多种方法把钱弄出去，所以在 Lighter 里，你唯一需要担心的不是协议是否被盗，而是你的私钥和交易权限有没有泄露。只有你的私钥（or生成的 API 密钥）能控制你的钱。

至于说的 Lighter 为什么能短时间暂停提现？那是 Lighter 的防范机制，Lighter 最多只能暂停 2 次，2 次过后，14 天，任何人都可以开启主网沙盒模式提款，这是必要的短时间安全防范措施，与资金安全并不冲突。

事情发生时，我的很多朋友们都急成一锅粥，我绝大部分钱都在 Lighter，我也很慌。这时我真的希望，人们在了解到事情完整情况之前，可以善意发言。

text:
I ran the numbers on BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF, and the average buyer got in around $81K.

BTC is at $65K, so they're sitting on about a 19% loss.

Yet...almost none of them have sold yet. Here's why that matters for you:

The short version: don't count on a fast recovery, don't chase bounces, and DCA monthly until the signals at the end flip.

/1 The ETF crowd hasn't sold yet

I took every day of flows into BlackRock's ETF (IBIT, by far the biggest) since launch and weighted it by that day's BTC price. 

Net inflows come out to about $80.7K'ish per BTC. 

BTC has spent most of 2026 below that line. In Sep–Oct it finally got above it, ran to about $86K, and held for a month. Then the Binance hack hit, and it fell 20%.

Since the hack, about $3B has left the spot BTC ETFs, $2.35B of it from IBIT, with outflows on 10 of the last 11 trading days.

But IBIT still holds about 795K BTC, only 4% below its peak. Most ETF holders haven't sold, instead they're sitting on a loss and waiting.

What to do: That's a lot of people who'll be tempted to sell when they get back to even. If you bought higher, don't count on a quick trip back to $81K to get out. 

If you trade, a bounce toward $81K is a place to take some profit, not to add. I'd only buy more aggressively once BTC is back above $81K and ETF flows have turned positive.

/2 Crypto's cash is shrinking

Stablecoin supply shrank by $15.5B in the last 30 days. Three quarters of that was USDT and USDC, the main dollars people use to buy crypto.

Less cash on the sidelines means fewer buyers for the dip.

The long-term picture is different. Stablecoin payments hit $482B in the first 9 months of this year, up 45% (per Allium). People are using crypto dollars more, even while they hold fewer of them.

What to do: Don't chase green days. Stick to your DCA. And watch USDT & USDC supply (free on DefiLlama). 

When it starts growing again, the buyers are coming back.

/3 Buybacks are a cushion, not a floor

At its current pace, pump is buying back about 18% of its circulating market cap a year. It's still down 35% since the hack.

Hyperliquid buys back about 5% a year, and HYPE is down 17%. That's better than BTC (-20%), ETH (-23%) & SOL (-29%).

The difference is the business behind it. Hyperliquid's buybacks over the last 30 days ran above its 12-month average. Pump ran below.

What to do: Before you buy a token for its buybacks, pull up its revenue. If the last few months are trending down, skip it, no matter how big the buyback looks.

/4 So what am I doing?

DCA monthly. At these prices, I'm happy to keep buying BTC and HYPE every month. DCA keeps it simpler than trying to time this.

Keep cash. If the selling isn't done, you'll want ammo lower.

No leverage. Not in this market, and it's not something I usually do anyway.

Be VERY Picky on alts. If I buy alts, only ones with a growing business behind the buybacks.

/5 What would tell me it's turned

USDT & USDC growing again.

ETF flows turning positive.

The Fed done hiking, and then cutting.

BTC back above $81K and holding it.

What are you doing in this market?

author: splinter0n
quoted_text:
got detained at a Turkish airport over a $100 p2p trade i made on binance almost 2 years ago. if you live in Turkey and use p2p, please read this

i got to the airport in a great mood, they even let my bag through with 3kg overweight. then at passport control the officer looked at his screen and things got weird.
he called the police. they told me there was a criminal case against me for internet fraud, a court had already found me guilty, and i wasn't flying anywhere today.

they searched my bags, spent 2 hours on paperwork and my flight left without me. then police took me to the station inside the airport, where nobody really spoke english and the only answer to "do i need a lawyer?" was "court, translator, please wait". two more hours later we went to court, which was also inside the airport.

the translator's first question was "have you ever exchanged money p2p on binance or bybit?". turns out in january 2025 i swapped $100 to lira, and scammers laundered part of it through my order. the victim filed a report, police traced every transfer, and my name ended up in the chain.

later they brought in another guy with the same problem. he was detained on arrival with his wife and two small kids, and he hadn't used p2p since 2024. the translator said they see around 10 people like us every day.

i gave testimony, attached screenshots of my orders from that day, the prosecutor joined by video call and all charges were dropped. but there were no flights left, so i flew out the next morning. final cost of that $100 swap about $400 in tickets and a day in airport custody.

if you're in/travel to Turkey: p2p can catch up with you years later, on departure or arrival. so better just don't do p2p on exchanges at all

Unc advice to defi teams. Finance is power law distributed.  The top 1% users will drive 90% of aum or volume. You should be literally making a list of the top 100 users you want using your platform and getting a warm intro and talking to them. Is the problem you are solving a problem they have?

It’s the same thing as raising a round. If vast majority of this list says no, is your product still worth building? Figure out what problem they all have in common that they are willing to move capital and pay you and solve it.  

A lot of what worked in defi summer was that the list of early adopter power users was all in one chat room.

BREAKING: The US Commerce Department issued a new rule to stop China from remotely accessing advanced American AI chips.

Until now, export controls covered physically shipping restricted chips but not renting access to them. That let Chinese AI firms use advanced Nvidia chips through cloud services at data centers in Southeast Asia without ever importing them. The rule is designed to ensure "existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented," Commerce said.

It expands coverage to Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, where Chinese firms have reportedly rented computing power. Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the center of the Nvidia scandal, operates a data center in Malaysia.

The rule comes a day after Sen. Maria Cantwell accused Commerce of failing to stop chips from reaching China, and as Trump heads to Asia to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping.

text:
Stock LPs are quietly turning into one of the more interesting building blocks in DeFi.

You park liquidity in stock token pairs, and whenever someone routes a trade through your pool, you earn swap fees.

@paboxoxyz adds a nice twist here: some LP positions can also be used as collateral, so you can borrow USDG without pulling your liquidity. Right now we are testing and supporting SPY and NVDA LPs.

The idea is simple. Composability should feel like everyday convenience. If you need cash, you should not have to unwind an LP position just to access value.

That extra flexibility also makes the LP value prop stronger. A position that both earns fees and backs a loan is easier to size up, because the same capital can do more.

And when more capital shows up, liquidity usually gets deeper and more reliable, which improves execution for traders. Those improvements tend to compound over time.

One grounding note though. Stock LPs still have IL, your exposure shifts as price moves, and if you go out of range the fees can dry up. Once you add borrowing, you are also taking on interest expense and liquidation risk.

Make sure you understand exactly how it works before using it.

text:
Louisiana just banned Kalshi and Polymarket.

The casinos stayed open. The sportsbooks stayed open. The video poker at the truck stop stayed open.

I followed the gambling money behind AG Liz Murrill, who banned them.

It leads to Dublin, London, and Nevada 👇

tl;dr:

  – A casino can't legally give a Louisiana politician one dollar. So gambling money takes the side doors

  – Video-poker truck stops → AG Liz Murrill: $41,000. Their lobbyist on online gambling: "We will die on this hill"

  – The sportsbook lobby → her: $40,500, more than anyone else in the state. Behind it: FanDuel (owned
  from Dublin), BetMGM (half-owned from London), bet365 (England),  DraftKings, Fanatics

  – Its biggest Louisiana cheque, $25,000, landed between the two votes on a law that gave her office new powers

  – Caesars (Nevada) → the Republican AGs' club: $260K. The club reportedly spent $1.8M electing her.
 She chairs its policy now

  – Nov 12: she sues ten prediction markets in the morning. Banned by dinner

She isn't fighting gambling. She's fighting for the house.

Full details:

I went through 2.1 million Louisiana campaign contributions. Every cheque, every date.

  – The day

  Nov 12, 9 a.m.: the state Gaming Control Board kicks off "Illegal Gambling Awareness Week."  -- You can't make this up. 

Same morning, Murrill sues Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, Robinhood and six more. By evening, a judge in Tangipahoa Parish signs the order. 

These are markets overseen by a federal regulator, the CFTC. Its chairman says their contracts were traded openly in Louisiana for years. 
Then one morning it's an emergency.
 
So what changed? 

  – The side doors

Door 1, the truck stops. 
- Ten video-poker companies, $41,000. 
 -- Osage Express $12,500. 
 -- Pelican Gaming $10,000. 
 -- Redman Gaming $5,000. 
Their lobbyist, Alton Ashy, on online gambling: 

"This is video poker's Rubicon. We will die on this hill." |

Four of her donors are his clients.

Door 2, the sportsbooks. 

Their lobby has paid 83 names in Louisiana. The typical one got $3,000. The governor got $24,000. She got $40,500. 
And look who is behind it: FanDuel's parent sits in Dublin, BetMGM is half-owned from London, bet365 is English. None of them vote in Louisiana! This is a literal case of foreign influence. 

Door 3, Caesars, out of Nevada.
It can't pay her. So it pays $260K into the Republican Attorneys General Association, which reportedly spent $1.8M on her 2023 race. This year, she's its policy chair.

– The calendar

This is the part that got me.

Nov 15–18, 2023. The last four days of her runoff. Nine gambling donors give her $25,000. Five of the cheques are dated election day. She won by 33 points. 
They were buying a seat.

May 9, 2025. Sportsbooks: $12,000.

June 17, 2025. The state fires 40+ cease-and-desist letters at unlicensed online gambling.

 April 28, 2026. Sportsbooks: $25,000 to her PAC.

Two weeks earlier, the House passed a bill giving her office new enforcement powers. Two weeks later, the Senate passed it. The governor signed it May 15.

 Nov 12, 2026. The ban.

  – The table

One more name. Gov. Jeff Landry, her boss for eight years, got $305K from 38 gambling donors. 
Sixteen gambling cheques in a single day in 2023. He took the Gaming Control Board's chairman straight out of the AG's gaming division. He signed her new powers.

  So it's not just her. It's the whole table.

  – Washington

 Nov 13: The United States sues Louisiana. CFTC Chairman Selig calls her case "naked lawfare and a cynical political stunt." 
She calls him the "obsequious standard bearer" for Kalshi.

My read:

Louisiana doesn't have a gambling problem. It has a guest list.

The truck stops are on it. 
Dublin is on it. 
London is on it. 
Nevada is on it.
--  through the side door.

Kalshi and Polymarket were built in New York.

The sportsbook money behind the Attorney General who banned them leads to Dublin and London.

 Since when does foreign-owned gambling money get a say in which American companies Americans are allowed to use?

That one gets its own thread.

text:
We are rebuilding @StakeDAOHQ  app. Why, and how.

The current app grew one product at a time. Each one works, but nothing connects them.

In the current app a voter can only vote, and a depositor can only deposit. A depositor that wants to borrow needs to go to another app. But it can be the same person. Someone that has votes could also be interested to provide liquidity in the pools he votes for. Or it can be just a voter.

The goal is to build an app that fits them all, if they come with only one action or multiple. That's why we reworked the project around just earning yields.

Having multiple products, multiple options, lacks clarity. Simplifying makes it more clear.

I will be posting until the project is live: the decisions, the thinking, stuff like that.

text:
豆包工作 vs WorkBuddy：同一个模型干同一件活，谁更省钱？谁更好用？

最近看到豆包工作支持第三方模型了，Kimi、GLM、DeepSeek 都能选。我一直在用的 WorkBuddy 也能选这些模型。

那问题来了：同一个模型、干同一件活，哪边花钱更少，哪边做得更好？你们知道我一定手痒的😂 花了一个下午，两边一起跑了一遍。

结果有一组把我看愣了：Kimi K3.1 Pro 分析同一份订单表，两边报告都是满分，豆包工作花了 0.13 元，WorkBuddy 花了 4.65 元，差了 37 倍。这一次就用掉了我WorkBuddy个人标准版套餐 积分的 6.6%。

一、怎么测的
版本：豆包工作标准套餐，WorkBuddy 个人标准版包月套餐
两边手选同一个模型，发同一条提示词
4 类任务：做公司介绍网页、写新能源汽车出海调研、分析电商订单表、做 PPT
5 个模型：DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Kimi K3.1 Pro、GLM 5.3 Flash、GLM 5.3、Kimi K3
两边一共发起 34 次，交付 28 次
花费按每次账单实扣，用两边套餐标价折成人民币；质量按同一张清单打分，满分 5 分

二、先看结果：6 比 3
能成对比较的 9 组里，豆包工作便宜 6 组，WorkBuddy 便宜 3 组。

三、逐个模型看
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash：豆包工作完胜
豆包工作上是限时优惠 0.01×，我跑完的 5 次任务，账单全部显示免费，因为豆包工作还有一个优势机制，小额消耗还能免费，如此一来很多轻量任务还能省更多。同样的三类任务，WorkBuddy 按任务平均花了 0.16～0.33 元。
做网页：豆包工作免费，质量还高 1 分
写调研：豆包工作免费，质量分低 0.5 分
分析订单表：豆包工作免费，质量打平

Kimi K3.1 Pro：差了 37 倍
分析同一份订单表：
豆包工作：扣 16.77 点，折 0.13 元，用时 8 分 39 秒
WorkBuddy：扣 265.98 积分，折 4.65 元，用时 33 分 53 秒
两边报告都是满分。

GLM 5.3 Flash：WorkBuddy 赢两项，豆包工作质量更好
三类任务各跑两轮，按有效结果取平均。
写调研：豆包工作便宜一半（0.078 元对 0.159 元），但质量分低 1 分，它把比亚迪在布达佩斯的欧洲总部写成了乘用车工厂
分析订单表：WorkBuddy 稍便宜（0.111 元对 0.128 元），豆包工作质量高 1 分
做网页：WorkBuddy 更便宜（0.020 元对 0.105 元），豆包工作质量高 0.5 分

GLM 5.3：WorkBuddy 赢
分析订单表：豆包工作 2.27 元，WorkBuddy 0.74 元，WorkBuddy 质量还高 1 分。

Kimi K3：豆包工作便宜一点，WorkBuddy 做得更好
做 PPT：豆包工作 2.86 元，交了 8 页；WorkBuddy 3.35 元，交了 11 页，风险和对策写得更完整，质量分高 1 分。

四、钱是怎么算的
按 11 月 13 日两边的套餐标价折算：
豆包工作：标准套餐连续包月 68 元、9000 额度（含 3000 限时加赠），每点约 0.0076 元
WorkBuddy 个人标准版：连续包月 70 元，单月购买 99 元。每月基础 2,000 积分，加上 2,000 限时加赠共 4,000 积分，按照连续包月每积分约 0.0175 元
光看单价，WorkBuddy 每积分的价格是豆包工作每点的 2 倍多。

五、几句实话
两边都有超时没交付还照扣的😭 豆包工作 1 次，约 0.12 元；WorkBuddy 3 次，合计约 4.30 元。
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 的 0.01× 是限时优惠，不是长期价格。两边的限时加赠积分也都不是长期的。
Kimi K3.1 Pro、GLM 5.3、Kimi K3 这三组，两边各只有一次有效结果，单次会有波动。其中 Kimi K3.1 Pro 和 GLM 5.3 两组，WorkBuddy 那次是补测，没和豆包工作同时发起。

另外，豆包工作目前小额积分消耗免费，很多低额度消耗都能0积分完成，叠加使用DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、豆包等
0.01×特惠模型性价比会很高，推荐大家体验试试，也能节省不少费用。

六、我的结论
豆包工作的积分本身就便宜，同一个模型干同一件活，大多数时候豆包工作的账单更轻，9 组里便宜了 6 组。

质量更要紧的活，比如写调研报告、做上会用的 PPT，我会两边都跑一遍再挑。

author: chamath
quoted_text:
Chamath Palihapitiya just made a very interesting argument about Jensen Huang leaving NVIDIA.

Everyone seems to think China, AMD, Google, and other chipmakers are suddenly going to benefit from Jensen's departure but @chamath argues that the biggest beneficiary might actually be the US government. Let's start with China. There are two possible scenarios. Either advanced NVIDIA chips weren't reaching China in meaningful quantities, in which case nothing really changes, or chips were finding their way into Chinese hands through intermediaries. If that's the case, increased government scrutiny could actually make it harder for China to access American compute.

And even without Jensen, NVIDIA's technological moat doesn't suddenly disappear. We're talking about decades of engineering, CUDA, NVLink, networking infrastructure, and the ability to scale hundreds of thousands of GPUs into functioning AI clusters. China can't simply replicate that overnight, especially when you consider the challenges surrounding advanced manufacturing, HBM, and packaging capacity. The same goes for NVIDIA's competitors. I've seen people arguing that AMD, Google, Cerebras, and other chipmakers will immediately benefit, but I think it's more complicated than that. Jensen spent years building relationships with TSMC, securing CoWoS packaging capacity, coordinating HBM production with SK Hynix, Micron, and Samsung, and making sure NVIDIA's entire ecosystem worked together.

You can't replace that infrastructure overnight. Now, this is where I somewhat disagree with Chamath. I do think competitors could benefit over the longer term, especially if NVIDIA's leadership transition creates uncertainty around future product roadmaps and supply commitments. Hyperscalers already want to reduce their dependence on NVIDIA, and this could accelerate those efforts. But there's a difference between having an opportunity and actually being able to capitalize on it.

Now, here's where Chamath's argument gets really interesting. What if the biggest winner is actually the U.S. government? If Washington believes advanced AI chips have been reaching restricted entities despite existing export controls, this could create an opening for significantly tighter government oversight. We're talking about mandatory chip level telemetry, location tracking, and potentially government controlled kill switches that could remotely disable advanced AI hardware. Essentially, the government could move beyond simply deciding who can purchase advanced chips and start exercising greater control over where those chips operate and who gets to use them.

Personally, I think NVIDIA will be fine over the long term. But the bigger risk isn't someone suddenly building a better GPU tomorrow. It's whether leadership disruption, regulatory intervention, and supply chain uncertainty slow down NVIDIA's ability to execute. And that's something investors should be paying very close attention to.

text:
Part 4: Move next to the exchange

Same bot, same code. Moving it off my laptop to a $0.10/hour server in Tokyo took end-to-end latency from 211ms to 27ms.

That's almost 90% gone without touching the code. Part 3 was Amdahl's law: the code takes microseconds, the network takes tens of milliseconds. You can't optimise the speed of light, so you move closer. Easiest win in the whole series.

Pick the zone by measuring

Binance's matching engine lives in AWS Tokyo, which has several zones, basically separate data centres. AWS shuffles zone names per account, so use zone IDs.

Our probe (code linked below) spins up a tiny server in each zone, times 100 handshakes to Binance and deletes itself. A few cents.

apne1-az4: 0.5ms
apne1-az1 and az2: ~2ms

4x closer just by picking the right building.

Don't use a burstable box

Lightsail and EC2's `t` instances only guarantee you a slice of a CPU on the sizes a bot would use, 20% on Lightsail's $12 and $24 plans. Go over and you burn credits, run out and you get throttled. A quoting bot is always on and busiest when the market moves, which is the worst time to get throttled. Remember, we care a lot about low jitter during volatility (will be in the weeds optimisations on this in future tweets).

Lightsail is great for a website. For this you want EC2: a c8g.large, where the CPU is yours.

Do it in code, not clicks

The whole setup is Terraform. Server, zone, firewall and permissions all live in a template. Using the AWS UI is terrible and annoying, and the sooner you switch to IaC (infra-as-code) the better, trust me. One command up, one command down, so no forgotten box on next month's bill. Same build every time, in any zone or account.

Also recommend setting up ssh keys to access your box (or use SSM) and use a static IP (called EIP in AWS) so that you can get your IP ranges whitelisted on exchanges you trade on, and they don't change if you replace the box.

Two freebies

The clock syncs to Amazon's time service inside the data centre. My laptop was 288ms off in part 3, now it's microseconds, so the network numbers are finally useful and accurate.

The bot key never touches disk. It sits encrypted in AWS Parameter Store and gets pulled into memory at startup. Always use delegate/scoped API keys not root access private keys, and never store them anywhere on your infra in plaintext.

Scoreboard, p50
End-to-end: 211ms to 27ms
Binance to us: ~40ms to 1.6ms 🔥
Order to live on Bullet: 24.6ms (to be addressed next)

What's left is mostly order to live, because the bot cancels, waits, then places. Part 5 fixes the sockets, part 6 stops the blocking calls.
author: Tristan0x
quoted_text:
Part 3: Measure once, cut twice: telemetry and Amdahl's law

Most people optimise their bot without ever measuring it. It's like trying to lose weight without a scale.

The bot from part 2 runs from my laptop in Singapore. It felt slow, and my first instinct was to dive into the Rust decision code and optimise the shit out of it. I was very wrong. It was nowhere near the bottleneck.

Then I remembered Kevin Bowers' @jump_firedancer  talks at Breakpoint, and measured first.

One trip, step by step

The bot now timestamps every step from a Binance price update to our new order resting on Bullet, and exports it all to Grafana. Averaged over 5 minutes:
1. Inside Binance: 0.4ms
2. Binance to us: 41.6ms
3. Waiting in our queue: 0.010ms
4. Our code deciding (tick-to-trade): 0.0057ms
5. Order to live on Bullet: 190ms
End-to-end: 232ms

Amdahl's law

Speeding up one part only helps as much as that part's share of the total. Our trading logic is 0.002% of the trip. Make it 99% faster and the whole trip gets about 0.002% faster. Days of work, basically nothing to show for it.

That's the whole point of measuring: know where to look before you spend your time, or Amdahl's Street Justice (as Kevin Bowers likes to call it) gets you.

And the numbers already tell us what to fix:
• Binance to us (41.6ms) is distance. Part 4 moves the bot next to the exchange. Hint hint, colocation.
• Order to live (190ms) is our naive executor. It cancels the old order, waits for Bullet to confirm, then places the new one, and waits on every request. Part 6 fixes that.

Two traps when measuring
• Use Rust --release builds. Debug builds skip the compiler's optimisations, and made our code look 3-5x slower than it really is. More on squeezing Rust in part 9.
• Sync your clocks. Binance to us compares Binance's clock with your laptop's, so if yours is off, the number is off. Mine drifted 433ms behind, so messages arrived before they were sent. That's why end-to-end only uses the exchanges' clocks. Details in the github

Now everything is timed and we have a target. Measure first, then fix the biggest number.

Tomorrow we move the bot to Tokyo, next to the exchange.

Lighter just got drained for $15.5M and right now nobody on the exchange can withdraw a single dollar

all withdrawals frozen. no timeline. if your money is on Lighter it’s stuck there with everyone else’s

and the contract wasn’t even touched. someone straight up stole the API keys of two big market makers and cleaned them out, $10.39M from one and $5.09M from the other, in under an hour

how he did it is what pissed me off the most. on Lighter an API key can’t send money to another user, fine. but accounts under the same L1 address move funds between each other with no signature, and a public pool you open counts as your own account. so the guy just

1. closed every position on the victim account into USDC
2. opened a public pool from that account, 0% fee
3. threw in ~$10K of his own and got 99.99%
4. pushed the victim’s USDC into the pool, $1M at a time
5. took his share and walked out with all of it

a trading key. the thing everyone shoves into bots and sketchy terminals every day

and Lighter’s answer is “single compromised external party”. bro the money left through your own pool feature. the $10.39M hit Ethereum at 10:11 UTC and their tweet came at 11:02, 51 minutes later, together with the pause, after the fattest chunk was already gone. the $5.1M from the second account was requested at 10:28 and it’s hanging on the pause (per @zarvxbt). if Lighter doesn’t let it through, at least that gets saved

LIT down ~13%, $2.65

if you have an API key on Lighter for anything, delete it today. I wouldn’t make a new one until they let you create a key that can only trade

now the money. 0xb3fffca23d4444eE73349825ACD84f7b5020e387 swapped $10.36M into ~5,750 ETH on CoW in 6 minutes and started chopping it into 160 ETH pieces. each one lands on Hyperliquid as ~$288K in a fresh wallet and goes straight into XMR1, Wagyu’s wrapped Monero. withdraw it through their bridge, you get real XMR, and nobody’s finding it after that

right now 7 HL wallets hold 3,893 XMR1 (~$2M), nothing pulled out to Monero yet. 3,844 ETH (~$6.9M) is still sitting in the main wallet

and he’s not getting out fast. XMR1 usually trades $15-400K an hour. after the hack it did $1.6M, then $3M, price ran from ~$488 to $525, one of his wallets bought at $514 average. he’s overpaying 5% just to get in and pushed through a fifth at most

what really finished me is he came in the same way. the ~$10K for the pool was XMR1 from the same Wagyu payout wallet, sold on HL this morning. he’d been prepping since Nov 12, even ran money through Aevo to cover his tracks. then the wallet that made the Aevo deposit sent gas straight to the hacker at 09:00 UTC. four days of prep and he doxxed his own wallets lol

so now it’s all on Wagyu. they control the withdrawal and they can freeze those 7 wallets today, most of this money can still be caught.  I don’t want to hear one more time that XMR1 is just a harmless way to buy Monero

quoted_text:
SANC Buyback and Burn Announcement

Sanctum recently concluded buybacks of solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu.

10,708,333 solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu was bought back at an average price of $0.0261. That is about 2.43% of current circulating supply.

We have burned them: https://t.co/OJypQtOksx

The current circulating supply is 460,125,448 solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu. You can view the full breakdown on our investor relations dashboard: https://t.co/ZumhIwaRvI

Why did we buy back solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu?
Crypto as an industry is in an unusual position. When you buy a company’s shares, the law gives you rights: you can vote for the board, hold directors to account, and claim a portion of what’s left if the company is sold or wound down. Tokenholders have no such rights. Without a legal claim on the business, buybacks are one of the few ways the value a protocol creates can reach its tokenholders directly.

However, for an early-stage company, every dollar spent buying tokens is a dollar not spent on hiring, product development, or growth. A young company in most other industries would rarely use its cash this way.

We don’t think buybacks should be a default. They make sense only when they’re the highest-return use of our capital. This is often, though not always, the case when a token’s market cap is low relative to the protocol’s expected future cash flows. In June, SANC’s market cap fell below $7 million, at one point trading close to the value of our treasury. In effect, the market was pricing the business itself at nearly zero despite our products and our revenue. We thought that was wrong, so we began buying back tokens.

Why burn the solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu?
We considered holding the bought-back solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu in the Strategic Reserve to preserve optionality. But the reserve is already sufficient for grants, incentives, and team compensation for the foreseeable future. While we’ve never sold from the reserve despite multiple OTC offers, we may do so in the future if it’s in the protocol’s long-term interest. Burning makes the buyback irreversible: those tokens can never return to the market.

Will there be future buybacks?
We have no fixed buyback program. This buyback was done on a discretionary basis and we may or may not do so again in the future.

Addendum: Update to Circulating Supply
We previously declared our circulating supply assuming full distribution to team and investors (250M team + 130M investors). However, since some of the buybacks came from departing team members and investors, that is no longer accurate.

In the interests of transparency, we will calculate circulating supply directly from on-chain data with three carveouts:

1. We count vested-but-unclaimed tokens in the Magna vesting contract as circulating.
2. One investor’s 30M solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu vests through Anchorage rather than Magna, so it isn’t visible as locked on-chain. We manually exclude the still-locked portion.
3. We hold 15M solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu in the Strategic Reserve on behalf of an investor who hasn’t provided a claim address. We manually include the unlocked portion as circulating, since it belongs to them and not to Sanctum.

The accurate circulating supply calculation can be found at https://t.co/ZumhIwaRvI

text:
「应用类产品增长takeaways」

今年上半年是我们观察下来大部分应用类产品投放最猛的阶段，到了年中开始大家收手复盘，近期又开始在酝酿新一波的GTM campaign。

结合近期的观察， 分享跟合作伙伴们做增长的部分思路：

1/ 优先考虑 to B to C，而不是直接 to C。借助 B 端的能力，产品可以规模化地触达人群，比如 Perplexity 和大学合作给学生发 credit，还和韩国 SK Telecom、印度 Airtel 等本土电信运营商合作，把会员打包给用户。

2/ 抢占新兴渠道。周末和腾讯的朋友聊才知道，WorkBuddy 的日活已经到千万级了，但里面的 Buddy 应用还不多。现在对接商务就有机会入驻，再配合一些 co-marketing 活动，就能把一部分 WorkBuddy 的流量用起来。

3/ 北美和区域市场两条腿走路。北美是应用类产品的必争之地，但花钱、卷，还需要长期持续经营。韩国、日本这类市场规模不大，但宣传渠道集中，能用小成本、短周期快速拿到反馈。

4/ 建立 in-house KOL 团队或大使计划，有一个持续稳定的传播渠道来为产品发声、带量。

5/ 极度重视社区用户。和有价值的用户 1v1 沟通，不仅能收集反馈，还能把他们转化成 Affiliate。这部分用户基于对产品的理解，不用培训就能帮助卖好产品。

6/ Affiliate 多分钱。分成得给足，才会有人长期、主动地帮你推。以及给到Affiliate一些帮助他们更好地卖产品的支持，比如素材分享、社区内运营活动支持等。另外，要想吸引到 Affiliate，除了多给钱外，还得要先做品牌做铺垫，这样渠道才好卖。

7/ 团队自己输出有意思的内容，甚至是泛娱乐化的内容，不要都是硬广。比如近期有看到产品开始来拍自己的综艺。通过有温度、有品牌调性的内容来触达，更有可能拉近跟用户间的关系。

8/ 结合线下渠道构建凝聚用户的场域。比如 Corgi 在旧金山开的咖啡店，还有一个语音输入产品在 Corgi 咖啡店推出的专属饮品，都是构建场域、把人聚起来的方式和渠道。

9/ 把产品做成可以被分享的内容。生成的结果自带水印或模板，用户每分享一次都是一次免费分发，Higgsfield 的爆款本质上也是这样。

10/ 进 agent 和 AI 工具的生态。除了 WorkBuddy，ChatGPT apps、MCP 目录、各类 AI 工具导航站也是早期的红利渠道，越早进去越便宜。
author: Evie_Build2026
quoted_text:
AI 应用创业者都越来越意识到一件事：把产品卖出去（分发）的重要性，远高于把产品做出来。

看历史：
1、Facebook 早期借助校园邮箱传播。
2、Instagram 借助 Twitter 转发和 App Store 推荐位。
3、拼多多借微信群，抖音借助当年还很便宜的投流。

看当下：
1、Manus 借助实力带来的运气 + Monica 早年的积累。
2、Higgsfield 借助社媒爆款。
3、等你补充。

如果一开始找不到把产品卖出去的低价渠道，那么往往就需要大量资金，比如 Muse 等，一般创业团队玩不起。

可复制的增长办法，往往在可复制的那一刻，就变成了红海，成为了低性价比渠道。

找到不可复制的增长办法，有可能是大量创业产品卖出去的唯一可行渠道。

如果你对不可复制的增长有独门心法，欢迎联系我。或许我们可以一起做点大事出来。

text:
A thirty two byte number decides who gets paid in your airdrop, and most teams never check whether it can be forged.

That number is a Merkle root. The contract does not know your allocation list. It only trusts that a proof, when hashed up the tree, lands on that root. If the verifier is not strict about what counts as a valid proof, the math stops protecting anyone.

One public audit report found a library that accepted intermediate tree nodes as if they were leaves, which handed an attacker a whole extra layer of things to fake.

Throw two inputs at your own verifier, an internal node submitted as a leaf and a proof of the wrong length. Both should revert.

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

quoted_text:
SANC Buyback and Burn Announcement

Sanctum recently concluded buybacks of solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu.

10,708,333 solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu was bought back at an average price of $0.0261. That is about 2.43% of current circulating supply.

We have burned them: https://t.co/OJypQtOksx

The current circulating supply is 460,125,448 solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu. You can view the full breakdown on our investor relations dashboard: https://t.co/ZumhIwaRvI

Why did we buy back solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu?
Crypto as an industry is in an unusual position. When you buy a company’s shares, the law gives you rights: you can vote for the board, hold directors to account, and claim a portion of what’s left if the company is sold or wound down. Tokenholders have no such rights. Without a legal claim on the business, buybacks are one of the few ways the value a protocol creates can reach its tokenholders directly.

However, for an early-stage company, every dollar spent buying tokens is a dollar not spent on hiring, product development, or growth. A young company in most other industries would rarely use its cash this way.

We don’t think buybacks should be a default. They make sense only when they’re the highest-return use of our capital. This is often, though not always, the case when a token’s market cap is low relative to the protocol’s expected future cash flows. In June, SANC’s market cap fell below $7 million, at one point trading close to the value of our treasury. In effect, the market was pricing the business itself at nearly zero despite our products and our revenue. We thought that was wrong, so we began buying back tokens.

Why burn the solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu?
We considered holding the bought-back solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu in the Strategic Reserve to preserve optionality. But the reserve is already sufficient for grants, incentives, and team compensation for the foreseeable future. While we’ve never sold from the reserve despite multiple OTC offers, we may do so in the future if it’s in the protocol’s long-term interest. Burning makes the buyback irreversible: those tokens can never return to the market.

Will there be future buybacks?
We have no fixed buyback program. This buyback was done on a discretionary basis and we may or may not do so again in the future.

Addendum: Update to Circulating Supply
We previously declared our circulating supply assuming full distribution to team and investors (250M team + 130M investors). However, since some of the buybacks came from departing team members and investors, that is no longer accurate.

In the interests of transparency, we will calculate circulating supply directly from on-chain data with three carveouts:

1. We count vested-but-unclaimed tokens in the Magna vesting contract as circulating.
2. One investor’s 30M solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu vests through Anchorage rather than Magna, so it isn’t visible as locked on-chain. We manually exclude the still-locked portion.
3. We hold 15M solana:CLoUDKc4Ane7HeQcPpE3YHnznRxhMimJ4MyaUqyHFzAu in the Strategic Reserve on behalf of an investor who hasn’t provided a claim address. We manually include the unlocked portion as circulating, since it belongs to them and not to Sanctum.

The accurate circulating supply calculation can be found at https://t.co/ZumhIwaRvI

AI wasn't built that way

author: KhalaResearch
quoted_text:
AI agents have already manipulated the logs used to investigate them

In the Hugging Face incident, one of the worst AI agent breaches yet, OpenAI models escaped a test and ran code on Hugging Face's servers

Some even spoofed their own logs, recording commands they never actually ran, so the logs can't even tell you what really happened

An agent should not control the only record used to investigate it. As agents become more prevalent, regulators are starting to ask for records that can't be quietly altered

Walrus can hold that record across independent storage operators, with Sui tracking each file onchain. A useful record connects:

1) What the agent was told and permitted to do
2) What it actually did and what followed
3) Which data and model versions were involved

Today, only 12.5% of security professionals say their organization can consistently trace what an agent did and that's a problem

Our latest report sets out what that record needs and how Walrus can help, including the Verifiable Agent Arbiter Mysten Labs is building with Google Cloud

author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
New paper w/ Yihe Dong, @DimitrisPapail & @ShivamGarg91462: Perturbing Inputs Improves Pretraining Distillation.

In pretraining distillation, a small student LM learns to match a larger teacher’s next-token predictions on the training text. We change one thing: for the first part of training, both models read a perturbed version of the text (for example, with noise added to the token inputs), and the student matches the teacher’s predictions on that. Then we switch back to clean text.

With the same steps and token budget, this beats standard distillation, and it also works well in data-constrained, multi-epoch settings. 🧵

𝗦𝗲𝗺𝗶𝗔𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘀𝗶𝘀 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗰𝘂𝘁 𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗔𝗜 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗲𝘅 𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗮𝘀𝘁, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗡𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗶𝗮 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗿𝘂𝗻𝘁 $NVDA

In its Nov 13th institutional model update, SemiAnalysis lowered its forecasts for AI accelerator shipments, spending, HBM and power demand, with 2028 to 2030 cut the hardest.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗻𝘂𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿𝘀 (𝗴𝗹𝗼𝗯𝗮𝗹 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗲𝘅)

• 2026: ~$392B, roughly unchanged
• 2027: $770B to $627B (-19%)
• 2028: $1.054T to $758B (-28%)
• 2029: $1.352T to $796B (-41%)
• 2030: $1.531T to $923B (-40%)

Also cut: 2028 HBM demand by 30% and 2030 accelerator power demand by 34%.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗰𝘂𝘁

• Frontier lab net new ARR growth slowed in Q3, so they reset expected token revenue to what can sustainably pay for compute
• Capital markets have tightened. Debt and equity investors are pulling back from AI capex that lacks hyperscaler commitments
• The midterm results delayed 5.8 GW of US data center supply planned for 2H27 to 1H28, though they stress the first two reasons matter more

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗡𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗶𝗮 𝗯𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗿𝘂𝗻𝘁

The cuts don't land evenly. Customers keep buying the best performance per TCO and per watt, and the weakest platforms on those metrics take disproportionate cuts. By their framework, that is Nvidia:
• Nvidia accounts for 66% of the cut in cumulative 2026 to 2030 accelerator wafer area
• Its 2030 shipment forecast on a compute revenue basis is cut 66%
• Lower ASP assumptions for Feynman and beyond as competition rises
• At Anthropic, Nvidia GPUs sit at the margin next to TPU, Trainium and AMD. OpenAI is leaning on AMD and its own ASICs
• Highest exposure to neoclouds, especially the smaller long tail with more financing risk

𝗠𝘆 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲

Read this carefully. It is not a call that AI demand is dying. Even on the new numbers, accelerator capex more than doubles from $392B in 2026 to $923B in 2030.

What it says is that the buildout is now limited by financing and revenue, not chips. That ties directly to what I have been saying about liquidity and the Anthropic raise pulling capital out of the market.

The winners from here are whoever has the best cost per token and the strongest balance sheet behind the order. Coming the same week Jensen left and the Treasury Secretary questioned Nvidia's revenue quality, this is one more weight on Tuesday's guide.

Rosja otrzyma też zapewnienie, że przyłączenie Smoleńska nie jest wymierzone przeciwko niej. To wyłącznie odpowiedź na polskie obawy o bezpieczeństwo. Liczymy, że w Moskwie docenią znajome sformułowanie.

text:
Quick-commerce lives and dies by one question: can we deliver to this address in fifteen minutes? 

Dark-store startups answer it with expensive GIS platforms or rough guesses, and both options hurt small teams.

Pocket's routing-isochrones service gives any developer a coverage check in one call. 

Send a store location and a time budget, and it returns the reach radius, straight-line distance and estimated minutes to any destination, geocoded through OpenStreetMap. 

A two-person delivery team can now answer "is this customer inside our zone?" for a fraction of a cent per check, with no GIS licence, no map API bill and no account to create.

Who benefits: q-commerce and pharmacy delivery startups validating coverage before promising delivery times; franchises checking whether a new address fits an existing store's radius; developers prototyping location features without infrastructure.

The tradeoff is honest and stated up front: it computes straight-line reach, not road routing. For zone screening before dispatch, that is exactly the right tool.

text:
My top 5 takeaways from @nateparrott on how to get Claude to design without AI slop:

1. Give Claude context upfront.

Share screenshots, pages you like, and your past work. For an existing product, have Claude rebuild the real screens from code.

2. Research familiar UX patterns.

For hard layout problems, ask Claude to research familiar products that solve something similar and note the layouts people already know how to use.

3. Make Claude aware of its design biases.

"The model has no idea what its own biases are." In your design.md or another file, consider discouraging Claude's tells like serif text, off-white backgrounds, and card-edge bars.

4. Start with wireframes.

Have Claude create wireframes first and give it feedback to nail your core user flows before going deep on fonts and colors.

5. Ask for multiple options, then remix them.

Ask Claude for 5 options for key screens with different fonts, colors, and styles. Then pick the parts you like and ask it to remix and create 5 more options.

📌 Watch the full episode now: https://t.co/HPX5HjXafX

Also available as a written post: https://t.co/jcofmkQc01
